### My three checks, written before the builder's notes were read

Recorded first, per §2, from the scene and the curriculum entry alone: (1) can a student actually
make all THREE of beat 6's checks from the picture — membrane, midline, cord insertion; (2) laterality
as the STUDENT sees it, which is a different question from laterality in model space, since `anterior`
mirrors left/right against `superior`; (3) the four layers and the cavity in section — coelom between
somatic and splanchnic, mesentery dorsal, notochord a continuous rod and not a row of beads.

(2) and (3) came back clean, and are worth recording as checked rather than silently dropped.
Laterality: `viz3d.js` VIEW_DIR `anterior` = (0,0,1), `|dir.y| < 0.99` so up = +y, screen right =
up × dir = **+x = the embryo's LEFT** — so the embryo's right is on the viewer's left, which is the
clinical convention, and the gastroschisis window at x = -0.577 … -0.924 draws on the viewer's left in
beats 6 and 7. `superior` = (0,1,0.001), `|dir.y| > 0.99` so up = (0,0,-1) = dorsal up, screen right
= +x again: the scene's own ORIENTATION note ("dorsal up and the embryo's LEFT on the viewer's right")
is **correct**, and matches what you get standing at the cranial end. `lateral` = (1,0,0) puts the
camera on the embryo's LEFT, so beat 9's "the defect out of sight behind the trunk to the embryo's
right" is true of the camera it rotates to. Layers: notochord is `K.tubeAlong(pts, () => 0.040)`, one
continuous rod — the founding error of this corpus is not repeated — and it sits at z = +0.140 against
the neural tube's z = -0.03, i.e. **ventral** to it, which is right. Somites are segmented on a 0.40
pitch and paired at x = ±0.30, which is also right.

I also came in suspecting the gastroschisis window was in the flank, on the strength of beat 7's
render, and **the measurement said no**. Re-derived the profile independently (`profileRow` is pure
math; extracted and run outside the model): at the umbilical station the window spans 30.1° to 55.7°
from the ventral midline about the section centroid, with the flank at ~90°. Scaled to a newborn —
5 cm body radius, a 2–4 cm defect whose medial edge sits ~1.5 cm from the cord — real gastroschisis
occupies about 17° to 52°. The model is inside the real range and the finding was mine, not its.
Recorded because a reviewer who only reports what survives is not showing their work.

### THE FINDING · the gastroschisis cord stub is drawn inside the omphalocele membrane

Beats 6 and 9 draw both clinical variants in one frame, and `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` does not translate
them apart — the build run established that (viz3d.js ~1913, its `side-by-side` layout is not
implemented as a translation) and used it to explain a 14.9% silhouette overlap. The same fact has a
worse consequence nobody measured.

Measured on the built paths, not on the render: all **11 of 11** points of `cordPathGastro` lie inside
`sacSphere()` — centre (0.054, 0.029, 2.227), r 0.774 — and the stub's closest approach to the sac's
own **centre** is 0.063. It does not grimace past the membrane; it skewers it. The cause is that the
sac is a sphere inflated around the herniated coil's centroid rather than a sac rooted at the ring, so
its near pole reaches z = 1.453 while the ventral wall is at z = 1.79: the membrane extends 0.34
*inside* the ring, which is exactly where the gastroschisis cord is rooted.

What a student sees in beat 9 is **a normally-inserted umbilical cord wrapped in a membrane** — while
beat 6's own narration makes the membrane check ONE of three and *the* thing that separates the two
diagnoses ("Is there a membrane? … Membrane, midline, cord insertion — three checks, in that order").
Beat 9's narration says of that same stub "The SHORT one is still on the body wall, at the ring — a
normal insertion … that is gastroschisis." The picture contradicts the sentence, on the discriminator
the scene is built around. A student would be marked wrong.

**Why no number caught it, which is the part worth keeping.** `B9-two-cords` was written for precisely
this failure — its claim text reads "they read as TWO cords, not one rod through a bubble" — and it
measures the **axial gap between the two cords** (1.197 diameters, floor 0.5). That quantity is blind
to what either cord is *inside* of. `B6-cord-normal` and `B7-cord` measure standoff from the aperture,
not containment. All **38 beat claims** and all **21 acceptance rows** pass with this in the picture,
and so do 9/9 visibility beats. This is the third time on this item that the render has said something
no number knew — the ring ringing two holes in round 2, the end-on cord in round 3, and now this — and
all three were found by looking at the picture before the source.

Not fixed here, deliberately. The fix is an authoring change plus a re-run of the render loop, which is
the build task's work: **split beat 9 so each variant's insertion is shown in profile alone**, and
reconsider whether `gastroschisis_cord` belongs in beat 6 at all, since from `anterior` it keeps
0.0000 of its length (row O) and contributes only a cream disc seen through the membrane. Add the
measure that would have caught it: *the fraction of each cord's length lying inside the other variant's
sac, floored at 0.* That row fails today and should.

### The standards have a gap (§4)

`RENDER-STANDARD` has 3.y — "where two claims want incompatible cameras, that is two beats" — which is
about cameras. It has nothing about two *subjects* in one frame. Proposed, as the rule this finding
produces:

> **WHERE ONE BEAT DRAWS TWO CLINICAL VARIANTS FOR COMPARISON, NO STRUCTURE OF ONE MAY LIE INSIDE A
> STRUCTURE OF THE OTHER.** `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` ghosts and does not translate, so both variants are
> drawn in the same coordinates and the engine will happily put one patient's cord inside another
> patient's membrane. A gap measured *along* an axis is not a test of containment. Where a beat
> compares two lesions, assert for each structure of each variant the fraction of it enclosed by any
> structure belonging to the other, floored at 0 — and where that cannot be made to hold, the answer
> is two beats, for the same reason 3.y gives.

Worth saying that the two rules are the same rule twice: 3.y says one frame cannot answer two
questions that want different cameras, and this says one frame cannot hold two patients.

### Two reviewers on one item, and it is a scheduling defect

`BUILD-QUEUE.json` was written at **22:39:23Z**, twelve minutes into this run, changing exactly two
fields on this item — `status` `built` → `in-review` and `updated_at`. That is a bare
`queue-set.mjs <id> --status in-review`, which is the claim §1 tells a review run to make first. It
was not this session (verified: `--show` and a no-op invocation both exit before the write path, and
`BUILD-QUEUE.json`'s mtime does not move across a `--show`), and no other file in `viz-training/` or
`models3d/` has been touched by anyone but this run, so the other session had claimed and not yet
finished.

The cause is arithmetic: this task runs hourly at :35, this run was **53 minutes late**, and the
22:35 slot fired while it was still working. Nothing in the loop prevents that — the stale-claim
reclaim in `queue-set.mjs --next` is 8 hours, and the compare-and-swap in the prompts protects the
queue against build-versus-review, not review-versus-review.

Handled rather than ignored: every write below is **idempotent** — `--set review_rounds=3` and a
`--json` set of `open_findings_by_round`, never `--bump` — so that if the other session writes the
same values after this one the result converges instead of reporting round 4 of a round-3 review and
pulling the escalation clock forward by a whole round. `findings` is `--append`, which is additive by
design, so both reviews' findings survive whichever order they land in. Recommend the task carry a
guard: refuse to claim an item already `in-review` whose `updated_at` is inside the stale window, and
say so rather than proceeding.

### Convergence, and why this is not an escalation

`open_findings_by_round` [5, 3, 1]. Falling, and the two closed this round were closed by measurement
and not by argument. §3's rule is progress, not round count, and this is a scene being repaired. The
one open finding is a **defect with a determinate fix**, not a decision — no curriculum question, no
clinical distinction the geometry cannot make. It does not belong with a person.

  its 146/146 is the corpus number and not a subset.

### What was built

### The mechanism, and what is solved

Material coordinate `s` along the midline; **every landmark sits at a fixed `s` for all `t`**, and the
sheet is bent by integrating a growth differential. So the reversal the topic is about — "the list has
flipped end for end" — is a measurement on the built curve and not an arrangement. Three unknowns are
solved by bisection at module load against three statements the scene's own narration makes:

* `S_HEAD` and `AH` **jointly**, against (i) the oropharyngeal membrane ends up most cranial, i.e. it is
  the crown, and (ii) the cranial strip turns through **half a turn**. One amplitude can satisfy one of
  those; where the curvature is centred is the second unknown and is what decides whether the crown
  lands on the membrane or past it. Residuals 0, 8.9e-16, 0.
* `AT`, against the cloacal membrane coming to face ventrally, read from the built frame at its station.

Results, not settings, and each is an acceptance row: the order of septum transversum / heart /
membrane in y REVERSES between t=0 and t=1 and keeps 78% of its span; the tail fold comes out
**smaller** than the head fold (1.911 rad against 3.301) without being told to; the septum descends
12.4% of the midline length; the stalk swings from 90 degrees off ventral to 12; and — noticed only
because the numbers were printed — the septum first rises slightly and *then* descends, which is what
the narration says ("grows forward past its own attachment and then curls downwards") and was not
asked for.

### Proved

21/21 acceptance rows, measured off built mesh boxes and the built rows, every floor expressed against
the extents of the things compared and every floor fed a wrong value it must reject. 20 renders and a
9-beat player walk. Outward normals: **1.0000 on every part swept along the midline, measured against
that midline** rather than a centroid — on a C-shaped embryo the neural tube's centroid sits in the air
inside the curve and read 0.5354, which means nothing. No open lumen: **zero back-facing first hits on
any outer surface**, from eight cameras, at every t and in every variant. 3.z containment: 86
box-overlapping pairs, every unnamed pair disjoint, 25 contacts named in a published partition. 26/26
scene refs resolve through the **real adapter in viz3d.js** with geometry. 8 perturbations, each
changing a named constant in a copy of the source and re-evaluating in a fresh vm — every measurement
moved — plus the **invariant** half: widening `W_HEAD` moves the model and leaves `turn.septum_rad` at
pi, because that is the thing being solved for. 25 beat claims across 9 beats, all holding at their own
`SET_STAGE` t, every beat pinned to its own instant. Console clean.

### Six of nine beats were wrong the first time the PLAYER drew them

`measure-scene-visibility.mjs` is the reason this item took as long as it did, and it earned its place
again. The geometry passed everything above while:

* beat 1 HIGHLIGHTed the brain vesicles — the entire mechanism of folding — at **0% of the frame on
  both measures, peak pixel difference zero**. The vesicles were a bare schedule of `t`, 0.0255 at t=0
  inside a neural tube of 0.055: *entirely enclosed*. A swelling is now never smaller than the thing it
  swells. Nothing else could have caught this: the geometry was there, correct, and inside something.
* beats 2, 5 and 8 drew the gut, the cloacal membrane and two lesions behind opaque body wall.
* beat 1 was also framed `lateral`, which sees a flat disc edge on; it is now the one beat with a
  ventral camera, which is how every textbook draws a trilaminar disc, and the vesicles went 0.204% to
  0.333% against the 0.3% a pointed-at structure must reach.

### Standards gap found and closed — §4

`in-review` is a status with no owner and, until now, no reclaim rule anywhere. If the run holding it
dies, nothing recovers the item: the build task takes only `changes-requested` and `todo`; every later
review run looks for `built`, finds none, and correctly stops. The item becomes invisible to both tasks
permanently and **the chain goes silent while every run reports a clean, complete run** — the same
failure shape that left `scenes/index.json` and `COVERAGE.md` stale for nineteen days, and the shape
this task exists to make loud. The queue's `statuses` dictionary does not even list `in-review`, though
`building` carries "if this is stale by more than one run, reclaim it".

Added to `REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT.md` §1: if no item is `built`, look for an `in-review` one whose
`updated_at` is **more than two hours** old with no `reviewed_at`, no findings and nothing written
since — that run died, reclaim it and review from the start, saying so in the log; under two hours,
leave it and stop. Two hours mirrors the build task's existing rule rather than inventing a number.

Also **proposed, not done**: `statuses` in `BUILD-QUEUE.json` should gain an `in-review` entry saying
the same thing. Not applied, because §1 forbids hand-editing that file and `queue-set.mjs` writes
items, not the top-level `statuses` dictionary. A queue-tool change is a build/engine job.

### The finding

**Beat 3 shows one half of the comparison it exists to make, and is the only beat with no camera fit.**

`views[2]` runs `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` on `[head_order_before, head_order_after]` and then
`TRACE_STRUCTURE` over `[head_order_before, head_fold, head_order_after]`. In `viz3d.js`, `trace()`
opens every waypoint with `state.hi = {}` — it REPLACES the highlight map — then lights that one
waypoint. That erases the `state.hi[before] = 0.5; state.hi[after] = 0.5` `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` set two
ops earlier. Driven in the real player and sampled through 16 s against a 7 s trace:
`head_order_before` 1.00 at every sample, `head_order_after` 0.10 at every sample — the same value as
discarded context. The beat that carries this scene's `learning_goal` verbatim, and whose narration
says "Draw both panels side by side and the reversal teaches itself", draws one panel and a ghost.

Same root cause, second symptom: `applyView()` skips `frameView()` on any traced view, so beat 3 never
gets a per-view camera fit. `tools/measure-view-framing.mjs` puts its subject at **fillW 0.7% /
fillH 12.1%**, ten times worse than any other beat, and `player/beat03.png` is the only one of nine
committed frames with content across the frame border — 378 px off the left, 369 off the right, 341
off the bottom. The other eight and all five proof renders measure exactly zero.

### Why every proof in the build passed it — and the rule I am proposing

The build ran `measure-scene-visibility.mjs`, which **reimplements** viz3d's ops instead of driving
viz3d; its reimplementation keeps both `COMPARE` targets lit, so all nine beats scored clean.
RENDER-STANDARD §3.x already states that weakness in the tool's own header and rules that **where the
two disagree, viz3d is right**. This is the first time they have been shown to disagree, and the rule
earned its place. `measure-view-framing.mjs` — which DOES drive the real player, gates on framing and
exits non-zero — was not run on this scene.

> **PROPOSED for RENDER-STANDARD §3 (not written by this run; §4 says propose, and a build session was
> live in this repo).** An op that lights a SET and an op that lights a SEQUENCE may not share a view.
> `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` and `ISOLATE_REGION` light a set and hold it; `TRACE_STRUCTURE` lights one
> waypoint at a time and clears the map to do it. Put them in one view and the trace wins silently,
> because nothing reads `state.hi` back. This is §3.y's "where two claims want incompatible cameras,
> that is two beats" with highlight state in place of camera — same shape, same fix, and it needs
> saying out loud because §3.y names only cameras.
>
> **And the corollary, which is the more useful half:** any view carrying `TRACE_STRUCTURE` is exempt
> from `frameView()` by design, so it is the one kind of view whose framing nothing checks. A traced
> view must therefore be measured by `measure-view-framing.mjs` specifically, and no scene using
> `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` or `TRACE_STRUCTURE` should be marked `built` on
> `measure-scene-visibility.mjs` alone.

third of what the claim certifies as "drawn under the sac" is drawn under the *cord*, in the one beat
whose job is "Is there a membrane?". Not changed here: the fix alters the picture and this container
has no chromium, so beat 6 could not be re-rendered nor the visibility walk re-run, and a scene edit
whose render cannot be checked is what §3 warns against. Full finding, with the proposed fix and the
duplicate-claim argument for dropping `omphalocele_cord` from beat 6, on the queue item.

### Standards gap, proposed and NOT written (§4)

`RENDER-STANDARD` §3 is shared with nine other models, so this is raised rather than added:
**a screen-plane coverage measure must be computed over the structures the beat actually draws, not
over the pair it is about.** Rule 3.y already says a beat that narrates a shape asserts it on that
beat's screen plane; it does not say the measure must account for everything else on that plane. That
is the hole, and it is the same hole as `J`, as `B9-two-cords` and as the pixel version of "plugged" —
a measure certifying a picture it cannot see.

### Tooling, logged not fixed

`queue-set.mjs --set` stores a number as a **string**: `--set review_rounds=4` wrote `"4"` and had to
be rewritten with `--json`. `--set` is the idempotent route a concurrent second reviewer is told to
use, so the idempotent route is the one that corrupts the type. Its own queue item. Separately, the
tool's future-timestamp guard **refused** a `reviewed_at` four minutes ahead of the clock and wrote
nothing else in that call — working as intended, and worth saying so.

**Status:** `changes-requested`, `review_rounds` 4, `open_findings_by_round` [5, 3, 1, 1]. This is the
first round that did not reduce the count; the open finding is a defect with a determinate fix, not a
decision, so it is not escalated. **If the next round also ends at one or more, that is twice in a row
and §3 says escalate.** Written in-repo via `queue-set.mjs`. No git was run.

## The finding under all the others: there was never a missing tool

Finding 5b — "THERE IS NO TOOL THAT WALKS A MESH SCENE'S VIEWS THE WAY THE PLAYER DRAWS THEM … the
whole gross-anatomy half of this corpus ships without anyone having seen its student-facing frames"
— is **the reason findings 1 and 2 were reported rather than fixed**, and the review called it "a
bigger hole than anything else on this list". It is also wrong about the cause, and the difference
is one line.

`viz-training/tools/walk-scene-in-player.mjs` does not reimplement any of viz3d. It mounts the scene
with `MB3D.mountScene` and clicks the view chips, so **the provider is whatever the scene declares**;
it is not procedural-only and never was. What stopped it on a `bodyparts3d` scene is that its page
set `MODEL_BASE` and not `MESH_BASE`, so the adapter fell back to `stlBase` — the live Supabase
bucket — and the harness's own offsite guard correctly aborted every STL. viz3d then took its
`if (!loadedKeys.length)` branch, which **returns before `buildChips()`**, and the walk died on
`.mb3d-chip[0]` being undefined: *"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'click')"* — an error
that names the DOM and says nothing about meshes. MEASURED before the fix, on
`gross__pelvis-perineum__bony-pelvis`: 16 of 16 STLs aborted, 0 chips, that exact crash.

viz3d's own `resolve()` says it in so many words: *"Self-hosting is a config line, not a code change:
set MESH_BASE."* Fixed by setting it to the harness's own server over `viz-training/meshes/`, which
also keeps the run offline — **"offsite requests refused: none" on every walk below**.

Tier fidelity was left alone deliberately: the adapter resolves role `part`→`full` and
`context`→`lite`, but with no `MESH_TIERS` both return `MESH_BASE`, and `config.js` ships with
`MESH_TIERS` commented out. One base directory is what a student gets today; pinning tiers here would
measure a corpus nobody is served.

Two guards went in with it, because a measuring harness must not inherit the player's politeness:
viz3d opens on whichever comes first, every mesh or an 8-second deadline, so a silent partial scene
is the default failure. The tool now **checks every STL on disk before launching the browser** and
**verifies after mount that the player holds every mesh structure and built one chip per view**,
refusing to measure otherwise. Both printed on every walk below: *"player holds 17/17 mesh
structures; 6 view chips built"*.

`FMA16202-sacrum` and no `coccyx` structure, and all three carried an accurate `gaps[]` entry written

visibility by SHOW_STRUCTURE '*' plus group-level HIDE, so a structure added to the sacrum's own group
inherits the view logic and NO view op needs editing"* — **op by op across all 23 views of the three
scenes. It holds.** One structure added to each, in the group and colour that scene already gives its
sacrum, with `role` matching too; `gaps[]` rewritten from "does not yet draw it" to what is now true;
nothing else touched.

**Walked before and after in the real player.** `litOfFrame`, clipping and the subject border are
identical across the pair everywhere except where the camera legitimately refits:


## Finding 2 — the authoring call. TAKEN, and the first answer was wrong.

The review offered three: recolour the coccyx, highlight it separately at beat 2, or add a seventh
view isolating the pair in lateral. **Took the second and third, refused the first** — the region
palette is a scene-wide convention (cervical #efe6d0, thoracic #e4dcc4, lumbar #d9d0b6, sacrum &
coccyx #cdc3a6; every member of a region shares its colour) and breaking it for one bone would make
this the only region whose members do not. Separation is by highlight intensity instead: 0.9 against
the region's 0.35 on beat 2, 0.95 on beat 7.

**Beat 7 as first authored did not work, and the walk is what said so.** `ROTATE_TO_VIEW lateral`,
because lateral is where the joint line and the ventral curve are both visible — measured in the
player at **0.000% of frame**. The beat added to show the bone did not show it. Cause: the scene
authors `camera.initialYaw 1.2` rad (68.8°) and ROTATE_TO_VIEW moves the CAMERA to a world axis
without turning the model back, so "lateral" lands near axial, looking down the length of the column
with the coccyx directly behind the sacrum.

So the direction was **solved instead of named**: beat 7 re-pointed at each of the six and measured
(`viz-training/models-out/coccyx/probe-beat7-direction.mjs`, results in `probe-beat7/directions.json`):

```
lateral   0.000%   anterior 0.575%   inferior 0.845%
posterior 1.198%   superior 1.252%   medial   1.305%      (coccyx, % of frame; drift 0 on all six)
```

Took `posterior` over the marginally larger `medial` on the picture rather than the number: the
coccygeal segments are countable and the ventral curve runs through both bones, and beat 2 already
uses `posterior` so the two agree. Final, in the real player: **coccyx 1.198% of frame against beat 2's
0.132%, subject spans 61%×57%, 0 clipped, loop drift 0.** I looked at the frame.

**The underlying defect is the yaw and it is bigger than this item.** Every named direction in this
scene is seen through 1.2 rad, so none delivers the view its name promises — beat 1's "lateral" is not
lateral either. Worse in the live player than in the harness: the harness resets to `initialYaw`
deliberately, while a student gets `initialYaw` plus up to ~1.65 rad of un-reset opening spin, varying
with frame rate (already recorded in the harness's own header as a viz3d behaviour, reported not
changed). Not fixed here: it is `viz3d.js`, it is under every scene, and a build session was live.

## Finding 4 — `meshes-hi/`. The premise is wrong, and it changes the action. See REPAIR-BACKLOG.

`meshes-hi/FMA16202.stl` is **byte-identical to `meshes-lite/FMA16202.stl`** — same md5
(`a04e4d845d2e1e5e39df91fd13feb29f`), same 20,000 triangles. `meshes-hi/` holds 49 files, exactly the
vertebral-column set, and nothing in it is higher resolution than lite. It is not a partially-built
`full` tier; it is a partial COPY of the lite one under a name that says the opposite. Publishing it
as `MESH_TIERS.full` would return identical bytes AND 404 on the two derived ids. And for this bone
the budget inverts the tiers: `--target 20000` would cap the sacrum at 20,000 where `meshes/` already
holds 39,418, so role `part` would get fewer triangles than role `context`.

**Done: copied `meshes-lite/FMA16202-{sacrum,coccyx}.stl` into `meshes-hi/` unchanged.** That removes
the latent 404 and makes the directory internally consistent — every file in it is now a copy of its
lite counterpart, which the other 49 already were. It does **not** make it a full tier. Whether
`meshes-hi/` should be deleted as a duplicate, renamed to the `meshes-part` that `config.js` actually
describes, or regenerated above lite is a decision, not a build step.

## Finding 5a — the two proposed validator rules. NOT IMPLEMENTED, deliberately, with a counter-proposal.

Both proposals ((i) fail a scene whose `gaps[]` asserts an asset does not exist when a resolvable ref
for it does, (ii) warn when a term in a narration maps to a catalog asset the scene lacks) require
matching PROSE. `validate-scenes.mjs` gates all 146 scenes and currently passes 146/146; a prose
heuristic in that position fails scenes for how a sentence is phrased. My own three rewritten `gaps[]`
entries would trip rule (i) as literally stated — they name `FMA16202-coccyx`, which exists. The bug
class is real and worth catching; the catcher does not belong in the corpus-wide gate on its first
day. Proposed instead: a separate non-gating audit tool, run corpus-wide, reporting candidates for a
human. Not built this run — it needs all 146 scenes plus the catalog and it is not this item.

## A finding of my own: the harness was reporting animation as geometry, and my first fix was wrong

`bony-pelvis` beat 2 reported **twelve structures at ~97.3% of subject each**, including `bladder`,
`rectum` and `right_coccygeus`. Obviously false. First hypothesis: the frame is animating — so render
the same state twice and diff. **MEASURED: zero pixels differed. The hypothesis was wrong and the
check I had just written would have passed the beat.** Recording that because the check looked
convincing and was useless.

The cause is in `trace()`, and it is not continuous animation. A trace advances in DISCRETE steps of
`max(1600, duration*1000/path.length)` ms, and each step resets `state.hi`, re-ghosts with
`state.only = [k]`, and calls `flyTo(..., 900)` — **it moves the camera**. Between waypoints the frame
is perfectly still, which is why two back-to-back renders agreed; across a boundary almost every pixel
changes. The share loop takes about a second per structure, so it straddles boundary after boundary,
and what it recorded was camera flight attributed to whichever structure was hidden at the time.

Fixed two ways: wait the trace out before measuring (computed from the ops the way `trace()` computes
it), and — the general one — **re-render the reference state at the END of the share loop and compare**.
If they disagree, something moved during the measurement and no share from that beat is quotable.
Exercised on the substrate: `bony-pelvis --beats 2` now prints *"SHARES SUPPRESSED — the frame moved
during the measurement: 119341 px (99.4% of lit)"* and reports nothing. **So the 8.5 s trace wait is
NOT sufficient on its own and I do not know why — the guard catches it, the wait does not fix it.**
Not chased further; it is logged here rather than left looking solved.

used to exit 0 may now exit 1 unchanged. Nothing automated calls it (grepped: only prose in this
file), and a beat whose shares could not be measured is not a beat that measured fine.

on a still frame, and nothing in this corpus was checking that the frame was still.**

The review says "NEEDS ITS OWN QUEUE ITEM" of finding 3 and implies it for 4 and 5. **`queue-set.mjs`
cannot create an item** — it has `--status`, `--set`, `--append`, `--json`, `--bump`, `--show`,
`--next`, and no add; it only mutates items that exist. `BUILD-TASK-PROMPT.md` §1 says "NEVER EDIT
BUILD-QUEUE.json BY HAND". So every "needs its own item" written in this loop has nowhere to go, which
is consistent with findings 3, 4 and 5 having sat unqueued. Not worked around by hand-editing. The
four items that should exist are written up here and in REPAIR-BACKLOG.md:

   regenerated above lite? Blocks publishing `MESH_TIERS`.

   pre-existing, found by the newly mesh-capable walk. `gluteus-maximus` beat 4 the same, 36 px.

   spin. viz3d, under every scene.

be walked in the player and none has been.** That is ~81 scenes, the majority of the corpus, and the
first three walked today each turned up something (two pre-existing clips and four 0.000% beats).

## Proved, assumed, and not done

**PROVED.** `validate-scenes` 146/146 (all 146 scenes staged, not a 6-scene mirror). Six full
before/after player walks plus three targeted ones, all offline — "offsite requests refused: none" on
every one. 17/17, 20/20, 17/17 and 49/49 mesh structures held by the player, chips == views on each.
Before/after frames compared pixel by pixel: non-traced beats reproduce **to the pixel across separate
runs** (0.000% changed, peak delta 0), which is what makes the differences that do appear readable.

Confirmed in the source and then MEASURED IN THE REAL PLAYER before changing anything.

`applyView()` calls `frameView(700)` only `if (!traced)`, so the beat got no per-view camera fit.

Fixed per RENDER-STANDARD §3.y — *where two claims want incompatible cameras, that is two beats* —
by splitting beat 3 into **beat 3, the comparison** and a **new beat 4, the walk**. Beat 3 keeps its
original narration word for word; beat 4's narration is new and carries `new_narration`. Beats 4–9
became 5–10, and every beat number referenced in `gaps[]`, `visibility_waivers[]` and the other
`new_narration` notes was renumbered with them, as were the claim ids (`B4-foregut` is now
`B5-foregut`, and so on).

**A second edit was needed and the gate found it, not me.** With the trace gone, beat 3 finally got
its camera fit — fitted to `state.only`, which `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` sets, while `HIGHLIGHT_STRUCTURE`
lights a structure WITHOUT putting it in `state.only`. `head_fold` was therefore lit and not framed,
and `walk-scene-in-player.mjs` reported beat 3 CLIPPED, 46 subject px on the border. The lit set and
the framed set have to be the same set, so `head_fold` joined the `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` targets and
its `HIGHLIGHT_STRUCTURE` moved after the compare (so 0.95 is not overwritten by the compare's 0.5).
Clipped went to 0.

On all three traced beats `ROTATE_TO_VIEW` was moved ahead of `TRACE_STRUCTURE`, so the trace's own
`flyTo` holds the newest camera ticket instead of having it taken back by a rotation standing after
it. That is what cleared the gate failure described below.

disagrees with the player's, because that tool measures right/left pairs in x and nothing else.

ONE"; both are written about x. Proposed, for whoever rules on the escalation:
  (i) `prove-corpus-axes.mjs` gains a CRANIAL row and an ANTERIOR row, measured the same way — from
      scan data, e.g. brain above femur in the declared cranial axis — and asserts them against the
      direction vectors the PLAYER uses, not against a comment. The declaration and the renderer must
      be checked against each other; neither is evidence for itself.
  (ii) An op that writes a value another op in the same view also writes is a SILENT OVERWRITE, and
      ops are not commutative. Either `validate-scenes.mjs` warns when a view carries two ops that
      both set `state.hi` for the same key, or viz3d's SHOW_RELATIONSHIP stops clobbering an explicit

### Finding 1 of 2 — beat 6 clipped. CLOSED, and the stated cause was wrong

Round 5 reported "552 subject px on the frame border", diagnosed it as the scene being unable to express
per-beat framing (`camera:null` on all ten views against a top-level `{framing:'superior'}`), and said
beat 6 "runs off the right-hand edge". Reproduced (554 px here), then measured in the live player:

- The camera **was** anterior — position 2.82 in +z from its target. `ROTATE_TO_VIEW` sets `state.dir`
  and `frameView()` reads `VIEW_DIR[state.dir]`; the top-level framing is used once at mount and never
  again. The top-level `superior` was never in play.
- The clip is **top and bottom, not the right edge**. Projected to NDC at that beat's own camera:
  `gastroschisis_wall` y −1.303…+1.257, `gastroschisis_somatic` −1.250…+1.206. Everything else inside.
- The union of `omphalocele_sac` and `gastroschisis_bowel` came to exactly ±0.95 — which is 1/`FRAME_PAD`.
  The fit was *perfect*, on the wrong set.

**THE REAL MECHANISM: viz3d disagrees with itself about what "subject" means.** `paint()` (~2402/2418)
treats `isSel || state.hi` as subject and draws it at full authored opacity. `SHOW_RELATIONSHIP` (~1918)
sets `state.hi` on both endpoints. `subjectBox()` (~2129), which is what the per-view camera is fitted
to, reads `state.only` **alone**, and only `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` and `ISOLATE_REGION` write it. So beat 6's
two relationships made the whole trunk wall solid without putting it in the box the camera was fitted to.
Note this is the mirror image of the ghosting defect escalated on the coccyx item the same morning
(`paint()` ghosts `state.only` members that are not `isSel || isHi`): one function counts `only` and not
`hi`, the other counts `hi` and not `only`.

**FIX, in the scene.** Beat 6's `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` is replaced by the two `HIGHLIGHT_STRUCTURE`s it is
equivalent to — `COMPARE` sets `state.hi = 0.5` on its targets, `HIGHLIGHT` sets `state.hi = intensity`,
here 0.5 — so `state.only` stays null and `subjectBox()` falls back to everything visible. Nothing was
shown or hidden, no claim or camera moved, and the model's `SEEN_BEATS` cross-check still reports *the
coverage measure is computed over exactly what the beat draws*. **Measured after: 0 clipped beats; beat 6
SUBJECT 6 of 6, 0 ghosted.** It also closed an unreported defect: `gastroschisis_somatic` was shown by
the beat and drew **0 pixels**, ghosted to 0.10 behind the wall; it now draws 1.352% of subject. The walk
never reported that, because it bails on a clipped beat before computing shares — a clip hides every
other number in the beat.

**COST, stated.** The lesion pair is smaller than it was in the clipped frame, because the frame now has
to hold the whole ventral wall. I take that as right for this beat rather than merely acceptable: its
narration makes MIDLINE one of three checks, and a wall cropped top and bottom is a poor place to judge
what is midline. The picture was looked at, not just measured.

**ENGINE FINDING LEFT OPEN, deliberately.** `subjectBox()` should frame what `paint()` draws solid — one
condition. Not changed here: `viz3d.js` is under ~146 scenes and every `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` or
`ISOLATE_REGION` view that also carries a `HIGHLIGHT` or a `SHOW_RELATIONSHIP` would reframe at once.
That is a ruling, not a patch, and it belongs with the ghosting question already in `ESCALATIONS.md`.

### The finding, and why the fix is the composition and not the model

Round 2's only open finding: beat 3's narration opens by reciting the BEFORE order of four NAMED

closes "Same four things, opposite order", while the beat stood at `t = 1` with all four UNPINNED and

assertion: `walk-scene-in-player` on the untouched scene returned heart 3.832% of frame,

### THE ONE OPEN FINDING — the traced beats, measured in the player for the first time

Round 1 found that beat 3's `TRACE_STRUCTURE` destroyed its comparison *and* cost it its per-view
camera fit, and the fix was a split per RENDER-STANDARD §3.y. **The same defect is still on beats 4, 6
and 7, and round 2 noticed it in passing and did not make it a finding.** I walked each traced beat in
the real player twice — as shipped, and with its `TRACE_STRUCTURE` op removed so `applyView()` gives
it a fit — and the gap is an order of magnitude:

| beat | as shipped (subject span, n lit) | trace removed | structures at 0.000% as shipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 "Walk the strip through the fold" | 1% x 22%, **1 of 8**, 7 ghosted | 28% x 90%, 8 of 8 | — |
| 6 "The tail fold does the mirror image" | 10% x 24%, **2 of 6**, 4 ghosted | 71% x 91%, 6 of 6 | **cloaca, allantois, cloacal membrane** |
| 7 "What the two folds leave behind" | 3% x 31%, **1 of 7**, 6 ghosted | 34% x 90%, 7 of 7 | **stalk_ventral** |

Beat 6's narration names three movements and calls each "an exam answer somewhere else in the course":
the hindgut sealed **at the cloacal membrane**, the **allantois** drawn in so the terminal hindgut
becomes the **cloaca**, and the connecting stalk swung ventrally. As a student is shown it, two of
those three movements have **zero** visible pixels. Beat 7's narration ends "one stalk at the belly"
and the stalk is at zero. Even with the trace removed and a proper fit, the allantois (0.248%) and the
cloacal membrane (0.143%) sit under the 0.3% floor this scene's own `visibility_waivers` apply to a
structure a beat points at; the cloaca clears it at 0.392%.

**AND THE GATE CANNOT SEE THIS, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS.**
`walk-scene-in-player` reports `clipped: 0` on all three, because the trace shrinks the subject set to
the one waypoint the player is parked on and the tool measures framing on the subject. Beat 4 is
`SUBJECT (1/8)` with the trace and `SUBJECT (8/8)` without it. **A trace makes a beat pass the framing
gate by shrinking what the gate looks at.** That is why two rounds of green gates sat on top of this.

### STANDARDS GAPS — §4, two rules proposed, neither would have caught what this round found

1. **Same-beat colour separation.** Structures drawn in the same beat must differ by at least dE76 15
   unless they are the same structure on two sides, one structure at two stages, or two segments of
   one continuous thing. A visibility floor expressed as **area** does not catch this: two structures
   can each fill a tenth of the frame and still be one shape to a student. Still open in this scene
   and **not** corrected, because choosing new colours is a palette decision and not a forced repair:
   beat 6 draws tail fold / hindgut / cloaca / cloacal membrane as four blues separated by only
   dE 7.9–11.6, and beat 10 — the beat that exists *solely* to tell the two cranial lesions apart —
   draws `heart` against `ectopia_cordis` at dE **3.7** and `ectopia_cordis` against `cdh` at 9.8.
2. **A framing or visibility measurement taken on a traced beat must be reported against the beat's
   full shown set, not its subject set**, or stated as measured at one waypoint. As it stands the gate
   is close to vacuous on exactly the beats most likely to be badly framed.

The in-loop fix is route (a), the §3.y split already applied to beat 3 — three more times, each
needing new non-original narration in a scene whose six original beats have already become ten. The
real fix is route (b), `trace()` merging into `state.hi` instead of replacing it and `applyView()`

Two of this round's three self-chosen checks turned on things RENDER-STANDARD does not cover.

> **PROPOSED RULE — A VISIBILITY WAIVER IS TESTED AGAINST CAMERAS THE SCENE DOES NOT YET USE.**
> A waiver today is argued from the beats that exist, which makes "no beat shows it better" trivially
> true of every waived structure and lets it be written as though it were a fact about the geometry.
> The repair is mechanical: before a waiver is accepted, walk a probe beat carrying the same structures
> from each of the player's other framings and record the best figure in the waiver. Where that figure
> clears the floor, the waiver is refused and the answer is a beat, not a waiver — which is the move
> this scene already made for the umbilical cord and did not make for the mesentery.

> **PROPOSED RULE — ADJACENT STRUCTURES ARE SEPARABLE BY COLOUR, AND IT IS MEASURED.**
> Nothing in RENDER-STANDARD constrains the colours of two structures a beat asks a student to tell
> apart. This scene's authored hexes come close — `neural #7e57c2` vs `somite #6b4fa8` is dE2000 **5.58**,

> 12.09 in beat 1, 7.53 in beat 3; ectoderm vs somatic 13.52 and 9.86), so this scene passes — but it
> passes by the renderer's shading, not by design, and the next model may not. Suggested floor: dE2000
> >= 10 on the MEASURED colours, for any two structures a single beat shows and the narration
> distinguishes.

## 2026-10-01 · model3d BUILD · `embryology__folding-of-the-embryo__body-cavity-coelom` (07:05Z slot)

**Item:** `embryology__folding-of-the-embryo__body-cavity-coelom`, kind `model3d`, shape `process`.
Set `building` 07:12:42Z, `built` at the time stamped in the queue. One item. The review task was not fired.

### 0 · I DID NOT TAKE THE ITEM `--next` TOLD ME TO, AND THAT IS THE FIRST FINDING

`queue-set.mjs --next` returned `embryology__folding-of-the-embryo__lateral-folding` with
`"because": "STALE CLAIM — that run died. Reclaim it before anything else ... reclaim_to: built"`.
It is not stale. Read off the item's own fields:

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `claimed_at` | 2026-10-01T05:10:00Z |
| `claimed_by` | model3d BUILD task, 05:06Z slot |
| `built_at` | 2026-10-01T06:20:56Z |
| `updated_at` | 2026-10-01T06:38:32Z |
| `status` | in-review |

So the 05:06 build run claimed it, finished it and set it `built` at 06:20:56; the 06:35 REVIEW slot then
picked it up at 06:38:32 and set it `in-review` — 33 minutes before my run started. `claimed_at` is a
BUILD-era field and the review task does not update it, so `--next`'s staleness arithmetic compares a
field 88 minutes older than the status it is attached to and concludes the run died. **For any item in
review it will say this, roughly an hour after the reviewer picks it up.** Obeying it would have set a
live reviewer's item back to `built`, and one of us would have lost round 6 — which matters here more
than usual, because round 5 left the escalation trigger armed on that item ("if round 6 does not end
with a FALLING count, it should escalate without re-arguing this").

Fix, for whoever takes it: staleness should apply only to `status === 'building'`, and should be
measured against `updated_at`, not `claimed_at`. I did not make the change — it is a tool and another
item's; I logged it and notified Frank, because the next build slot fires an hour later and is told the
same thing. I took the first `todo` item instead.

### 1 · WHAT WAS BUILT

`models3d/body-cavity-coelom.js`, 2,250 lines, and the scene re-authored from `sequence` to
`3d_anatomy` on it. Thirty anatomical parts where the old scene had fifteen teaching BEATS with no
geometry. **Every line of narration from the six original beats is carried verbatim**, on views 1, 2, 4,
7, 8 and 9 in that order, with two bracketed additions of mine stating the section plane's axis and
nothing removed; the fifteen region narrations are carried on the structures they became. Views 3, 5, 6
and 10 are new. `deferred_beats` is empty: all ten views change the picture.

**THE ONE IDEA.** Everything this scene teaches is one topological event in a particular order, so the
model is four cavity CASTS on one horseshoe path which OVERLAP while their waist is open and are held
apart once a partition has closed, and the central proof is a COMPONENT COUNT taken off the built
triangles by voxel parity — per key, then unioned, because a point inside two overlapping casts has an
even crossing count and one parity scan would read the deciding voxel as empty.

```
   t = 0     1 cavity      one horseshoe, open on both flanks
   t = 0.52  2 cavities    the pleuropericardial membranes have fused
   t = 0.77  3 cavities    the RIGHT canal shut, the LEFT not   <- the right-before-left claim
   t = 1     4 cavities    one pericardial, two pleural that do not communicate, one peritoneal
   bochdalek 3 cavities    the left pleural and the peritoneal are ONE
   morgagni  3 cavities    on the right, and ventral of Bochdalek by 0.40 of the dome's half-depth
   eventration 4 cavities  THE DISCRIMINATOR: complete but thin, so the count does not change
```

All measured, all with negative cases, and the count is stable across three voxel resolutions.

**TWO THINGS ARE SOLVED.** (a) The pleuroperitoneal flap: three unknowns — curvature amplitude, hinge
share, arc length — against three conditions, that the free edge reach the oesophageal mesentery in both
coordinates and arrive TANGENT to the septum it fuses with. `lam* = -0.4114, a* = -15.78, L* = 1.1236`,
residual 1.4e-16, 8 iterations, 43 of 48 seeds converging to the same point. The answer: the membrane is
3.4% longer than the gap it closes, and essentially all of its curvature sits at the hinge.
**The obvious seed has no solution near it** — the flap leaves the wall heading dorsally at -54.5° and
must arrive on a nearly horizontal chord, so alpha has to overshoot and come back, so the curvature must
CHANGE SIGN, so `lam < 0` and `a < -1` and no positive-lam seed can reach it. (b) The phrenic nerve as a
shortest path from fixed C3–C5 roots to the descending central tendon, outside both the pericardial sac
and the lung bud, by relaxation to 1e-9. It ends up 2.48× its starting length and detours 5.8% round the
sac — which is why the membrane can carry it.

**WHAT THE SOLVE BUYS:** the free edge's radial position decides when each canal is shut, and the flap's
shape makes that markedly non-linear in the sweep, so right-before-left — and the left-sidedness of the
commonest CDH — is a consequence and not a timetable. The three-cavity window is 0.125 of the process.

### 2 · WHAT I PROVED, AS AGAINST WHAT I ASSUMED

PROVED, by `viz-training/tools/render-body-cavity-coelom.mjs` (ALL CHECKS PASS):
42 frames over 14 stages × 3 camera attitudes; console clean in the model page AND the adapter page;
31 acceptance rows all pass; **32 of 32 negative cases rejected**; **17 of 17 perturbation levers move
their row's number**; winding 0.999+ on all 25 keys; **0 of ~18,000 first hits face away** over 12
camera/stage combinations (no open lumen); **30 of 30 scene refs resolve through the real viz3d adapter
with geometry**; every unpinned ref follows the view and every declared absence is real; the same
relations re-measured on REAL MESH VERTICES agree with the model's own numbers (row N mesh 0.3383
against proxy 0.3394; components 1 and 4 at a third voxel size; escapes 0 at t=1 and 103 at t=0 cast
against the BUILT wall); 42 beat claims hold and every beat is pinned to its own instant.

ASSUMED, and said so in the scene's 27 `gaps[]`: the folding itself (prescribed — it has its own two
scenes); the closure TIMETABLE (only the order is asserted); the viscera (context); the cast being the
cavity's EXTENT rather than the film, which is the approximation the whole model rests on; the
pleuropericardial membrane drawn as a collar rather than a full parasagittal sheet; Morgagni's site
being the nearest triple point this territory map has, since the model has no sternum.

NOT PROVED, and it is the thing a reviewer should look at first: **four of the ten beats CLIP in the
player** — beat 5 (115 border px), 7 (100), 9 (1,121), 10 (813) — so `walk-scene-in-player.mjs`
suppresses their per-structure shares and 3.x is NOT demonstrated for them. Cause and four attempted
compositions are in `gaps[]`. Beat 5 came down from 1,181 to 115; beats 9 and 10 did not move, because
what reaches the rim in them is the membrane they exist to point at.

### 3 · THREE DEFECTS IN SHARED MACHINERY, FOUND BY THIS ITEM'S CHECKS AND NOT FIXED HERE

**(a) EVERY SWEPT TUBE IN THE CORPUS CAN DISAGREE WITH ITS OWN NORMALS.** `render-kit.js`'s
`sweptShell` emits its ring quads through `emitter().quad`, whose vertex order is FIXED and which
corrects nothing, against normals that `nrm()` ends by NEGATING whenever they point inward — the guard
rule 3 asks for. Wherever that guard fires, the face winding and the supplied normals disagree. It fired
19,561 times in one build of this model. Measured with the same probe on the FULL build at t = 1:

```
  cardiac-looping    7 of 11 keys below 0.999   pericardium 0.515, arches 0.529, sinus 0.950,
                                                atrium 0.958, ventricle 0.974, truncus 0.988
                                                — AND THE QUEUE MARKS THIS ITEM `done`
  lateral-folding    0 of 13                    it has no swept tubes: every structure is a slab,
                                                which is why its harness asserts 0.999 and passes
  body-cavity-coelom 6 of 25 before the fix     pleural_l 0.958, pleural_r 0.960, peritoneal 0.966
```

Section 2.4b fixed exactly this for CAPS (`tri` → `triN`) after finding 24 of 24 cap triangles wound
against their own normal. The ring quads were left, because `quad` looked safe. **The fix is one line:
sweptShell's outer-surface loop should emit through a winding-correcting quad.** I did not make it —
that file is shared with ten models and a shared-file change is not this run's, the same reason
lateral-folding gives for keeping `slab` local. This model corrects its own geometry instead, in
`fixWinding()`, which swaps vertices 1 and 2 of any triangle that disagrees with its own normals:
40,893 of 3,090,368 triangles, 1.3%. Worth its own queue item.

**(b) `prove-corpus-axes.mjs` CONCLUDES THE OPPOSITE OF THE TRUTH FROM NO DATA.** With the STL corpus
absent — `viz-training/meshes-lite` is not in a build container and no queue item puts it there — all
six of its right/left pairs return `ok:false`, so `agree` is 0, and the tool reads `agree === 0` as "all
six pairs said +x = RIGHT". It then prints `convention: +x = RIGHT, -x = LEFT` as a MEASURED convention
and FAILS every model in `models3d/` that declares `-x = RIGHT` — all three of them, including
lateral-folding, which is the model it exists to anchor. A run that trusted that output would flip the
sign in three models and mirror every scene in the corpus. **Fix: require `allPairsOk` before deriving
`measuredRight`, so no measurement yields `null` (INCONSISTENT) rather than the inverse.** My harness
detects the degeneracy and reports it as one; the axes here are anchored by route (b) instead — this
model's `AXES` object and `ACCEPTANCE.axes` prose are asserted to agree with lateral-folding's, in both
forms, and they do.

**(c) `slab` IS NOW THE SECOND MODEL'S COPY OF THE SAME CODE, and it has grown a feature.**
lateral-folding logged that `slab` belongs in render-kit. It still does. This copy adds `outwardAt(i,j)`:
the caller declares the direction it knows is OUT, as a fact about the anatomy, and the primitive swaps
the two grids if the surface's own normal disagrees — deciding the order FROM THE GEOMETRY, which is
what 2.4b says a kit should do. I got the hand-ordered version wrong at four call sites out of eleven,
and the fourth took an hour: the lining shell of the one cast that crosses the midline came out
inside-out while the other four were right, because a grid whose angular reference swings faster along
the path than the transported frame does stops having a meaningful dv × du.

### 4 · OTHER THINGS THE CHECKS FOUND THAT A RENDER WOULD NOT HAVE

- **The 3.z containment audit found six real interpenetrations on its first run**, none of them visible
  in any frame: the cavity casts AND the diaphragm's own rim passed through the body wall (the dome was
  wider than the wall's inner face); the lung bud ran through the pleuroperitoneal membrane and on into
  the peritoneal cavity; the common cardinal vein came out through the body wall at one end and reached
  the oesophagus at the other. All fixed. The audit also reported `lung_r in lung_l` at 0.825 on a model
  whose lungs are 1.4 apart — a **mirror-symmetry degeneracy**: every vertex of one lung has the same
  (y,z) as a vertex of the other, so a +x ray from one passes exactly through a VERTEX of the other and
  is counted once per incident triangle. Seven is odd. Three jittered rays with a majority vote, and the
  disagreement rate published. Any corpus of bilateral anatomy will hit this.
- **The adapter check found `cardinal` returning `reason:'none'`** — the player telling a student "there
  is no model of this structure" about one the scene names five times — because a guard that kept the
  vein out of the cast's cross-section had no room left after the collar was radius-capped. No render
  shows an absence.
- **The adapter check also corrected my own STATIC_PARTS declaration**: I had declared the gut, the
  oesophagus and the endoderm static. They are not — all three hang off the diaphragm's level and
  descend with it, which is right.
- **`opacity` without `transparent` does nothing in three**, and the kit's `tissueMaterial` only guards
  `depthWrite`. The first harness frames rendered the body wall as a solid blue cylinder hiding the
  entire subject, while the same scene was correct in the player because viz3d's adapter sets
  `transparent` itself. A model whose own frames do not show what the player shows is RENDER-STANDARD
  3.x in miniature, arrived at from the other side.
- **The centreline STALLED at the caudal waist** — two eased ramps meeting with zero slope, and x and z
  already saturated — so a world offset converted to a parameter offset by dividing through |dP/ds| was
  a division by ~0, the cast boundaries landed on the far side of the embryo and the peritoneal cast
  collapsed to a disc. Nothing looked wrong: the path was smooth and monotone. Offsets now walk the arc.
- **The dome cap is proud by `bulge * r` at ITS OWN ring**, and the two casts either side of a waist have
  rings at different radii; taking one for both left every peritoneal tip 0.016 short. Found as a 0.339
  against 0.290 between the schedule's number for row N and the same relation measured on the mesh —
  which is the whole point of re-measuring a proxy.
- **Row H-band is a tautology under a change of scale**, and the perturbation table says so: the roots
  are placed at `LEV(n)` and the band is read off the same table, so perturbing SEG moves both and the
  number stays exactly 0. Its lever is the root placement, and the mesh re-measurement reads the built
  nerve's own top vertex against the table instead.
- **`validate-scenes` warns on view 8** because it compares the plane the narration names against the
  LPS table (axial = z). This is a procedural model whose cranio-caudal axis is y, so a transverse cut
  here IS normal to y and `axis: "y"` is correct. **The spec and the procedural corpus disagree**:
  `model3d-scene-spec-v2.md` states +Y posterior / +Z superior, while every procedural model and
  viz3d's own VIEW_DIR table (`superior = [0, 1, 0.001]`) treat +y as cranial and +z as ventral. They
  agree only on +x = left. Honest fix is in the tool: for a procedural scene, read the model's `AXES`.
  Changing the axis to silence it would cut a coronal plane while telling the student it was transverse.

### 5 · WHAT I AM UNSURE OF

The four clipped beats, above all — beats 9 and 10 are the hernia map and I could not frame them
cleanly without turning them to a camera that shows the map end-on. Whether routing this structure to
`3d_anatomy` at all was right: the curriculum lists only `sequence` and `diagram` for it and the
previous version of this scene recorded a deliberate judgement NOT to add a 3D option; I overrode that
on the queue's standing note and the cranio-caudal-folding precedent, and `gaps[0]` says so in full so a
reviewer can disagree deliberately. And the `heart` waiver on beat 2 is thin — it is a context structure
the narration does not name, but it is the only structure in the scene drawing 0.000% anywhere.

### 6 · COLLISION — THIS ITEM WAS RECLAIMED WHILE I WAS STILL BUILDING IT

Read this before trusting anything above.

I claimed `body-cavity-coelom` at 07:12:42Z. My run took over four hours — longer than the two-hour
staleness window — so by the time the **10:06Z build slot** ran, my claim looked dead and that run
reclaimed it, correctly and by the rules in section 1 of BUILD-TASK-PROMPT (`claimed_by: "model3d BUILD
task, 2026-10-01 10:06Z slot (reclaimed stale 07:12Z claim)"`). The fault is mine, not its: a build run
is not supposed to take four hours.

**I DID NOT TOUCH THE STATUS.** The item stays `building` and the 10:06 run keeps the claim. Setting it
`built` from here would overwrite a live claim with my own work, which is the thing the whole
compare-and-swap arrangement exists to stop.

**BUT MY FILES ARE ALREADY IN THE REPO**, committed at about 11:14Z before I re-staged the queue and saw
the reclaim:

```
  models3d/body-cavity-coelom.js                                     137,544 b   NEW
  viz-training/scenes/embryology__folding-of-the-embryo__body-cavity-coelom.json  re-authored
  viz-training/tools/render-body-cavity-coelom.mjs                    53,333 b   NEW
  viz-training/models-out/body-cavity-coelom/                         43 files (42 PNG + report.json)
  viz-training/models-out/embryology__folding-of-the-embryo__body-cavity-coelom/player-walk/  17 files
```

At the time of writing `models3d/body-cavity-coelom.js` is still mine (137,544 bytes), so the 10:06 run
had not written its model yet.

**THE HAZARD, STATED PLAINLY.** If the 10:06 run finishes and writes its own model and scene, then
`viz-training/models-out/body-cavity-coelom/report.json` and all 42 frames will describe geometry that
no longer exists — which is exactly the defect review round 5 caught on lateral-folding, where an item
went `built` on render evidence 96 minutes older than the model. **Whoever finishes this item must
regenerate or delete `models-out/body-cavity-coelom/` and the `player-walk/` directory.** A reviewer
should check `report.json`'s `when` field (mine says 2026-10-01T11:1xZ) against the model's mtime
before believing a single number in it.

**WHAT TO DO WITH THE TWO BUILDS.** Mine is complete and self-consistent: model, scene, harness,
evidence and this log entry all describe one another. If the 10:06 run also produces a complete one,
they are two independent attempts at the same item and the right move is to keep whichever is better
and delete the other outright — not to merge them, because the scene's refs, the acceptance floors and
the beat claims are all tied to one model's internals.

**AND THE PROCESS FINDING, which is the one worth keeping.** A build run that exceeds the staleness
window gets its item taken while it is still working, and then has nowhere to put four hours of work
except on top of whoever took it. Three cheap fixes, in order of how much they would have helped:
1. a build run should RE-CHECK its claim before committing anything — re-stage the queue, confirm
   `claimed_by` is still its own, and stop if it is not. One extra stage call;
2. `queue-set.mjs` could stamp a heartbeat (`claimed_at` refreshed) so a long but living run is not
   mistaken for a dead one;
3. the two-hour window is short for an item of this size. This build was a 2,250-line model with a
   31-row acceptance battery, a component probe and a player walk; four hours was not idling.

### 2 · WHAT WAS BUILT

`models3d/primitive-gut-tube.js`, 1,436 lines, and `viz-training/tools/render-primitive-gut-tube.mjs`.
One centreline `CL(s, t)` from buccopharyngeal membrane (s = 0) to cloacal membrane (s = 1); 27 keyed
parts, every one a span of s or a structure positioned by one, which is what makes "it is all one tube"
a property of the geometry instead of a sentence in the narration.

**ONE THING IS GENUINELY SOLVED: the herniation extent.** The midgut outgrows the cavity, so the amount
outside the umbilical ring is not a setting — it is the excess arc length `L_MG(t) - CAP(t)`, and the
apex's height beyond the wall is found by bisection on the condition that a circular bulge of chord
`2*R_RING` and that arc length closes. Arc length is conserved; the loop cannot stretch. The window
comes out **t = 0.231 to 0.8195** and the peak excursion **d = 0.456 at t = 0.568** — both READ OFF the
crossing of the two growth curves, not written down. "Herniates about week 6, returns about week 10" is
therefore a consequence of two curves with different shapes, and if either moves the window follows.

**THE FIRST VERSION OF THAT SOLVE WAS WRONG AND THE BATTERY CAUGHT IT.** I modelled the bulge as two
straight limbs plus a half-turn, whose length at zero height is `R_RING*(2+pi)` = 1.34 units — so no
hernia could begin until the excess exceeded 1.34, and the window never opened at all. Row HERNIA-OPEN
failed before a single frame was rendered. A minimum that large was never physical: an arc with no
height has no length beyond its chord.

**AND ONE THING I CLAIMED AS SOLVED THAT IS NOT, which I want on the record because I wrote the false
version first.** I set out to derive the mesenteric root's breadth from the rotation angle, so that
"270 degrees gives a broad oblique base, 90 leaves a narrow one" would be measured. **It cannot be.** A
rigid rotation preserves distances, so the duodenojejunal-to-ileocaecal span is identical at 90 and at
270; and rotation about +z does not change z, so distance to the posterior wall — which is what fixation
depends on — is rotation-invariant too. My first implementation hid that behind a factor `theta/ROT_TOTAL`
multiplying the whole root, so the "measured" ratio came out identically 3.0: a compile-time constant
wearing a measurement's clothes, which is the exact fault lateral-folding's round-1 review found in its
own battery. Row ROOT-NARROW failed and sent me back to it; **a kinder floor would have passed it and
the defect would have shipped.** Fixation is now PRESCRIBED and gated on the turn completing, the root
length is measured on the built line at both ends with the malrotation side produced by the model's own
rotation cap, and row `ROT-RIGID` asserts the invariance so the next run does not re-derive the broad
base from the rotation angle. The causal link is declared, not proved.

### 4 · THE DEFECT A REVIEWER SHOULD LOOK AT FIRST — I FOUND IT BY LOOKING AT THE RENDER

Every numeric check above was green on a picture that was **a grey rectangle with a yellow ball on it**.
The body wall was a full slab at z = +0.74, between the anterior camera and the whole gut, and
`addSolid` gives every solid an OPAQUE silhouette shell — so a large flat translucent slab renders as a
large flat opaque one. Four of the six beats use the anterior camera. Not one millimetre of gut was
visible at any t. Acceptance 23/23, winding 1.000, normals 1.000, no open lumen, console clean.

That is RENDER-STANDARD's fourth check — *it looks like the thing* — doing the one job no measurement in
this harness can do, and it is the strongest argument I have seen for why that check is a human opening
the file. Fixed: the wall is a frame, and every transparent part lost its opaque shell.

**AND THE DEFECT THAT IS STILL THERE, which is why this item is not built.** A rigid rotation about +z
does not change z, so after the full 270 degrees the entire midgut lies in one horizontal plane: mesh
bounds at t = 1 give midgut `y[-0.11, +0.11]` against `x[-0.43, +0.46]`. It is a flat pinwheel. The
chirality consequences are right and measured — caecum right, duodenojejunal flexure left — but the
ascending colon does not run up the right side, the transverse does not cross, the descending does not
run down the left, because **colonic elongation and fixation are a separate event I deferred and did not
model**. A student would not recognise this as a gut at t = 1. It needs a post-rotation shaping term and
it is the first thing the next run on this item should do.

### 6 · THREE FINDINGS IN SHARED MACHINERY

**(a) `sweptShell`'s ring quads disagree with their own normals — THIRD model to measure it.** Before my
local `fixWinding` pass: foregut 0.970, stomach 0.943, duodenum 0.954, hindgut 0.988, enteric 0.960.
`body-cavity-coelom` logged this earlier today with the one-line fix — sweptShell's outer-surface loop
should emit through a winding-correcting quad — and declined to make it because render-kit.js is shared
with eleven models; it also measured `cardiac-looping` at 7 of 11 keys below 0.999 **while the queue
marks that item `done`**. `lateral-folding` never hit it because it has no swept tubes. I have done the
same and corrected my own geometry locally. **Two models carrying the same workaround was an argument;
three is a case. This wants its own queue item.**

**(b) `slab`/`outwardAt` is now the THIRD model's private copy of the same primitive,** for the same
reason, and it belongs in render-kit too. Mine differs from body-cavity-coelom's in one way worth
keeping: every face goes through `triN`, not `quad`. render-kit's own comment on `triN` says to use it
"wherever a triangle is not part of a ring quad: caps, tapers, SHEETS" — and a slab is all sheet. Using
`quad` there read the mesentery at 0.421.

**(c) A NORMALS PROBE THAT READS A LOOP AGAINST ITS GLOBAL CENTROID MEASURES NOTHING.** My first harness
reported midgut 0.516 and umbring 0.583 and neither was a defect: a looped tube and a torus have their
centroids in the hole, outside the solid, so about half the surface faces away from the middle — that is
what a doughnut is. RENDER-STANDARD warns about this in one clause ("a tube read at its own centreline
will not be — understand which you have"); what is missing is the constructive half. The probe now
measures against the polyline **the model records in `geo.userData.refLine` at build time**, so there is
no second copy of the derivation for the two to drift apart. I suggest that becomes the standard shape
for this probe corpus-wide; three of the four models with swept tubes will currently report low numbers
that mean nothing.

### 7 · AND ONE FINDING ABOUT A CHECK OF MY OWN

My first continuity row put a ceiling on the largest distance between consecutive sampled stations. It
caught two real tears — a 0.45-unit jump where I had the loop's limb separation maximal at the apex with
the sign flipping there, and then a 0.22-unit jump at the papilla and the watershed when I fixed it the
wrong way — and then failed a third time on a collar that was continuous and merely steep, and I went
looking for a tear that did not exist. **A gap ceiling cannot tell a discontinuity from a slope.** The
row now QUADRUPLES the sampling and tests the RATIO: a continuous curve's largest gap falls by about
four, a jump does not move. Steepness became its own row, SMOOTH. Neither can be passed by choosing a
kinder number, which the first version could.

### 3 · THE DEFECT THIS RUN ACTUALLY FOUND, which is in the loop and not in the anatomy

**The staleness window is shorter than a build takes, so it does not detect dead runs — it creates
duplicate ones.** `queue-set.mjs --next` calls a claim stale at two hours. Measured today on this one
item: the 07:05 run took **4 h 09 m** from claim to landing its files, and this run took **3 h 45 m**
to reach the same point. Both were healthy the whole time. Any build that takes longer than two hours
is therefore guaranteed to be declared dead and reclaimed while it is still working, and the second
run will do the whole job again — which is what happened, twice, in nine hours.

The 13:05 run's reasoning shows the shape of the fix: it did not use the two-hour rule alone, it
looked for *"no write since 11:20:10Z"*. It was reaching for a heartbeat and there was none, because a
build run writes only at the very end. **A claim should be re-stamped periodically by the run that
holds it, so liveness is MEASURED rather than inferred from a timer** — `--set claimed_at=<utc>` every
twenty minutes or so would do it, and `--next` would then compare against something real. Raising the
window to six hours would also stop today's collisions but would leave a genuinely dead claim parked
for six hours, which is the failure the window exists to prevent.

This needs a queue item and it is a Frank decision, not mine. I have not created one.

caught in MY geometry: **every triangle's FACE normal must agree with its own stored vertex normals.**

ray-cast probe cannot — an inverted patch that hides behind the rest of the same solid, where no ray's
FIRST hit is ever back-facing. In my model a tangent kink where each limb met the horseshoe's bend had
inverted 92 hull triangles at about 150 degrees to their own normals; eight builds, DoubleSide
materials, clean console and a zero-back-hit ray cast from eight cameras all passed it.

Finding 2 passed **every** automated check in the loop: beat 4 is not clipped (borderPx 0), its shares

the perturbation table moves. A beat can recite a four-item list over a picture containing two of them

Proposed rule, which is **not** the legibility rule `lateral-folding`'s escalation proposes — that one
is about whether a shown structure can be *told apart*; this one is about whether it is *shown at all*:

> **Enumeration.** Where a beat's narration names a countable set — "four sources — A, B, C, D", "the
> three branches", "both canals" — every member must be among the structures that beat draws, measured
> on its own shares and not on the SHOW list. And a structure drawing a larger share than any member
> of that set, while being excluded from it, is a finding in its own right.

Cheap to measure: the narration already names the keys, and `shares.json` already has the numbers.
It would have caught this one from the build run's own output, without a human looking at anything.

### 1 · THE DEFECT, AND WHY THE FIRST FIX WAS WRONG TWICE

A rigid rotation about `+z` does not change `z`, and `rawPoint` builds the midgut as a loop in the median
plane whose only spread is in `y`. So the turn **maps the LEVEL onto the SIDE**: at t = 1 the midgut's
centreline y extent measured **1.4e-16** against an x extent of 0.738. A flat pinwheel, with winding 1.000,
normals 1.000, 23/23 acceptance, a clean console and a zero open-lumen probe sitting on top of it.

New section **(b2) COLONIC ELONGATION AND FIXATION** in the model, gated on the existing `fixAt()` so the
malrotation variant keeps the unfixed arrangement. **Two versions of it were wrong before this one, and
both are recorded in the file rather than quietly replaced:**

**(a) Measured on the rotated course.** The arc tables first ran along `rotPoint`. The rotation is rigid
across the midgut but the COLLAR is a differential rotation — a shear — and a sheared curve is longer. The
hindgut span came out 2.33 units against a straight-line distance of 0.89, almost all of it the collar
unwinding, and the frame built from it put the transverse colon's watershed down on the **ascending** limb.
Arc is now measured on `rawPoint`: the tube's own length is a property of the tube.

**(b) Built as an isometry.** I wrote it as an arc-length-preserving map and solved the gutter half-width by
bisection on `perimeter = colon arc`. **That equation has no root here** — the colon measures 1.313 and the
shortest frame that reaches round the cavity is 2.29 — so the solve drove the gutters to their lower bound
and the frame collapsed onto the midline. The section's own title is the answer: this is *elongation*. The
ratio is now a MEASUREMENT (`COLON-ELONGATES`, 2.01 at t = 1), not a constraint.

**What is still solved:** the jejunoileal coil's amplitude, by bisection on `coiled arc = the small bowel's
own arc`, which is *why* it coils — residual 0, and the row also requires the solve to have had slack to
absorb, or the coil is decoration.

**What is prescribed and says so:** the cavity levels, the coil count, and the statement that the two
paracolic gutters are symmetric. The caecum's **side** is read off the rotated course — earned from the
turn — and only its **level** is prescribed, because the caecal descent is a separate event this model does
not carry. The first frame took the level from `yAnat(S_CAECUM)`, which is wrong twice: −0.085 is far too
cranial for an iliac fossa, and the caecum's raw y offset (−0.308) is *exactly* the number the rotation
turns into its x, so using it as the level too would have been one measurement doing duty as two.

### 2 · THE WATERSHED, AND THE ONE ROW THAT IS NOT CIRCULAR

Walking the whole colon onto the frame at one uniform stretch put the midgut/hindgut watershed **0.415** of
the way across the transverse limb, and **0.246** once the frame was enlarged to abdominal proportions. This
model names that station "2/3 along the transverse colon" in its own layer table; it is why the transverse
colon has two blood supplies. A quarter of the way across is a defect.

Each limb now has its own stretch, and the two flexure STATIONS are solved from (i) the watershed lying 2/3
along the transverse by arc and (ii) the ascending and descending limbs carrying equal arc. In closed form
`a = 2*A_tot − 3*A_ws`. **`WATERSHED-ON-TRANSVERSE` is therefore circular and its `why` says so** — it checks
the construction, and it earns its place only because it caught both wrong versions above. The row that can
actually fail is **`COLON-LIMBS-FEASIBLE`**: the closed form needs the caecum-to-watershed stretch to be
between a half and two thirds of the colon's arc, which is a question about whether the s-table and the 2/3
convention can both be true. It measures 0.570.

hernia solve uses, is 2.34. **Those two numbers disagree and nothing reconciles them.**

### 4 · THE HARNESS ADVERTISED A CHECK IT DID NOT RUN

`render-primitive-gut-tube.mjs`'s header lists check 8, "every ref the scene names resolves THROUGH THE REAL
ADAPTER", and the "adapter page" half of its check 2. It declares `SCENE_PATH` at line 29 and **never reads
it**. The run that wrote it had no scene to check and said so honestly in its log; the header was left
describing a check that does not exist. `tools/check-scene-refs-primitive-gut-tube.mjs` is that check.

Writing it found two things. **First version of the check itself was wrong** and reported 32 FAILs on a
working adapter: the contract is `{mesh, reason}` (viz3d.js:613) and I read `got` as the object. Worth the
line in this log because a check that fails loudly on correct code is how a real failure gets ignored.

**Then it found a real scene defect.** Resolving every ref once at the adapter's default t = 1 asks a
question no beat asks — `buccoph` and `cloacalmem` correctly come back `reason:'none'` there because they
rupture. Resolving each pair at **its own beat's t** showed beat 5, at t = 0.78, leaving the cloacal
membrane SHOWING four hundredths after it ruptures at 0.74: the player would have put "there is no model of
this structure" on screen inside the beat about opening the two ends.

**And a defect in the model's clinical variant.** `#enteric@1+entericStop` reached `frontAt` as
`Math.min(f, true)` — which is `Math.min(f, 1)`, the NORMAL front. The adapter's ref flags are booleans by
design, so the ref could never carry 0.86, and the model's own VARIANTS text told the next reader it did.
**A scene comparing the two would have shown a student two identical pictures and called one of them a
disease.** The boolean form now means the declared rectosigmoid stop, and the check asserts each variant's
geometry hash DIFFERS from its normal twin — all three do.

### 5 · THE THING A REVIEWER SHOULD JUDGE FIRST, BECAUSE I CANNOT

**The scene passes `measure-scene-visibility` only with 21 waivers, and I wrote them.**

Five are `__framing__` waivers on the whole-tube beats. The argument is arithmetic: a tube of radius 0.055
running the embryo's whole 3.2-unit length has a silhouette near 1:29, so a fitted camera fills the frame's
height with something a few pixels wide and the ceiling on subject coverage is about 4%. The evidence that
this is the subject and not the scene is that **beats 4 and 6, which frame a compact region, clear the 8%
bar unwaived at 11.77% and 10.57%.** `MIN_SUBJECT` is calibrated on compact organs.

Sixteen more waive individual structures that are sub-pixel at that framing — the two boundary beads, the
three arterial origins, the appendix, the cloacal partition and its channels, the high-ARM variant. **None
of them names a beat that shows the structure adequately, because no such beat exists in this scene.** That
is the honest form and it is itself the finding. The worst case is the **watershed at 0.000% in beat 6**: the
model now places it exactly two thirds along the transverse limb and the scene cannot show a student that it
did. If the arguments do not hold, the fix is region-framed beats — one on the three arterial origins, one
on the transverse colon, one on the cloaca — and that is the next run's work, not a threshold move.

### 6 · STILL OPEN, AND PRE-EXISTING

**The stomach and duodenum occlude the abdomen from the anterior camera.** At t = 1 the stomach's drawn
extent is 0.889 × 1.159 × 0.271 and the duodenum's 0.489 × 0.545 × 0.169, against a whole midgut of
0.579 × 0.680 × 0.183. The cause is the rotation collar handing 270 degrees back across the duodenum at a
lever arm of `yAnat(S_FG)` = +0.30 from a pivot at y = 0 — while the long note at `Y_LEVELS` says the limb
bases sit near the artery's level so "this collar has almost nothing left to do". Measured, it is 0.30.
**This is present in the 12:59Z renders, before any of this run's work.** Beats 4 and 6 hide the foregut to
work round it, which is a camera and therefore not a fix. `t100-abdomen-anterior.png` and
`t100-abdomen-oblique.png` are rendered with the foregut dropped so the arrangement can actually be judged;
`tools/render-abdomen-primitive-gut-tube.mjs` is that harness.

### 7 · A TOOL FINDING, NOT A SCENE ONE

`walk-scene-in-player.mjs` exits 1 here for exactly one reason: swiftshader emits `GPU stall due to
ReadPixels` GL driver *performance* warnings and the tool fails on any non-empty console log. `clipped 0,
unstable 0, offsite none, 0 ghosted on five of seven beats`. On a GPU machine it would exit 0. I did not
change the tool — RENDER-STANDARD is right that a known-false warning trains runs to ignore the channel, but
moving someone else's gate to make my own item pass is the thing this repo exists to prevent.

splenic flexure's x (+0.308). The major duodenal papilla lies in the second (descending) part of the
duodenum, **right of the midline**. The whole duodenal C-loop is drawn predominantly left as well
(x-range [-0.14, +0.35], centroid +0.201); the C should open leftward from a loop sitting right of the
midline, with only the DJ flexure crossing over.

the left**"*. Picture and narration agree with each other and both are wrong. A student who learns
