Run fired 04:05:48Z. **No item claimed, no item built, no file changed except this log.**

### What I verified before deciding (not assumed)

1. **Repo reachable.** Staged `viz-training/BUILD-QUEUE.json` — 899,784 bytes, device mtime
   `2026-10-02T03:46:01Z`. Read it. §0's proof-of-access passes. `device_bash` not attempted (§0).

   back-pressure is NOT the reason I stopped. Full counts: todo 112, escalated 16, done 4, built 1,
   building 1.
3. **No rework waiting.** Zero `changes-requested` items, so rework-first had nothing to offer.
4. **Head of the queue is `embryology__week-3-gastrulation__primitive-streak`, status `building`,
   `claimed_at: 2026-10-02T03:16:31Z` — 49 minutes old at the moment I read it.**

### Why I stopped instead of taking the next todo

The scheduled prompt says: *"If the first todo item is already `building` and less than two hours old,
leave it alone and stop."* The head of the work queue is `building` and 49 minutes old, well inside
that window, so this run stops. I did **not** reclaim it (§1 reclaims only past two hours) and I did
**not** step past it.

**That 49-minute claim is almost certainly a live run, not a dead one.** `blastocyst`'s round-2 rework
claimed at 01:07:52Z and set `built_at` at 02:43:27Z — **1h36m of wall clock for one item.** A claim
49 minutes old is mid-build by that measure, and the two-hour staleness threshold is barely longer
than one normal build. Stepping past it would have put two builders on `render-kit.js` and the queue
at once, which is the hazard §0's compare-and-swap exists to contain, not an outcome to court.

### DISCREPANCY WORTH A HUMAN'S ATTENTION — the prompt and the tool disagree here

`node viz-training/tools/queue-set.mjs --queue <staged> --next` returned:

```
{ "take": "embryology__week-3-gastrulation__trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers", "because": "first todo" }
```

i.e. **the tool told me to step straight past the live claim and build the next todo.** Read its
source: `staleClaim()` surfaces a `building`/`in-review` item only once it is older than
`STALE_CLAIM_MS` (2h); a *fresh* claim falls through the filter and `--next` then hands over
`rework || first todo`, with no mention that an item above it is held. The 2026-09-29 header comment
explains that change was made to stop stale claims being orphaned — it solved that, and it left the
*fresh*-claim case silently taking the opposite line to the scheduled prompt.

So §1's "`--next` tells you what to take" and the prompt's "leave it alone and stop" give opposite
answers whenever a build is in flight, which — at 1h36m per item against an hourly `5 * * * *` slot —
is **most slots, not an edge case.** I followed the scheduled prompt, because it is the instruction
Frank approved and BUILD-TASK-PROMPT.md is merely *silent* on a fresh claim rather than contradicting
it; silence does not override an explicit instruction. This is the third sighting in this project of
the shape the queue-set header itself names: *a rule is only as good as whatever makes you look.*
Here the thing that chooses what a run sees actively points the other way.

**The decision is a human's, not a task's:** either `--next` should report a fresh claim as
"held, stop" so the tool and the prompt agree, or the prompt should say "skip a fresh claim and take
the next todo" and accept two concurrent builders. Whichever Frank picks, one of the two documents
needs changing. I changed neither — a method change is not this run's call.

### The parameter that is solved, and why that one

RENDER-STANDARD: "ask which number a student would be marked wrong for, and solve THAT one against a
stated constraint." The marks here go on *"the lower layer of the trilaminar disc is not the old
hypoblast renamed — it is epiblast that migrated down and evicted it."* So the constraint is a
**conservation**: every cubic micron of definitive endoderm, intraembryonic mesoderm and notochordal
process has to have come through the groove or the pit, and nothing may appear that was not delivered.

- `K`, the delivery per unit of groove length, is solved in closed form from the **measured** volumes
  of the three built layers at `t = 1` against the **measured** time-integral of the groove's own
  length.
- `dEndo(t)` and `dMeso(t)`, the two spreading fronts, are solved by bisection at every `t` against the
  built-grid volumes.

Worst conservation residual across thirteen stages: **3.5e-9**. Nothing about "one source, three
layers" is a caption; it is the constraint the geometry is built to satisfy. Row C reports the
residual, and the perturbation battery is what makes that a measurement: moving `hVent`, `hMeso` or
`wMax` moves all three solved values, and moving the dorsal convexity moves none — the declared
negative control for a quadrature that is stated to be planar.

### What LOOKING at the render caught that no measure did

This is the part worth keeping, because section 3's fourth check is the one with no exit code.

1. **The cells were 60 µm across** — wider than the whole three-layered disc is thick — so in the
   transverse section they hung below the ventral lamina like beads on a string. A 16 µm layer cannot
   contain a 60 µm cell. Now 22 µm. Every measure in the model was about *where* the cells are and not
   one about *how big*, so nothing could have caught it.
2. **Two holes in the disc**, wherever a beat showed the epiblast without the membranes — because the
   membranes OWN their footprint of both laminae, which is what makes them two-layered islands. The
   visibility walk passed both beats: it asks whether shown structures are visible, not whether unshown
   ones leave a hole where they were.

A third thing came out of the same looking: the harness was fitting its camera to everything a beat
shows, while `viz3d` fits an `ISOLATE_REGION` beat to `state.only`. On beat 2 that is the whole frame —
the player is tight on the streak and the harness was drawing the entire disc. Fixed in the harness,
and it is the same shape as the fault RENDER-STANDARD 3.x exists for.

### A render-kit defect, reported and NOT fixed

A kit tube whose radius function reaches **exactly zero** at one end, capped at the other, comes back
non-manifold at the capped rim: three triangles on every rim edge. The mechanism is specific.
`sweptShell` writes a solid tube's two flat end discs through `triN`, which **drops a degenerate
triangle** — so a zero-radius end gets no disc at all. `stripFlatCap` then fails its own
`pos.count === hull + 6 * ring` assertion and returns the geometry **unstripped**: the start's flat disc
stays in place and the start's dome is laid over it, coincident. That is exactly the defect
`tubeCapped` was written to remove — the kit's own comment calls it *"a one-pixel dark ellipse round
every capped end, which is the hard rim this whole change exists to remove"* — reappearing wherever a
tube comes to a point, which is **every arrowhead in this corpus**.

Section 10b of the harness reproduces it in five lines with no model code, and keeps a positive control
(a bare hemisphere, which must read as open) beside it. **Not fixed from a build run**: `render-kit.js`
is shared by every model and changing it changes all of them at once. This model stays off the shape
instead — its arrowheads are blunted to 6% of their own radius, which the probe measures as clean and
which is 1.3 µm on screen.

### Two readings of my own instrument that were nearly filed as geometry faults

Recorded because the standard's §6 is about exactly this, and because both looked convincing.

- The edge census called 105 parts leaky. The cause was **negative zero**: at a surface of revolution's
  pole the profile radius is `sin(π) = 1.22e-16`, so the pole's x and z come out at ±1e-16 and
  `(-1.2e-16).toFixed(4)` is `"-0.0000"` while `(1.2e-16).toFixed(4)` is `"0.0000"`. One point, two hash
  keys. Rounding before formatting fixed it. An earlier revision of the harness had already scoped
  check 10 away from the kit-tube parts on the strength of that misreading, with a long comment
  attributing it to render-kit. It was wrong, and the scoping is gone.
- The node's and pit's vertex **first moment** is asymmetric at 9e-4 of its own scale. That is a
  triangulation multiplicity artefact, not a surface one: row J3 measures every sheet's set of distinct
  vertex positions and finds **not one** lacking its mirror. Row J4 pins the residual so it cannot grow.

is worth not re-discovering.

`REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT.md` §0 was corrected on 2026-09-30 to say the outage is intermittent and to try

succeeded immediately, node v22.23.2 is in-repo, and the queue was therefore written through

measurements were still done in this container — chromium is not on that machine. The prompt also
still describes an eleven-item backlog; the queue holds one `built` item, as §0 says it would. Both
disagreements are reported rather than resolved: **the scheduled prompt needs editing, and only a
human can do that.**

**F1 — the mesoderm-free zone at the two membranes is a single POINT, not the membrane's footprint.**
`membraneMask()` is `cos(r·π/2)²`, so the exclusion factor `1 − mask` is zero only at the centre and
reaches FULL thickness at the rim — 0.854 of full at r = 0.75. Measured by raycast on the built
triangles at t = 1, silhouettes excluded: mesoderm present at 16/17 points inside the oropharyngeal
footprint and 17/17 inside the cloacal, max 0.2248 against a 0.2600 flank, and its z-span lies wholly
inside the membrane's at every one. Three quarters of each membrane's AREA carries at least half
thickness. The model holds two incompatible definitions of the same object: `membraneExtent()` is a
hard ellipse (it builds the membranes and is `mesoCoverFrac`'s denominator), `membraneMask()` is a
soft cone, and the cone is in the one place that decides the examinable fact. Acceptance K2/K3 and
beat 7's claims all evaluate `mesoThicknessAt()` at the exact centre — the one point where the cone
bottoms out — and `mesoThicknessAt()` recomputes the field analytically from the constants the
geometry was built from rather than reading a vertex, which RENDER-STANDARD's "AN ACCEPTANCE
MEASUREMENT MUST BE A FUNCTION OF THE BUILT GEOMETRY" already forbids in those words. **A standing
rule was violated; this is not a gap in the standard.** Invisible in every shipped frame, because
beats 3 and 5 section at x = 0 — through the one point where the model is right. Full measurements,
the fix and the knock-on re-solve are in the item's `findings`.

**§4 proposal — A CLAIM ABOUT A REGION IS SAMPLED OVER THE REGION.** Magnitude floors, negative cases
and the built-geometry rule are *all three* satisfied by a point sample of a field that is correct at
exactly that point. Where a row or beat claim asserts a property over an area or a volume, the measure
should sample a grid covering it, read off the built geometry, and report the WORST point. Proposed
for `RENDER-STANDARD.md`; not written there by this run, because §4 says propose and this reviewer did
not build the thing the rule would govern.

**Checked and sound, so round 2 need not re-spend it:** builds clean at all six required t; winding
re-derived independently, 0 disagreeing of 38,828 at t = 0.44; the notochordal process is ONE
connected component at every t — not the beaded notochord `ARTWORK-STANDARD` was written around, which

**What the run found on arriving, and did not cause.** The first non-terminal item in the queue
(`primitive-streak`) was `building` and 1 h 50 m old when this run fired — inside the two-hour window,
so it was left alone; by the time the claim was written it had gone to `built` on its own and the

### The two open findings

**R1 — a cut solid was drawn as an open bowl.** `cutSkip()` drops every quad facing the cut and emits
nothing on the plane it opens. That is right for the trophoblast (a WALL) and for the blastocoele (a
SPACE), and wrong for the inner cell mass, which is the only solid tissue here: the materials are
`DoubleSide`, so the opening showed the unlit inside of the far dome. Fixed by emitting the section as
geometry in each material part's own colour, through the kit's `triN`, outside `hullCount` so no
silhouette shell is inflated across the opening. The mass fans its section from the same pole it is
star-shaped about — which is the second dividend of round 2's partition, since a star-shaped solid has
a star-shaped section and needs no ear-clipping. The trophoblast's annulus is a strip merged between
two boundary polylines on *different* grids about *different* centres, walked on the embryo's own
polar angle; it is watertight because the cut plane falls on grid meridians (`NV`, `NV_M`, `NV_Z` are
all even), so the cap's rim is the surfaces' own vertices, bit for bit, rather than a second
approximation of the same curve. The alternative — rebuilding the inner arc from `rin()` on the outer
grid — was rejected by arithmetic: ~0.004 units of sagitta between two polylines through one curve,
about a fifth of a pixel of crack, the same order as the 0.2 µm clearance that once put a moiré right
round beat 3.

**R2 — beat 1 drew the polar/mural distinction on a solid morula, at the equator.** Took the review's
option (a). `phiSeam` no longer has a degenerate-window special case at all; before cavitation the
wall is one key, `trophectoderm`, and `polar_troph`/`mural_troph` are not built. The ref is PINNED at
`@0`, because a part that exists only for `t ≤ T_CAV0` would resolve to `reason:'none'` at the
adapter's default `t = 1` — the confident lie `FULL` exists to prevent. The 82.9° label jump is gone
rather than relocated, and row K now asserts it absent where it used to permit it at `T_CAV0`.

### What was PROVED, as against assumed

New acceptance row **CUT** states the review's proposed rule as a property of the EDGES: on the cut
build, every edge lying in the cut plane is shared by exactly two triangles. Phrasing it that way
makes it indifferent to the polar/mural seam — an open boundary at a *latitude*, no business of the
plane's — and makes an uncapped section and a doubled one fail in opposite directions. The one open
edge it allows is the seam chord, allowed by what it SPANS rather than by where it is: measured, seam
chords span 0.193–0.558 of the radius and edges along a surface span 0.000, threshold 0.02, and every
unshared edge's own ratio is published so the separation is in the proof rather than in a comment.

Then the same two findings measured on pixels, because both were findings about PICTURES and row CUT
alone would repeat round 2's mistake of proving the wrong thing well:

* `viz-training/tools/probe-cut-cap.mjs` (new) renders one key alone, cut, face-on, from *either*
  version of the model under identical lighting, camera and framing. Unlit interior inside the mass's
  own silhouette: **24.05% → 2.25%** at t = 0.42 and **21.81% → 2.29%** at t = 0.52, on an identical
  silhouette pixel count; the residue is the silhouette shell, which is meant to be dark. Luminance
  across the silhouette collapses from 50–155 to 120–124 — a flat, evenly lit section face.
* The review's own seam scan, re-run on both frames: round 2's `beat01.png` peaks at **y = 422**, 120
  of 260 sampled columns jumping >100 in RGB, (201,20,14) against (255,139,129) — reproducing the
  review's y = 422–424 exactly. Round 3 peaks at y = 204 with 23 columns, and that is the embryo's top
  edge against the background.

21/21 acceptance rows pass, 21/21 negatives reject; console clean; winding 1472/1472; 12,795 ray first

### Found by looking, pre-existing, and deliberately not fixed

**Half the triangles on every P-grid surface are collapsed to a point.** Measured against round 2's
own file first, to be sure it is not this round's: byte-for-byte identical in both. The `icm`'s uncut
buffer carries 7,168 triangles and **1,760 distinct vertices**, 3,588 of them duplicating the single
point (0, 5.695, 0) — which is `P`. The cause is geometric and benign for the picture: `P` lies on the
inner wall at the embryonic pole, so across the whole outward hemisphere of directions the void has
zero extent, `dWall` returns 0, and those vertices all land on `P`. Volumes are exact, row N holds,
the ray probe finds no holes. It is pure waste, on four surfaces, and it bears directly on this
model's own declared cost (60,700 triangles, 0.93 s per rebuild). Not fixed here because it changes
the grid every volume integral in this file is computed on — the arithmetic round 2 verified sound —
and it is neither of the findings this run was given. It is a queue item.

its reasoning holds here: at ~1h36m of wall clock per build against an hourly slot, a claim just under
two hours is as likely mid-build as dead. The next slot may reclaim it legitimately; this one may not.

**I am recording that this claim is a strong reclaim candidate at the next slot**: no log entry, no
`built_at`, and `updated_at` three seconds after `claimed_at` means it wrote its claim and then did
nothing for two hours. That is the shape of a run that died at the claim, not one that is building.

### THE FINDING OF THIS RUN — `--next` told me to hijack a running review

`node viz-training/tools/queue-set.mjs --queue <staged> --next` returned:

```
{ "take":  "embryology__week-3-gastrulation__primitive-streak",
  "because": "STALE CLAIM — that run died. Reclaim it before anything else",
  "status": "in-review", "claimed_at": "2026-10-02T06:17:35Z",
  "stale_for_hours": 2.8, "reclaim_to": "built" }
```

**That item is not stale and that run did not die.** Its `updated_at` is `2026-10-02T08:53:35Z` —
**thirteen minutes** before this run fired — the queue file's own device mtime is the same timestamp,
`BUILD-QUEUE.json.lock.released` is stamped `08:53:35Z`, and the item now carries a full round-1
findings block written by that review. A reviewer was working on it minutes ago.

**The bug, in one line:** `staleClaim()` ages an item by `Date.parse(i.claimed_at || i.updated_at)` —
it prefers `claimed_at` — but **the review task never sets `claimed_at`.** `REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT.md`
§1's claim command is `queue-set.mjs <item> --status in-review`, with no `--set claimed_at`. So for
every `in-review` item the staleness clock is reading **the builder's claim timestamp**, left in place
from before the review began. `primitive-streak` was claimed by its builder at 06:17:35Z and built at
06:49:11Z; from 08:17:35Z onward it reads as "stale" no matter how recently the reviewer touched it.

**This is systematic, not an edge case.** Builds here run ~1.5h, and the review starts after the build
finishes — so a review's `claimed_at` is *always* close to two hours old before the reviewer has read
anything. Essentially every `in-review` item will be offered to the next build run as a corpse.

**It is also self-masking, which is the part that compounds.** `staleClaim()` sorts oldest-first, so
`primitive-streak` (06:17:35Z, by the wrong clock) is handed over ahead of `trilaminar-disc`
(07:11:00Z) — the one claim that genuinely looks dead. Once trilaminar-disc crosses two hours at
09:11Z it becomes correctly reclaimable, and `--next` will *still* name primitive-streak first, every
slot, until the review flips that status by hand. The real stale claim is hidden behind a false one.

**What a run that trusted it would have done:** set a live review's item to `built`, erasing the
`in-review` hold while its reviewer was mid-write. The reviewer's own commit then lands on top of mine
or is refused by `expectedMtimeMs`, and either way one of the two is lost — the exact
two-sessions-on-one-file loss §0 and `REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT.md` §5 both exist to prevent. The
`queue-set.mjs` header already recounts this happening on 2026-09-29 to `cardiac-cycle-pumping`
("one step from rebuilding an item finished six and a half hours earlier"). **That fix corrected
`reclaimTo()` — where a reclaimed item lands — but not the clock that selects it.** Same failure,
one layer up, and `reclaim_to: "built"` is a *worse* landing than 09-29's, because it advances the
item out of review rather than back into it.

**PROPOSED FIX, for a human — I changed no code.** In `staleClaim()`, age an `in-review` item by its
`updated_at`, not `claimed_at`:

```js
const t = Date.parse(i.status === 'in-review'
  ? (i.updated_at || i.claimed_at || '')
  : (i.claimed_at || i.updated_at || ''));
```

and honour the rest of `REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT.md` §1's rule, which `--next` does not implement at all: an
`in-review` item is reclaimable only if it ALSO has no `reviewed_at` and **no findings from that
round**. `primitive-streak` has round-1 findings, so that clause alone would have excluded it.
Worth considering too: `--next` is the *build* run's selector, and an `in-review` item belongs to the
reviewer — the review prompt gives the reclaim rule to the review task, not to this one. Handing
`in-review` items to a builder at all may be the wider mistake.

### F3 — FOUND, NOT FIXED, BUILD-SIDE. A hole in the dorsal surface immediately cranial of the node.

Those 22 columns are not a second instance of F2. There is a region, on the midline just cranial of the
node, where **no dorsal part exists in the model at all** — not epiblast, not streak, groove, node or
pit. Fine scan at x=0, t=0.44: `pit` ends at y 0.96 at thickness 0.287, **nothing from y 0.99 to 1.14**,
`epiblast` resumes at y 1.17 at its full 0.280. Not a taper between two regions — both sides terminate
at full thickness with 0.18 units of nothing between them. Extent:

| t | gap, x | gap, y | size |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.33 | −0.48…0.48 | −0.95…0.25 | 108 × 125 µm |
| 0.44 / 0.52 / 0.58 | −0.48…0.48 | −0.25…1.15 | 108 × 145 µm |
| 0.70 | −0.48…0.48 | −0.60…0.75 | 108 × 140 µm |
| 0.80 | −0.24…0.24 | −0.95…−0.85 | 60 × 15 µm |

Absent at t 0.20 and closed by t 0.86. At its worst it is roughly **3% of the disc's area**, and it is a
0.27-unit-deep notch in the dorsal surface: at y 1.05 the topmost thing in the column is `mesoderm` at
z −0.246, where one row cranially `epiblast` tops out at z −0.519.

**It is visible in a shipped frame, as a see-through hole.** Beat 8 (t 0.46) draws `epiblast`, `streak`,
`groove`, `node`, `pit`, `laterality`, `membranes` and **no** endoderm or mesoderm, so there is nothing
behind the gap: **925 pixels of exact background colour (14,22,38) sit inside the disc outline just
cranial of the node** in `beat08_posterior.png`, a clean dark triangle cut into the epiblast. Beat 7
(t 0.58) shows the same gap filled by mesoderm and the notochordal rod sitting a quarter-unit below the
epiblast surface — a pit in the back of the embryo on the beat that teaches "a dorsal and a ventral
surface".

**Why a student is marked wrong.** The epiblast is a continuous epithelium over the whole disc; there is
no opening in it cranial to the node at any stage. The one real opening in this neighbourhood — the
neurenteric canal — runs through the **pit**, and this model explicitly and correctly refuses to draw it
(row I2, "the pit is a dimple, not a hole"; beat 2 narrates "a dimple in that mound"). So the geometry
denies the opening that exists and draws one that does not, 0.2 units away from it.

**Why nothing caught it, and this is the sharp part.** Acceptance row **P1** asserts "on every row the
named pieces cover the disc's full width with no gap left over" and passes. P1 is a statement about each
quadrature **row**, across x. This gap is a run of roughly eight consecutive rows that are *missing*
along y. **P1 proves every row is covered across its width; nothing in the battery proves consecutive
rows are contiguous along the length.** It is F1's shape rotated ninety degrees — the same
`regionsAt()` bookkeeping that `gaps[]` entry 26 already declares a one-row transition in, failing by
eight rows in the other axis, undeclared.

**Not fixed here because it is not a scene edit.** The medial lane boundaries in `regionsAt()` decide
it; moving them moves the epiblast's volume and therefore K, dEndo(t) and dMeso(t), and re-runs the
conservation. That is a build run's work, with the battery behind it.

### A DECLARED GAP I CAN CLOSE: THE HANDEDNESS IS PROVED, AND IT IS CORRECT.

The model carries `axesProved: false` and a header warning that "a symmetric model cannot prove its own
handedness — flipping the sign in this header would mirror the picture, teach a rightward nodal flow,
and leave every row below passing." **That is too strong, and the chain closes:**

1. `viz3d.js` `VIEW_DIR.posterior = [0,0,-1]`, used at line 2180 as `camera.position = target + dir*d`
   — so the camera sits at −z. `camera.up` is never assigned, so three.js's default (0,1,0) holds.
2. Camera at −z looking to +z with up +y gives screen-right = **−x** (three.js `lookAt`:
   x-axis = cross(up, z-axis) = cross((0,1,0),(0,0,−1)) = (−1,0,0)).
3. The anatomical frame is right-handed: in RAS, R × A = S. The model declares CRANIAL (S) = +y and
   VENTRAL/anterior (A) = +z, which forces **R = −x** and **LEFT = +x**. Those two declarations are not
   free choices: the oropharyngeal membrane is cranial by definition (V_ORO 0.915, y +4.15), and the
   epiblast faces the amniotic cavity, which is dorsal. Given them, the third axis is not available to
   be flipped — flipping it makes the frame left-handed, which is not a convention but an error.
4. The arrow is built at lines 1253–1263 as an arc x −1.95 → +1.95 with `head = arc.slice(13)` — the
   arrowhead at **+x**, and row X measures `flowTipX/flowSpanX = 0.491`. +x is screen-left, and in a
   dorsal view the observer and the embryo face the same way, so screen-left is the embryo's left.

**The picture teaches a leftward nodal flow, and that is correct.** The frame confirms it: the
arrowhead renders at screen-left. Not edited — flipping `axesProved` means adding a row that carries
this argument, which is build-side — but it should stop being listed as unproven.

### §4 — standards gaps, with the rules proposed

1. **A BEAT THAT DRAWS A LAYER MUST DRAW EVERYTHING THAT OWNS PART OF THAT LAYER'S FOOTPRINT.** Where a
   part is carved out of a layer's geometry rather than laid on top of it, hiding that part leaves a
   hole in the layer, and `measure-scene-visibility` cannot see it: it checks that shown structures are
   visible, not that unshown ones leave no hole. The check is cheap and mechanical — lattice over the
   subject at each beat's own t and flags, count columns where the model has geometry and the beat
   draws none — and it is what turned F2 from four guesses into 65 counted columns and then found F3.
   **This should be a tool.** Round 1 proposed "a claim about a region is sampled over the region";
   this is its companion: *a beat is checked over the region it draws, not over the parts it names.*
2. **CONTIGUITY ALONG THE SWEEP, NOT ONLY COVERAGE ACROSS IT.** P1's "every row is covered across its
   width" cannot see a missing row. Any model whose regions are decided row by row needs the
   orthogonal row too: consecutive rows must be contiguous, to a stated tolerance, or the gap is
   declared with its size.
3. **THE REVIEW TASK NEVER SETS `claimed_at`**, which is the root of the `--next` bug the 09:06Z build
   run diagnosed below — `staleClaim()` ages an `in-review` item by the *builder's* claim timestamp, so
   every item under review reads as a corpse about two hours in. That run's proposed fix is to
   `staleClaim()`; the cheaper half is in `REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT.md` §1, whose claim command should be
   `queue-set.mjs <item> --status in-review --set claimed_at=<utc>`. I did not edit either file. **This
   run was itself the item `--next` offered up for hijack, thirteen minutes after it claimed.**

* **Watertight.** Zero unpaired edges over every body in every build. The check runs **per body**, and

* **Conservation.** Both delivery rates are solved in closed form from measured full-cover volumes;
  both fronts are solved by bisection at every t. Residual is within one measured quadrature step at

* **The player walk passes with NO waivers**: every structure every beat draws or points at is

* **34 refs resolve with geometry through viz3d's own procedural adapter**, one per structure per beat,

* **Console clean**, in both the build page and the adapter page. Four software-WebGL substrate notices

* `validate-scenes.mjs`: valid, no warnings.

### WHAT I ASSUMED, AND WHAT A REVIEWER SHOULD GO AT FIRST

Full detail is in the scene's `gaps[]` (15 entries). The ones I am least sure of:

* **The handedness is DECLARED, NOT PROVED.** Every structure is mirror-symmetric in x — row T measures
  the worst residual at 0.000 — so nothing in this model can witness its own left/right. No narration in
  the scene names a side. The ingression routes are drawn on both sides specifically so that no single
  arrow could be mistaken for evidence of one.
* **The somite-clock margin is thin**: the clock outruns the disc at day 21.31 and the last beat stands
  at day 21.0. A reviewer who wants beat 6 moved earlier, or the disc given a length that grows, has a
  fair argument.
* **Beat 2 clears the subject-coverage floor by 0.12 of a point** (8.12% against 8.00%). Dropping the two
  route tubes from that beat — the three SHOW_RELATIONSHIP arrows already carry the same content — would
  roughly double the margin.
* **The section beats and the plan beats disagree about which way is up on screen.** viz3d holds the
  camera up-vector at world +y, which is CRANIAL here, so only a camera looking along ±y puts the
  dorsoventral axis up the screen. Beat 1 gets the textbook stack that way; beat 2 cannot (the hypoblast
  it is about measures 0.000% from there) and shows the same stack rotated 90°. Not fixable from a scene.
* **The midline strip cranial to the notochord's tip carries no middle layer.** Anatomically it is the
  prechordal plate, which this model does not build as a named part.
* **The day the hypoblast vanishes is an INPUT**, not an output. What the model earns is the spatial
  spreading.
* **Not reconciled with `primitive-streak.js`**, built the same morning, which models an overlapping
  subject seven days earlier. Same scale and axis convention (row S pins that); no shared vertices.
  Whether they should be one model is a real question this run did not answer.

### FINDINGS OUTSIDE THIS ITEM

* **The queue item's note is wrong about its own starting point.** It says "neurulation.js already builds
  this exact disc". There is no `neurulation.js` in `models3d/`. The only file of that name is
  `viz-training/spike/neurulation.js` — a frozen spike that nothing loads, registers nothing on
  `window.MB3D_MODELS`, and predates render-kit.js, so it hand-rolls its own winding reversal, index
  buffers and `computeVertexNormals`, which RENDER-STANDARD §6 now forbids. Its LENS IDEA is kept; none
  of its code is.
* **`validate-scenes.mjs`'s cut-plane advisory is wrong for every procedural scene.** Its `PLANE_AXIS`
  table is LPS (axial = z), which is right for BodyParts3D meshes and wrong for every procedural model
  in this corpus — cardiac-looping, primitive-streak and this one all declare CRANIAL = +y. viz3d clips
  on the world axis the op names, so in a procedural model's frame a transverse plane's normal is y. It
  fired on this scene's first composition and no longer fires (the beat became a plan view), so it is
  reported rather than worked around. The fix belongs in the checker and in
  `model3d-scene-spec-v2.md`; a build run should not quietly change a shared checker to make its own
  item green. viz3d's header records the SCALE mismatch between the two providers and says nothing about
  the AXIS mismatch, which is the same shape of problem.
* **`measure-scene-visibility.mjs` does not implement `CROSS_SECTION`.** It has no reference to clipping
  at all, so a beat with a cut is measured as if uncut. On this disc that made no practical difference —
  the frame is set by the bounding box either way, and clipping does not shrink a `Box3` — but a model
  where the cut removes the occluder would be measured wrongly. The tool's own header already says it
  reimplements viz3d's ops rather than driving viz3d and that viz3d is right where they differ; this is
  one of the places they differ.
* **A general sheet-sweeper is now duplicated across two models.** `primitive-streak.js` and this file
  each carry their own `sweepRegion`/`sweepRun`/surface-normal helpers built on the kit's emitter. By
  RENDER-STANDARD §6's own argument — four bugs fixed in one file so they stop being paid for again —
  that machinery belongs in `render-kit.js`. Not moved here: the kit is shared, and promoting it mid-item
  without a review is exactly the kind of change that should be proposed rather than made.
* **`index.json` and `COVERAGE.md` were NOT regenerated, deliberately.** This container holds only the
  scene files this run staged, so `build-scene-index.mjs` would have written a 2-scene index over the
  real 150-scene one — it was run, saw 2 scenes, and the result was discarded. A review run with the
  full corpus should rebuild both; the scene is `candidate`, so nothing is served from the stale entry
  in the meantime. Separately, `primitive-streak.json` and `blastocyst.json` both changed on disk while
  this run was working, so a snapshot-based index rebuild would have been stale on arrival anyway.

### WHAT I FOUND THAT THE REVIEW HAD NOT, AND IT CHANGES THE FIX

**The proposed scale group does not work.** F5 proposed a group sharing one camera distance "computed
once from the LARGEST subject box in the group". Measured: beat 1's subject is `{zona, trophectoderm}`
and its box is **15.685** units — that box is the ZONA's outer diameter, not the morula's. Beat 8's
subject is `{mural_troph, polar_troph}` and its box is **19.2117** units, with no zona at all. Those
stand in the ratio **1.2249**, against the narrated 1.5 and the model's own `embryoDRel` of 1.5758 at
t = 0.78. A group fitted to subject boxes would draw "half again" as 1.22× — better than 1.00× and
still wrong, and wrong in a way nobody would notice because the frames would finally be changing size.
Showing the ratio a student is examined on needs the group fitted to a **declared reference measure**
(the embryo's own diameter, which the model already exposes as `embryoD_um`), not to whatever each
beat happens to isolate. That is a schema design, not a field in a scene file.

**And it sits on an already-escalated function.** The distance comes from `subjectBox()`, which is the
subject of `engine__refit-camera-on-isolate` — whose reviewed round-2 fix is ABSENT from `viz3d.js`,
and which Frank ruled must be restored by merging hunks out of git, staying escalated until a safe
lock-handling procedure exists. Beats 2, 3, 4 and 6 of this scene isolate, so their boxes ARE the
`state.only` boxes that item calls the wrong subject; beats 1 and 8 do not. A scale group written
today would be fitted across two different definitions of "subject", one known-broken and under
repair, in a function that has already silently lost one session's edits.

So: `viz3d.js` **was not touched**, on round 4's own written instruction — "if it turns out that the
scale group belongs in viz3d rather than in this scene, that is the moment to escalate it as an ENGINE

Round 4 named `embryology__gametogenesis-fertilization__cleavage-morula` as carrying the same exposure

figures — because that scene's subject genuinely does not change size, which is the whole thing it

compare a size ACROSS beats"**, and the corpus sweep that follows is a search of narration and claims,
not a re-walk of everything. That is recorded in the tool and on the queue item.

The first version of the `scale:` line ended every beat with "flat box_fill with rising world-per-px =

### ADDENDUM — AN INFRASTRUCTURE DEFECT IN THE STAGE-IN/COMMIT-BACK SHAPE ITSELF, FOUND BY THIS RUN

**A `device_commit_files` call that was REFUSED still landed on disk, and it reverted another run's
change.** This is not a defect in any queue item and no review round can fix it, so it is written here
where the next run will read it.

What happened, in order:

1. 10:46:22Z — I set the queue locally, copied it to the session's output path and committed. The call
   was **REJECTED**: `written: []`, reason "device file changed since stage", `deviceMtimeMs`
   1790937408625. That refusal was correct — the review task had written the queue at 10:36:48Z to
   claim `trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers` as `in-review`.
2. I did what the prompt says: did NOT force, re-staged the fresh file, re-applied both of my changes
   on top of it (the review's `in-review` claim intact), copied the result **to the same output path**
   and committed again. That call was **ACCEPTED**.
3. Read-back showed the file on disk was **the content of the REFUSED first attempt**: `built_at`
   10:46:22Z, the engine item stamped 10:28:46Z, and `trilaminar` back at `built` — the review task's
   claim gone.

**The likely mechanism, and the rule that follows.** The commit sends a path in the session's output
store, and that store appears to bind the path to the bytes first written there — the second `cp` over
the same filename did not replace what the accepted commit actually uploaded. Re-committing from a
**fresh output path** (`outputs/fix1/BUILD-QUEUE.json`) landed byte-for-byte on the first try, sha256
of the file read back matching the file sent, which is what confirms it.

> **RULE, for every run using this shape: never reuse an output path within a run.** A retry, a merge
> after a refusal, or any second version of the same file goes to a NEW path. And read back by CONTENT,
> not by mtime — the mtime was new and correct on the clobbered write, and only comparing the bytes
> showed it was the wrong version.

**What I restored.** `trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers` is back to `in-review`, verified on disk. Its
`updated_at` is now this run's, not the review's 10:36:48Z — I could not restore that, and anything the
review task wrote to the queue **after** 10:36:48Z was lost by my clobbering write and is not
recoverable from here. The review task's own run and its findings are unaffected; only the queue entry
was touched. If that review committed findings between 10:36Z and 10:47Z, they are gone and it should
be re-run on that item.

`blastocyst` carries `built_at` 10:46:22Z rather than the 10:47:09Z of the merge, because the first
attempt's bytes are the ones that landed. Both are real clock times from inside this run and neither is
in the future, so the entry is honest; it is recorded here so nobody has to wonder why it is a minute
behind the queue's own `updated_at`.

## 2026-10-02T10:52Z · REVIEW round 1 · `embryology__week-3-gastrulation__trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers` → `changes-requested`

Reviewed by the model3d review task. I did not build this. The device shell was **available** this run
(`ls $HOME/mnt/...` succeeded on the first try), so `queue-set.mjs` ran in-repo under its real lock and
nothing went through the stage-in/commit-back path for the queue. Renders were done in my own container
because chromium is not on that machine.

**My own three checks, written before reading `built_notes`:** (1) is mesoderm genuinely interrupted at
the oropharyngeal and cloacal membranes, or only labelled so; (2) is the notochord one continuous rod
rather than beads; (3) is the layer identity/order right — ectoderm dorsal facing the amnion, endoderm
ventral facing the yolk sac. Two passed. The third failed, and it failed in the one beat a student sees
first.

### FINDING 1 — BLOCKING. Beat 1 renders the disc VENTRAL-SIDE-UP. Inverted germ-layer order.

Scene view 1 ends with `{"op":"ROTATE_TO_VIEW","view":"inferior"}`. What a student sees, top to bottom,
is **yolk sac, endoderm, mesoderm, ectoderm, amniotic cavity** — under a title reading "Cut it — three
sheets, **the right way up**" and narration reading "Ectoderm on top, facing the amniotic cavity.
Endoderm underneath, facing the yolk sac... dorsal still means the amniotic side."

Two independent measurements, because the first one alone would have been a reading of a thumbnail:

* **The shipped frame.** `models-out/trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers/beat01.png`, sampled down the block
  at x=550: top band (126,72,9) = endoderm `#f39c12` at 0.52/0.46/0.50 of full; middle (22,81,37) =
  mesoderm `#27ae60`; lower (22,58,75) = ectoderm `#2980b9`; the envelope below them (84,102,120) =
  amnion `#aed6f1` at 0.48. Consistent per-channel scaling, so these are those materials dimmed, not
  some other body.
* **The geometry, projected.** Building the model and dotting each body's centroid with the camera's
  screen-up axis, using viz3d's own `VIEW_DIR` and THREE's default `up`: `inferior` puts screen-up at
  world **+z**, and the model's header declares `VENTRAL=+z (DORSAL=-z)`. Order top→bottom:
  yolk_sac +0.912, endoderm +0.234, mesoderm +0.140, ectoderm −0.113, amnion −0.968.

**The model geometry is correct and is not the problem.** Measured z-extents at t=0.4: ectoderm
[−0.298, 0.122] dorsal-most, mesoderm [−0.018, 0.338], endoderm [0.004, 0.482], amnion [−1.04, −0.09]
dorsal to the disc, yolk sac [0.62, 1.77] ventral to it. Acceptance rows B and R pass honestly. The
defect is entirely the view's camera choice.

**Root cause.** `viz3d.js` never assigns `camera.up` anywhere in the file — it stays THREE's default
(0,1,0) — while `VIEW_DIR.inferior` is `[0,-1,0.001]`, very nearly antiparallel to it. The up-vector is
degenerate and screen-up falls out as the residual, world +z = ventral. The build harness reproduces it
because it uses the same convention, which is why the frames looked consistent with the proof.

**Why the one-word fix is NOT sufficient, measured.** `superior` does give dorsal-up (screen-up = world
−z; order amnion, ectoderm, mesoderm, endoderm, yolk sac). But at beat 1's own t=0.4 it hides the middle
sheet: rendered mesoderm pixels fall from **25,999** under `inferior` to **38** under `superior`,
because `BLK_Y1 = 3.20` is cranial to the mesoderm front at that stage (mesoderm reaches y=3.036 against
the block's 3.155) so ectoderm and endoderm meet and close over it. The beat would then show two sheets
while narrating three — a different wrong answer. At t=0.6 `superior` shows all three cleanly
(ecto 23,645 / meso 22,102 / endo 13,931 px).

**So the fix is `superior` PLUS a stage at which the mesoderm front has reached the block's cranial
limit — or pulling `BLK_Y1` caudal to meet the front.** I did not apply it. Either change has to be
re-run against the player visibility walk and the subject-coverage floors, which needs the full corpus
and the player, and this build's own notes record beat 2 clearing that floor by 0.12 of a point. I tried
`superior` alone, measured that it hides the mesoderm, and **reverted**: the scene on disk is
byte-identical to the build's (sha256 b01bce924ba60a68…, `view1 rotate: inferior`). Nothing in the scene
or the model was changed by this review.

No other view resolves it. At t=0.4: `anterior` shows endoderm only, `posterior` ectoderm only,
`lateral` and `medial` show all three but with screen-up = +y = cranial, so the sheets lie left-to-right
rather than stacked.

### FINDING 2 — A STANDARDS GAP (§4). The player and the repo's own renderer disagree about which way is up.

`viz-training/tools/render-scene-views.mjs:59` explicitly sets `camera.up` to (0,0,−1) for `superior`
and `inferior`. `viz3d.js` sets `camera.up` nowhere and relies on the `[0,±1,0.001]` nudge, whose own
comment says it "keeps a straight-down view off the pole, where the up-vector is undefined". **The same
scene therefore renders one way in the repo's tooling and the other way in the player, and no scene
author can control which.** 55 scenes use `superior`/`inferior`; **25 use `inferior` at least once**.
Every one whose subject has its dorsoventral axis on z inherits this silently.

Proposed addition to `RENDER-STANDARD.md` §4's ladder, near the top, above the depth-buffer rungs:

> **Before explaining a wrong-looking orientation by geometry, check the view's up-vector.** `superior`
> and `inferior` have no defined up in viz3d: screen-up resolves to world ±z by the 0.001 nudge alone,
> and `inferior` resolves to **+z**. A model that declares `DORSAL = -z` renders dorsal-DOWN in
> `inferior` while every acceptance row about layer order still passes, because the geometry is right
> and only the camera is wrong.

Whether viz3d should adopt `render-scene-views.mjs`'s explicit `camera.up` is an engine decision across
55 scenes and I have not made it. It is adjacent to `engine__refit-camera-on-isolate` (escalated).

### FINDING 3 — MINOR. Beats 6 and 8 are close to visually indistinguishable.

Same camera (`posterior`), same t=0.7, same three columns plus notochord. They differ only in that 6
adds `somatic` and 8 adds `coelom` + `splanchnic` — all pale (`#76d7c4`, `#d6eaf8`, `#a9dfbf`) and
occupying the same lateral band. The mechanical rule forbids *consecutive* identical frames and these
are not consecutive, so this is not a breach; but a student stepping 6→7→8 meets the same picture twice
under different narration. A highlight or a section op that makes the coelom read as a *space* would fix
it.

Scheduled 11:05Z slot, fired 11:12:24Z. Cloud container, stage-in / commit-back. Took round-3 finding
F3, the only one left open. One item.

**F3 WAS NOT WHERE ROUND 3 PUT IT, AND THAT IS THIS RUN'S MAIN RESULT.** Round 3 prescribed moving the
medial lane boundaries in `regionsAt()`. Measured here, that would have moved the hole rather than
closed it: the partition is exact at every row centre — row P1 passes on the unfixed file, and a
lane-by-lane sweep of all 56 rows at nine values of t reports not one uncovered micron — because
`regionsAt()` is only ever ASKED about a row centre. The hole lives BETWEEN row centres, in `sweepRun`.
Every region was swept from the first row centre of a contiguous run to the last, so wherever the part
owning a column changes from one row to the next (groove→pit, pit→epiblast, membrane→epiblast) both
runs ended at their own row centres and the row-wide strip between them belonged to nobody. The
y-boundaries of this model's parts are ellipse rims and named landmarks, and not one of them lands on a
row centre.

**THE FIX.** The dorsal lamina's four central parts and the epiblast are swept over a SHARED STATION
SET: every row centre, plus a station on every y where any of them appears or disappears, each found by
bisecting the lane itself rather than from a list of landmarks that could drift out of date with the
partition. A part that fades out does so at a station where its own width is ~0; a part that stops
ABRUPTLY (the groove at the node's caudal edge) does it as a RUN BOUNDARY with coincident end caps,
because a step in a swept surface is not a very short sweep. A run that begins at a step holds the next
station's lane across its first interval, so the opening rim never has to be swept.

**PROVED, not assumed** (`viz-training/tools/render-primitive-streak.mjs`, ALL ELEVEN CHECKS PASS):
49 acceptance rows pass and 49 negatives all reject; winding 1.0000 face-vs-vertex over every triangle
at every t and all three variants (re-derived on a unit sphere each run); every signed volume positive;
10,202 ray first hits from five cameras, 0 facing away; 0 unbalanced half-edges; 70 refs resolve with
geometry through viz3d's real procedural adapter at each beat's own t and flags; console clean with 4
swiftshader notices excluded by an exact counted pattern; worst unnamed pair sharing space 0.009;
`check-beat-claims` 61 claims, 0 failures, 0 beats unpinned; `measure-scene-visibility` 10/10;
`validate-scenes` valid.

whether the dorsal lamina is there at all — P1 and P2 both walk the partition row by row and neither
can see a defect that runs along the sweep. Value `[0, 68, 6007]`: zero uncovered columns away from the
declared regions, 68 within one row of a membrane's rim or the disc's own tip (declared, not waived —
the number is in the row so it cannot be mislaid), 6,007 columns tested so the row cannot pass by
testing nothing. The harness's new `rowsOnly` control regenerates the pre-fix construction FROM THE

plug set or draw a hole, and on beat 5 carrying the plug set and teaching the beat are mutually

footprint and drawing the sub-parts over it — the second moves the epiblast's volume, so K, dEndo(t) and
dMeso(t) re-solve and the battery and frames re-run, and it is the one that makes the whole class
unreachable instead of re-fixable. Neither is a reviewer's call. The question is in ESCALATIONS.md in
full. **The item now waits on a human and neither task will touch it.**

escalation. A run's log is written from intent, so **a log entry is never evidence that the queue moved.**

exit non-zero on a mismatch — rather than in another paragraph asking runs to be careful. Prose cannot fix
a rule conditioned on noticing; the thing that does the write has to check itself. (Third sighting of that
lesson, per `queue-set.mjs`'s own `--next` comment.)

## 2026-10-02T16:57:59Z · embryology__week-3-gastrulation__notochord · model3d BUILD run

**RE-AUTHORED, NOT WIRED.** The sequence version was built for the SVG panel engine: 15 structures
that were teaching PANELS with no geometry, 8 beats of prose, `status: planned`, provider `svg`,
and no artwork — so it rendered nothing at all. It is now a `3d_anatomy` scene of 42 structures and
11 views on a new procedural model, `models3d/notochord.js` (2,600 lines), with a new proof harness
at `viz-training/tools/render-notochord.mjs`. **Nothing was cut:** 13 of the 15 structure narrations
and all 8 beat narrations are carried VERBATIM; the 14th ("disc_context") rides verbatim on
`amnion`; the 15th ("axis") is in `deferred_beats[]` because it defines the whole notochord rather
than any part the model builds. 3 beats and 17 structure narrations are new and each says so in its
own `narration_from`.

### THE IDEA THE MODEL IS BUILT ON

All four stages exist AT ONCE, arranged along the axis. The notochordal process grows cranially from
the pit and reaches the prechordal plate about day 18; the canal→plate→rod transformation then sweeps
CAUDALLY from the cranial end, because the cranial material is the oldest. So at day 18.8 the midline
carries, head to tail: definitive rod, notochordal plate, hollow process, node and pit. That is one
frame in which the four stages of a sequence are four PLACES on one structure, and it is beat 4. The
whole axis is ONE swept superellipse from node to tip whose section SHAPE is a function of v and t;
`process`, `plate` and `definitive` are three consecutive v-ranges of it, so they cannot drift out
of agreement with one another because there is only one thing.

### WHAT IS SOLVED RATHER THAN TUNED

The relation a student is marked wrong for is that the rod is the SAME MATERIAL as the tube. So the
cross-sectional AREA of notochordal cells is the conserved quantity and it is carried across both
fronts and through both transitions. A0 = pi(R_PROC^2 - R_IN^2) is typed from two numbers; the
semi-width at every station is SOLVED from the area against whatever height and squareness the stage
calls for. Two teaching points then fall out rather than being typed: the plate is WIDER than the
tube (measured 2.02x) because it is flat, and the rod is NARROWER (measured 0.74x of R_PROC) because
it has lost its lumen. Measured section areas at the three stages at t=0.48: 0.15618 / 0.15623 /
0.15577 against A0 = 0.15708 — worst deviation 0.84%, which is one step of the ray-cast quadrature
that measures them.

Induction is the second solve: the neural plate is drawn where the signal from the axis crosses a
declared threshold, not where it would look right, and its extent is the axis's own extent one
induction lag ago. The `failed` variant sets the source to zero and the SAME builder returns a flat
strip of epiblast — so "no notochord, no neural plate" is a build, not a sentence. The adult fate is
the third: whatever regresses out of the vertebral bodies has to arrive in the discs, and the nucleus
pulposus's radius is solved by bisection against that budget.

    variant flags, per-structure opacity and camera, with viz3d's own up-vector rule copied) plus 4

    variants plus the adult build; **1,323 closed bodies, every signed volume positive**; **zero
    unpaired edges per body**, welded at 1e-6 rather than rounded to a grid; and a 6-camera ray cast
    over 25,944 triangles with **0 of 0 first hits facing away**. The radial-normal probe is reported
    as INVALID here rather than passed — five keys are sheets, where it sits near 0.5 on correct
    geometry.
 4. **Looks like the thing** — I looked at beats 3, 4, 7 and 8. See "what I am unsure of" below.

### THE PLAYER WALK FOUND TEN DEFECTS OUT OF ELEVEN BEATS, AND THEY WERE REAL

composition in which **ten of the eleven beats were wrong**, and the walk found them:

  the median section the scene's own first sentence asks for, with the sheets cut at the median plane

* **A cast inside the wall that encloses it.** `canal` is a solid lying inside the tube, so it drew
  0.000% in all three beats that show it. The process now carries a FENESTRA facing the camera —
  which is what the sequence version's own gaps[] asked for: "drawn as a HOLLOW tube with its canal
  open into the pit".

  and from `inferior` the near face is at v 0.655, where the tube is still hollow: `plate_sec`, the
  beat's own subject, measured 0.000%. It is `superior` now, where the near face cuts the plate.

  the embryo's 10), and the walk rendered it at 0% ink. It is now 1.5 units per segment — declared.

`sweptShell`'s ANNULAR end caps are emitted with `E.quad`/`E.quadFlip` in an order chosen by

So the §2.4b fix reached the solid cap and not the annular one. **Every hollow sweptShell in the
corpus has one cap inside out** — the neural tube, the gut tube, a bronchus, a great vessel — and the
cutaway-rim branch below it is written the same way. **This run did not change render-kit.js**: a
build run editing the shared machinery changes every model in the corpus at once, unreviewed, and
this item is the notochord. This model emits its collars and its annulus fibrosus through its own
`axialSweep`, whose annular caps go through `triN`. The reviewer should decide whether to fix the
kit or file it as its own queue item.

### §4 — three standards gaps, none of which this item can close

1. **`CROSS_SECTION` never cuts a taught structure.** `viz3d.paint()` sets `material.clippingPlanes` only
   when `!isTaught(s)`, and `isTaught` is `role !== 'context'`. So a cut only ever removes scaffolding.
   Beats 1 and 2 here both carry CROSS_SECTION ops whose written rationale is a paramedian face through
   the three germ layers — that is not what happens; what makes those beats legible is the model's
   `+block` variant. Any scene whose narration promises a cut of a taught structure is promising
   something the engine cannot do, and nothing warns. **Propose:** `validate-scenes` flags a view whose
   CROSS_SECTION targets nothing but `context` structures.
2. **Op order is load-bearing and silent.** `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` and `SHOW_RELATIONSHIP` both assign
   `state.hi[k] = 0.5` unconditionally, so an authored `HIGHLIGHT_STRUCTURE` placed before them is lost.
   Three of this scene's eight beats were affected, and beat 8's was introduced by round 2's own fix.
   **Propose:** `validate-scenes` flags a HIGHLIGHT_STRUCTURE whose intensity a later op overwrites.
3. **A reviewer's harness that keeps the model's own materials measures the wrong picture — I did this
   twice and it cost me two false findings.** `viz3d`'s procedural adapter (viz3d.js:609) takes only the
   merged GEOMETRY from the model and builds its own `MeshStandardMaterial` with `transparent: true` and
   `opacity` from the SCENE. The model's `matOver` (coelom 0.34, amnion/yolk_sac 0.16) therefore never
   reaches the player. A harness that reuses the model's meshes gets materials with `transparent`
   unset, where `opacity` is inert — so ghosting appears to do nothing and translucent structures appear
   opaque. I "measured" the splanchnic sheet as invisible behind the coelom, and beats 6/8 as
   near-identical, before checking the adapter; both were artifacts of my rig and both are fine.
   **Propose:** RENDER-STANDARD §4's diagnostic ladder gains a rung above the depth-buffer ones —
   *"before believing an opacity or ghosting result, confirm the harness built its materials the way
   the adapter does, not the way the model does."*

Also noted, not a defect: `COMPARE_STRUCTURES`'s `layout` field ("stacked", "side-by-side") is read by
nothing in viz3d — the op sets `only` + `ghosted` + `hi` and no more. Beat 1's stack and beat 5's columns

### 2026-10-02T17:05:06Z · ADDENDUM TO THE NOTOCHORD ENTRY · **BUILD-QUEUE.json IS BEING WRITTEN WITHOUT COMPARE-AND-SWAP**

This is the most important thing this run has to report and it is not about the notochord.

**What happened.** This run's `built` write landed at 17:01:05Z (device_commit_files returned it in
`written`, with `expectedMtimeMs` matching). Re-staging the queue immediately afterwards returned a
file with mtime **17:01:08Z** — three seconds later — carrying a copy staged **before 14:30Z**. That
copy did not only revert this item to `building`. It had also erased:

* the review task's entire **round-2 verdict on `trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers`** — status
  `changes-requested` back to `building`, `review_rounds` 2 back to 1, both findings, `built_at`
  15:46:53Z back to 09:57:20Z, `updated_at` 16:58:26Z back to 12:22:57Z;
* the **`primitive-streak` round-4 transcription** — `updated_at` 14:41:24Z back to 14:14:09Z,
  `escalated_at` and the round-4 `reviewed_by` note gone.

That is precisely the failure `queue-set.mjs`'s own header describes — *"whichever wrote second
silently erased the other's changes … a review's findings simply vanish"* — and precisely what the
`expectedMtimeMs` compare-and-swap in BUILD-TASK-PROMPT §0 exists to make impossible. **Something is
writing BUILD-QUEUE.json from a stale stage, either without `expectedMtimeMs` or with `force`.**

**What this run did about it, so it can be audited.** Re-staged the queue, diffed the two lineages
item by item — 135 items, **exactly 3 differed** — and took the record with the LATER `updated_at`
for each of those three, so the review task's work was restored rather than lost. Nothing else was
touched. The one field taken from the other lineage is this item's own `claimed_at`.

**And it happened again while this was being written.** The merged file was committed at 17:03Z and
returned in `written`; the read-back at 17:03:20Z shows the queue holding this run's *17:01* content
instead — `built` and the restored review data are all there, but the second `built_notes` entry
describing the merge is not, and `claimed_at` reads 14:14:39Z (this run's first, REFUSED claim)
rather than 14:15:16Z (the one that landed). So writes are being replayed or raced on a timescale of
seconds. **This run then stopped writing the queue**, on the principle that a contended file should
not be hammered, and recorded the finding here instead.

**The queue's substantive state as this run ends is correct**: `notochord` **built** with its notes,
`trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers` **changes-requested** with both findings and `review_rounds` 2, and
`primitive-streak` **escalated** at 14:41:24Z. The review task at :35 will find the built item.

**For whoever picks this up:** this is worth its own queue item, ahead of more scenes. Two things to
check first — whether any run commits BUILD-QUEUE.json without `expectedMtimeMs` or with
`force: true`, and whether a OneDrive-synced folder is replaying its own earlier versions over
freshly written files, which would produce exactly this signature and would mean the compare-and-swap
is being defeated outside the tasks altogether. If it is the second, every file this corpus writes is
exposed, not only the queue.

### WHAT WAS BUILT

`models3d/trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers.js` gains a third variant, **`slab`**: the same lens, the same
masks, the same height functions, built only inside a cranio-caudal window at FULL mediolateral extent.
The sweep's own end caps become the cut faces, which is what a transverse figure shows.

* **Thickness = `W_SOM` (one somite, 105 um)** — a typed dimension already in the file, not a new tuned
  constant. Framing is nearly insensitive to it: it enters only through the near-face term, half of 1.05
  against a standing distance of ~7.2.
* **Cranio-caudal LEVEL IS SOLVED, not typed.** `slabCenterY(t)` scores every candidate level by the
  completeness of the section it would cut — each of notochord / paraxial / intermediate / lateral plate
  summed over the window and normalised by that key's best window total, taken as a minimum over the
  four — and takes the best, breaking ties on the fullest section. This matters because three of the four
  come and go with t: the notochord is cranial to the streak's tip, the columns spread outwards from the
  streak, and the paraxial column is interrupted by its own fissures once it segments. At beat 5's
  t = 0.50 it chooses y = 0.8929, completeness 0.9565.
* **A SOLVE BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED INSIDE THIS RUN, and it is worth recording because it failed
  silently.** The first version scored a window by the per-row MINIMUM. From the moment the paraxial
  column segments, every candidate window contains an intersegmental fissure row where the paraxial area
  is exactly zero, so every candidate scored 0, the tie-break was also 0, and the solve quietly returned
  its first candidate — measured completeness 0 at t = 0.76 / 0.90 / 1 with the window parked at the
  caudal end of the disc. A section through a fissure is anatomically correct; what the figure needs is
  AREA, so the score became a window total. Completeness now reads 0.87-0.96 at every t where all four
  keys exist at all.
* **Routes are not built in the slab**, declared in `buildDisc` and in row SL's exclusion list. They are
  kit tubes, so the window's predicate never reaches them (row Y records the same for the block). In a
  paramedian block that is right — an arrow enters from the groove and must start outside. In a
  TRANSVERSE slab it is not: the arrow runs cranially out of the section and would hang in front of the
  cut face pointing at nothing.
* **Context envelopes become a roof and a floor** over the slab's own footprint, as the block's do, so a
  dome sized to the whole disc cannot put 2.5 units of z back into a box whose point is to be 0.7 deep.

2. **`viz3d`'s `frameView` IS DIRECTION-AWARE.** The model's own note at `inBlock`, this scene's
   `narration_from` on beat 5, and round 2's review all say frameView fits the bounding box "with no
   knowledge of where the camera is". It is not so: `distanceForBox(size, dir)` builds screen axes from
   `dir` and projects the box's half-extents onto them (viz3d.js:2155). The term that actually hurts is
   `ext(dir)`, the **near-face term**, which adds the box's half-extent ALONG the view axis: for a
   superior camera on the whole disc that is 5 units, so the camera retreats to 11.8 units to look at a
   stack 0.7 thick. The practical conclusion is the same — only building less geometry helps — but the
   stated mechanism was wrong, and a future run reasoning from it would look for the fix in the wrong
   place. Corrected in the model's new comment and in the scene's gaps.
3. **MULTI-FLAG PROCEDURAL REFS ARE COMMA-SEPARATED AFTER ONE `+`**, and nothing in the model, the scene
   spec or the task prompt says so — every existing ref in the corpus carries at most one flag. I wrote
   `#paraxial+split+slab`, which `parseProceduralRef` reads as a single flag named `split+slab`; the
   structure resolved to nothing. The correct spelling is `#paraxial+split,slab`. Worth a line in
   `model3d-scene-spec-v2.md`.
4. **THE RENDER HARNESS WAS NOT FLAG-GENERAL, AND ITS BEAT-5 PROOF FRAME WAS NOT THE PLAYER'S PICTURE.
   FIXED IN THIS RUN.** `render-trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers.mjs` derived two booleans, `needsSplit` and
   `needsBlock`, so the moment the model grew a third variant the harness went on rendering the build it
   knew about: a frame that looks fine and is the wrong build. It now reads the flag set off the scene's
   own refs. The union across a beat's structures is the harness's own approximation and is now declared
   in a comment — the player builds each structure with ITS own flags, and check 5 is the per-structure
   truth.
5. **`measure-scene-visibility.mjs` CRASHES INSTEAD OF FAILING when a beat's structures all resolve to
   nothing** — `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object` at line 628, because `r.pct` is
   null and `Object.entries` is called on it. That is how I found finding 3: a dead ref took the whole
   tool down mid-walk rather than reporting a beat with no subject. **NOT FIXED — it is shared tooling
   the review task also runs, and a build run should not quietly change a checker mid-round.** A guard
   that turns a null render into a reported FAIL is a few lines and belongs to whoever owns that tool.
6. **`viz-training/scenes/index.json` CARRIED A BADLY STALE ENTRY FOR THIS SCENE, AND ROUND 1 DECLARED
   THE INDEX CLEAN.** Round 1's review wrote: *"index.json needed NO rebuild (146 entries vs 146 scene
   files, 0 missing, 0 extra, this scene already in it)."* That is a COUNT check, and a count check
   cannot see a stale entry. The live entry read `mode: sequence, provider: svg, status: planned`, 13
   structures, and listed the pre-conversion SVG parts (`one_source`, `backwards`, `teratoma_layers`,
   `whats_next`) — the scene as it was before the queue converted it. **Regenerated with the full corpus
   present.** I dry-ran it first: 146 entries before and after, 0 added, 0 removed, and exactly **4
   entries changed** — this one and three neighbours left stale the same way by other runs
   (`blastocyst` 13→14 structures, `cleavage-morula` 8→9, `primitive-streak` 30→33). Ours is now
   `3d_anatomy / procedural / candidate`, 26 structures, 22 parts. `notochord_slab` is correctly absent

7. **`viz-training/COVERAGE.md` WAS STALE THE SAME WAY** — it listed this scene and three others as
   `planned` when they are `candidate` on disk, and undercounted authored views by 7. Dry-ran, then

8. **A WHOLE-FRAME PIXEL DIFF IS NOT A LIKENESS MEASURE FOR SPARSE FRAMES.** See the likeness numbers
   above: beats 2 and 5 score 12.50% changed, which on round 2's own scale would read as "more alike than
   the pair we called a defect", and they share nothing but background. Any future use of that metric
   should normalise over the union of the two subjects' pixels, which is a one-line change to how the

#### ADDENDUM, 17:44Z · A BAD QUEUE WRITE OF MINE, WHAT IT COST, AND THE SHAPE-LEVEL LESSON

Appended after the entry above because it happened during the hand-over, and it is the most portable
thing this run learned.

**What happened.** My first `built` write to `BUILD-QUEUE.json`, at 17:42:47Z, came back
`{"written":["…BUILD-QUEUE.json"],"rejected":[]}` — and did not land. The file on the machine took a
fresh mtime and the bytes of an EARLIER version of the same staged path: 1049378 bytes, the queue as it
stood right after my 17:08 claim, with `built_notes` still 2 entries long.

**Why `expectedMtimeMs` could not catch it.** The compare-and-swap in BUILD-TASK-PROMPT section 0 guards
against a CONCURRENT WRITER changing the device file under me. This was not that. `queue-set.mjs` writes
by temp-file-plus-rename, so the path I had already committed from once pointed at a new inode the second
time, and the commit tool sent a stale snapshot of MY OWN file. The mtime it checked was the device's,
which was exactly what I had staged, so the guard passed and was never relevant.

**What it cost.** It reverted `embryology__week-3-gastrulation__notochord` from `in-review` — set by the
review task's 17:35 slot, which is live as I write — back to `built`, rolling its `updated_at` from
whatever the review had written back to 17:01:03Z. That is precisely the silent erasure the
compare-and-swap rule exists to prevent, arriving through a door the rule does not cover. I restored the
item to `in-review` and recorded the reason in a `restored_by_build_run` field on it; **the live review
run's own verdict write should be trusted over my restoration**, since it knows what it claimed and I am
reconstructing.

**What caught it.** Only the read-back. BUILD-TASK-PROMPT section 3 — *"A COMMIT THAT WAS ISSUED IS NOT A
COMMIT THAT LANDED"* — says to re-read every file off the machine and says, explicitly, that this is
STRICTLY STRONGER than checking the `written` and `rejected` arrays. It is, and this is the case that
shows why: the arrays said success, the mtime said success, and the content was two notes short. The
09-11 incident that put that rule in the file was a run whose commits never landed at all; this is the
same rule catching a subtler version, where the commit landed and carried the wrong bytes.

**The lesson, which belongs in section 0 rather than in this entry.** Two lines:

1. **Commit the queue from a path nothing has committed from before.** I re-did the write from
   `/mnt/user-data/outputs/qfix/BUILD-QUEUE.json` and it landed correctly first time — 1058259 bytes on
   the machine, matching the local file exactly.
2. **Verify the committed CONTENT off the machine, not the `written[]` array** — for the queue as much as
   for the model and the scene. Size and a parsed field or two is enough; I compared size, status,
   `built_at`, `built_notes.length` and the length of the new note.

For completeness, the other seven files of this run were content-verified and were all correct on the
first commit: the four text files by sha256 against the local copies, and `index.json` / `COVERAGE.md`
because they were generated by node ON the machine rather than committed across.

### Section 4 — a gap in the standard, and the rule I propose

`measure-scene-visibility.mjs` passed beat 6 with **0 failures**, and it was right by its own definition:
the rod had plenty of pixels. It counts TOTAL screen coverage, so it cannot see that the coverage arrived
in four disconnected pieces with opaque drums between them. Every geometric proof in this build passed on
that composition too, because the geometry was never wrong.

> **PROPOSED RULE (RENDER-STANDARD section 3).** A structure's screen-space visibility is measured as
> CONNECTED FRAGMENTS, not only as total coverage. For any structure a beat narrates as continuous — a
> rod, a tube, a vessel, a nerve, a continuous sheet — the measure is the number of connected components
> of the pixels it is responsible for, obtained by rendering the beat with and without it and differencing.
> More than one component is a finding, whatever the total coverage. A continuous structure shown in
> pieces teaches a segmented one, and occlusion by an enclosing neighbour produces exactly that picture
> while every winding, volume, watertightness and coverage check passes.

The negative control matters as much: run the same measure over every beat's subject and it must not cry
wolf. I did — beat 8's `nucleus_pulposus` comes back as four near-equal fragments and that is CORRECT,
because there are four intervertebral discs. The rule is for structures the narration calls continuous.

   | light-tan #d9b382 | 35.1 | 35.1 | 86.7 | 50.2 | 79.3 | 19.2 | 31.0 |
   | ivory-cream #efe3c8 | 17.5 | 17.5 | 87.1 | 55.5 | 86.5 | 17.5 | 14.7 |
   | fibrous-blue #9fc3d8 | 16.8 | 16.8 | 68.8 | 41.7 | 69.3 | 11.4 | 16.2 |
   | blue-white #cfe0e8 | 5.5 | 5.5 | 77.0 | 50.9 | 80.4 | 5.5 | 7.1 |
   | **incumbent #a6acaf** | **16.3** | 16.3 | 66.5 | 32.6 | 62.6 | 5.0 | **2.7** |

   Amber **#c98b2f** wins on the stated rule. The incumbent's own numbers are the point: dE 16.3 is not
   small in the abstract, but at chroma 2.7 against another chroma-2.7 neutral it is a lightness
   difference that shading erases, which is exactly what the review saw. `annulus_fibrosus` is drawn in
   beat 8 and in no other beat, so the in-beat column is the one that decides; the corpus column is
   hygiene and amber's nearest corpus neighbour (16.2) never co-occurs with it.

2. **The cut-away cylinder is now a MEDIAN SECTION** — the convention `hemi` already uses on the embryo
   in this same scene, and the convention an atlas uses on a spine. It was an angular window of
   half-angle 0.95 rad over the middle 80% of each piece's height, which left an intact collar at each
   end: the "flanges". It is now half-angle exactly pi/2 over the WHOLE height, so the +x half — the
   camera's side on this beat — is gone and the window's own rim walls ARE the cut faces. The midline
   bodies (nucleus, regressed thread) are left whole and stand proud of the cut, which is what section 10
   already does for the embryo and for the same reason.
   RING 32, NOT 30, AND THAT IS MEASURED NOT TIDINESS: the rim wall lands on a ring VERTEX, so the cut is
   the median plane only if there is a vertex at pi/2. At ring 30 the nearest are 84 and 96 degrees and
   the cut would have overshot by 6 degrees. Acceptance row T measures `adultCutMaxX` = 6.1e-17 of the
   body's radius, against a floor of 1e-9.
   Three changes were needed in `axialSweep` to let a window run off both ends, and all three are
   provably inert for every other call in the file (they are gated on the new `winFull` flag, or on
   `cellWin`, which is false at the ends of a fenestra by construction): the window's v-span, skipping
   end-cap cells inside the window, and suppressing the spurious floor the v-direction rim-wall loop
   emitted at i = 0. The proof that they are inert is the harness: winding agreement 1.000000 over
   1,757,740 triangles across 13 stages x 5 variants, zero unpaired edges per body, and 26/26 rows pass.

3. **The disc now reads as a unit.** Two sub-changes. (a) `ADU_R_ANN` is no longer an independent 0.44
   against the body's 0.52 — it is DERIVED as `ADU_R_BODY`, because a disc is bounded by the end plates
   of the bodies it joins and its margin is level with theirs. It was drawing narrow washers tucked
   between wide drums. (b) The annulus's BORE now follows the nucleus it wraps, instead of being a
   straight cylinder of radius rN*1.04 over the disc's whole height while the nucleus occupies only 0.70
   of that height — which is the "ring of empty disc space" the review saw as "a small ellipsoid in a
   large hollow". A disc has no void in it. The bore is the nucleus's own profile at the same 4%
   clearance, closing to `ADU_BORE_MIN` where the nucleus has ended, floored rather than zero because a
   zero-radius lumen is the degenerate quad the fenestra note already records the cost of.
   Measured (row T): `discBoreTaper` 0.0511 against a floor of 0.25 — a straight bore is exactly 1.000
   and that 1.000 IS the defect; `discBoreClearance` 0.0400, the declared clearance.

   **WHAT DID NOT CHANGE, deliberately: the conservation.** The nucleus's radius is still solved by
   bisection against the volume the bodies squeeze out plus what already lay between them, its shape is
   untouched, and claim B8-grown's pinned `nucleusRadiusFrac` is unmoved at 2.2567 — checked, not
   assumed. The legibility fault was in the annulus and the cut, not in the solved parameter.

**BEAT 3 — the neural plate was a steep midline cone.** The fault was in the biology, not the drawing.
`npThickAt` mapped thickness LINEARLY onto a signal that falls EXPONENTIALLY with distance, so the
thickness fell exponentially too. But induction is already modelled as a THRESHOLD — `npHalf()` is the
crossing, and it is what sets the plate's width — and a cell either is induced and becomes tall
pseudostratified columnar, or is not and stays cuboidal. There is no cell of intermediate height in the
middle of a neural plate. So the response is SATURATED above threshold and the only shaping is at the
lateral border.

TWO BORDER WIDTHS WERE TRIED FIRST AND BOTH WERE MEASURED, NOT ARGUED AWAY:

| border width | plateau at t 0.40 /block | plateau at t 0.70 /hemi |
|---|---|---|
| the graded law the review rejected | 0.150 | 0.350 |
| one plate-thickness (hEcto * NP_MAXFAC = 0.728) | 0.175 | 0.600 |
| one flat-ectoderm cell (hEcto = 0.280) | 0.325 | 0.600 |
| **two of the plate's own mesh columns (2 * half / NP_COLS)** | **0.425** | **0.800** |

The first of those is WORSE than the law it replaced: 0.728 is wider than the plate's own half-width
(0.646), so the ramp swallowed the plate and made a smoother dome. That is why the border is now scaled
to the plate rather than being a length that can outgrow it: a threshold response has no biological
width, and what sets the bevel is the mesh — the narrowest a mesh can carry without a staircase is two
of its own columns. `NP_COLS` is now one constant used by both the builder and `npThickAt`, so the
border and the mesh that has to carry it cannot drift apart.

The thickness profile at beat 6's own t, read off the built triangles at 13 stations from the midline to
the plate's edge: 0.7023 x11 then 0.4886, 0.2727 — flat-topped for eleven twelfths and then a bevel. At
beat 3's t the plate's half-width varies along its length, so the row-Y measure (which normalises by the
BBOX half-width, i.e. the widest station) under-reports and gives 0.425; at the mid-length station the
profile is 0.6581 x6 then a bevel. Row I is untouched at 2.5366.

New acceptance **row Y**, floor `NPPLATEAU` 0.25, set between the two WORST numbers rather than the two
best — 70% headroom on the one it must pass, 40% clear of the one it must reject. Two negative cases:
the graded law's 0.150, and a plateau of a tenth.

**BEAT 3 vs BEAT 7 — two transverse conventions.** Said to the student, not harmonised. Harmonising
means moving beat 3 to `inferior`, which points it at the caudal face of the block — still a hollow tube
at that t, with no notochordal plate on it, which is the one thing beat 3 exists to show. The sentence
is on BEAT 7's narration and not beat 3's for two reasons: beat 3's narration is carried VERBATIM from
the sequence version and gap 0 forbids rewriting it, and a student meets the mirror when the SECOND
transverse section appears. `gaps[7]` records that the argument now reaches a student and not only a
reviewer.

**BEAT 6 — not touched.** `sclerotome` opacity is still 0.4, verified in the scene after every edit.
