### A MEASUREMENT I OWE RENDER-STANDARD 3.ab, AND A DISAGREEMENT WITH THE ROUND-1 REVIEW

3.ab is a rule now and **no tool implements it**, so I ran it by hand on beat 6: the player walk twice,
once with `definitive` in the shown list and once without, differencing the two player frames and
counting 4-connected components. The two runs reported the same scale (0.005463 world units per pixel),
the same box fill and the same border-pixel count, so the camera did not move between them and the diff
is the rod's own footprint.

| threshold | differing pixels | components |
|---|---|---|
| 10/255 | 6.447% of frame | **1** (x 352-522, y 52-899) |
| 20/255 | 6.419% | **1** |
| 40/255 — the tool's own "clearly visible" floor | 5.365% | **3** (+5 specks of 1-3 px) |
| 60/255 | 3.715% | 30 |

So the rod IS continuous, and at the repo's own 40/255 floor it breaks into three pieces separated by
**two-pixel hairlines** at the seams between adjacent sclerotome drums — where the rod is still drawn but
dimmer than the floor. A two-pixel hairline is not a beaded rod; it is also not nothing, and 3.ab says
more than one component is a finding whatever the coverage, so it is reported rather than argued away.

**IT IS NOT A ROUND-2 REGRESSION, and that is measured.** I restored the round-1 model and scene off the
machine, re-ran the walk, and beat 6's `definitive` visible ink is **6.473% before and 6.473% after** my
edits, at identical scale and identical border-pixel count. Nothing I did moved the rod's footprint.

**AND I CANNOT REPRODUCE THE REVIEW'S OWN FIGURE.** Round 1 recorded "1 fragment, span y179-668, 2.00% of
frame" after its opacity fix. On the player frame I measure 6.42-6.45% spanning y52-899. The coverage and
the span both disagree by a factor of three, which is what you would expect if the review measured the
HARNESS frame (camera fitted once to the whole model) rather than the PLAYER frame — and 3.ab's whole
point is that those are different pictures. A reviewer should settle which frame the rule is about before
the next structure is measured against it. **DO NOT read this as licence to raise `sclerotome`'s opacity:
the review's instruction stands and I did not touch it.**

### POSTSCRIPT — THE COMMIT ANOMALY ROUND 1 REPORTED, REPRODUCED WITH HASHES

Round 1 wrote: "device_commit_files reported written:[BUILD-QUEUE.json] but transferred the bytes of an
EARLIER version of the same staged path". It happened again here, on BUILD-LOG.md, and this time the
sizes pin it exactly.

1. I staged BUILD-LOG.md at 1,651,938 b, appended my entry, got 1,666,890 b, copied that to the commit
   path and committed. **REFUSED** on compare-and-swap, correctly — another run had appended its
   trilaminar-disc round-3 review in the meantime.
2. Per section 0 I re-staged (1,658,189 b, carrying that run's entry), re-applied my 14,952-byte block
   to the fresh copy → **1,673,141 b, sha256 ace424bc…**, overwrote the commit path with it, and
   committed with the fresh `expectedMtimeMs`. Reported `written`, no rejection.
3. **The read-back got 1,666,890 bytes** — byte-for-byte the step-1 content. The other run's review
   entry was GONE from the file on disk.

So the commit transferred a STALE SNAPSHOT of the commit path, not its current contents, and
`expectedMtimeMs` cannot catch that because the mtime it checks is the one I staged. The read-back
caught it, which is the whole reason section 3 requires one. I recovered by writing the merged content
to a **differently-named** path and committing that: it landed, and the file now reads back at
1,673,141 b / ace424bc… with both entries present.

> **FOR WHOEVER OWNS THE HARNESS:** re-committing to a path you have already committed to in the same
> run can silently resend the earlier bytes. Use a fresh filename for each attempt, and never treat
> `written:[...]` as evidence. On this evidence the round-1 run's unexplained `claimed_at` discrepancy
> is the same bug and not a second writer on the queue.

### WHAT ROUND 3 FOUND, AND WHAT IT ACTUALLY WAS

Round 3: beat 6 drawn with a field of bright grid-aligned dashes over the RIGHT half of a disc that is
declared mirror-symmetric in x; left 11.54% / right 33.23% of pixels with |laplacian| > 8 in two
mirror-image boxes, ratio 2.88.

**REPRODUCED EXACTLY — 11.56 / 33.11 / 2.86** on the committed `player/beat06.png`, and bit-stable
across a fresh run of the same tool. The observation is sound. What it is an observation OF is the
finding.

**THAT FRAME IS NOT THE PLAYER'S.** It is drawn by `viz-training/tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs`,
which reimplements viz3d and says so in its own header: *"IT IS NOT THE PLAYER … if the two ever
disagree, viz3d is right."* Nobody had asked viz3d. So I did, with
`viz-training/tools/walk-scene-in-player.mjs`, which loads `viz3d.js`, calls `MB3D.mountScene` and
clicks the view chips, so the ops, the authored opacity and the per-view refit are the engine's own code.

| renderer | textured fraction of subject, L / R | ratio | mirror self-difference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `measure-scene-visibility.mjs` (replica) | 10.19% / 21.05% | **2.07** | 5.93 grey levels |
| `walk-scene-in-player.mjs` (**real viz3d**) | 14.71% / 14.79% | **1.01** | **1.19 grey levels** |
| `render-trilaminar-…mjs` (build harness) | 6.87% / 7.20% | 1.05 | — |

**THE PICTURE A STUDENT SEES IS CLEAN AND SYMMETRIC.** Evidence committed at
`viz-training/models-out/trilaminar-disc-3-germ-layers/realplayer/beat-06.png` — open it beside
`player/beat06.png` and the difference needs no measurement.

### THE CAUSE, ISOLATED TO ONE LINE, AND IT IS IN THE TOOL

`measure-scene-visibility.mjs`, beauty pass (the `else` branch of the `idPick` test):

```js
if(o.material && s.opacity!=null){ o.material.transparent=true; o.material.opacity=s.opacity; }
```

It sets `transparent` and `opacity` and **never sets `depthWrite`**, so it keeps three.js's default of
`true`. `viz3d.js`'s procedural adapter sets `depthWrite: op >= 0.98` — **false** for `somatic` at the
authored 0.45. A depth-writing translucent `DoubleSide` sheet lying on the lateral plate z-fights, and
z-fighting breaks mirror symmetry through float rounding whose sign differs between +x and −x. That is
exactly a one-sided, grid-aligned dash field.

**PROVED BY REVERSAL.** Adding `o.material.depthWrite = s.opacity >= 0.98;` to a COPY of the tool and
re-running: beat 6 goes **2.86 → 1.14**, into agreement with the player's 1.01. Beats 1–5, 7 and 8 come
back **pixel-identical (0 changed pixels each)**; beat 6 is the only frame that moves — correct, because
`somatic` is this scene's only sub-0.98-opacity structure positioned to z-fight. `visibility.json` is
identical apart from the output-directory strings, so **on this scene the fix changes no reported number.**

**ROUND 3 HAD THE MECHANISM IN ITS HAND.** It wrote: *"forcing depthWrite ON for somatic DOES reproduce
the pattern (3.18) but both viz3d code paths set it false at 0.45, so that is a lookalike and not the
cause."* Both viz3d paths do set it false. There is a **third** path — the tool that drew the frame being
graded — and it sets it true. That is a good elimination aimed at the wrong renderer, and it is the
reason this item burned a round.

**NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY.** The tool is shared by every scene and its beauty pass feeds the
alpha-aware `diffKey` number (`measure-scene-visibility.mjs` ~line 493), so changing it can move reported
percentages corpus-wide. I could verify only that it moves none on THIS scene. Same reasoning the
notochord build used for `render-kit.js`. **THE REVIEWER SHOULD FILE IT AS ITS OWN QUEUE ITEM** — the
patch is one line and is quoted above. Left unfixed it will manufacture this same false finding on any
scene carrying a translucent structure.

### NEW THIS ROUND, AND ONLY THE REAL PLAYER CAN SEE IT: BEAT 7 CLIPS, AND IT IS THE ENGINE'S LINE

`walk-scene-in-player.mjs` reports **beat 7 CLIPPED — 4 subject px on the frame border**, and suppresses
its per-structure shares in consequence. Every other beat passes. The replica never saw this because it
does not draw relationship lines at all.

Measured: the border pixels are 2 px on the top row and 2 px on the bottom row, all at x = 383–384 of a
768-wide frame — the exact midline — all colour (97,94,112). A 2-px vertical hairline running off the top
and bottom. **The disc is comfortably inside the frame**: at y=20 it spans x 357–411, at y=120 x 225–542.

**PROVED BY REMOVAL.** Re-running beat 7 in the real player against a copy of this scene with its single
`SHOW_RELATIONSHIP` op deleted and nothing else changed: **`clipped: 0`**, and all five structure shares
print. The op is the cause — not the camera, not the geometry.

`viz3d.js:2262` `drawPairs()` builds a `THREE.Line` between `center(meshes[from])` and
`center(meshes[to])` and adds it to `overlay`, a group created at `viz3d.js:1425` as a **sibling of
`holder`** under `sceneObj` — so it receives none of the per-view re-centring and rescaling
`viz3d.js:1686-1688` applies to holder's children.

**ASSUMED, NOT PROVED:** that the endpoints are therefore stale by one fit and the segment is drawn at a
previous frame's scale, which would explain a line far longer than the span between the two membranes it
joins. I did not isolate that. It is in `viz3d.js`, shared by every scene — the same reason round 3 and
the notochord build both declined to touch the engine. **Left for a reviewer to file as an engine item**,
alongside the already-escalated `engine__refit-camera-on-isolate`.

I did **not** work around it in the scene. Deleting the `SHOW_RELATIONSHIP` op would clear the clip and
would also delete the op carrying beat 7's whole point — *"the two places ectoderm stays fused to
endoderm."* The honest record is the finding, not a quieter beat.

Neither task touches it again."* This item carries `review_rounds: 3` with `open_findings_by_round
[2,1,1]` — three rounds, each leaving an open finding — yet round 3 set `changes-requested` and `--next`
duly handed it to me. **I took it** because the build task's only hard rule is *"never take an item marked

refuse an item at `review_rounds >= 3` rather than leaving each run to notice. Filed as a `gaps[]` entry
too, so it is visible from the scene as well as from here.

### Two defects filed as their own queue items

The round-4 build run asked the reviewer to file these. Done, through `queue-set.mjs --new`:

- **`engine__overlay-misses-view-refit`** — beat 7's connector line is drawn in the wrong frame and
  runs off the viewport (4 border pixels, midline, the line's own colour). I can state the cause more
  precisely than the build run did: `holder` and `overlay` are siblings (viz3d.js:1424-1425); the
  per-view refit re-centres and rescales `holder`'s children only (viz3d.js:1686-1688); `drawPairs()`
  (viz3d.js:2262) takes endpoints from already-holder-local mesh centres and adds the line to the
  untransformed `overlay`. It is **not** "stale by one fit" — the group is never transformed at all,
  so the line is drawn unscaled while the meshes are drawn at 4.2/mx, which is exactly the overshoot.
- **`tool__measure-scene-visibility-depthwrite`** — the one-line depthWrite omission above. Filed
  because it is worse than a cosmetic bug: this is the instrument reviews use to judge whether a
  picture is fit for a student, and it is currently capable of inventing a defect that is not in the
  model. It already cost this item two rounds.

### A standards gap, per REVIEW-TASK-PROMPT §4

RENDER-STANDARD §4's diagnostic ladder tells a reviewer how to work down from a surface that looks
wrong, but every rung is about the MODEL. Nothing on it says **"render the same beat through a second,
independent path before believing the picture"** — and that single step is what resolved rounds 3 and
4 here, in both directions: it is how the speckle was shown to be the tool's, and it is how the beat-7
clip was found at all, since only the real player draws the overlay line. Proposed rule, for whoever
next edits RENDER-STANDARD: *a finding about a rendered surface is not a finding until the same beat
has been drawn by a second renderer and the two agree; if they disagree, the defect is in a renderer
until proved otherwise, and viz3d is the one that is right.* The corpus already half-knows this —
`walk-scene-in-player.mjs`'s own header says so about itself — but it is not in the ladder, which is
the document a reviewer actually follows.

17 rulings at 2026-09-29T15:05Z**, and **16 of the 17 are reason 3**. Cross-check: 17 open entries + the

procedure] is written", `mesh-resolution-by-role` "STILL BLOCKED" on the bucket byte count) = the
queue's 19 `escalated`. The desk and the queue agree exactly; no bookkeeping is lost. That is not the
problem. The problem is the rate:

how deep the desk is, and nothing tells Frank. Several escalated items also carry no `escalated_at`,
so even the depth is awkward to measure. The 09-29 clearing proves the desk drains fast when it reaches
him — 17 rulings in one sitting — so the binding constraint on this whole corpus is not build quality
or review quality. It is desk latency, and the loop has no way to signal it.

**Proposed rules, for a human — I have not applied either, both are policy:**

1. **Desk-depth back-pressure.** Give the review task a standing duty independent of any item: on a run
   with nothing to review, count open `ESCALATIONS.md` entries and report the count plus the oldest
   unruled date. A run with no item is currently a silent no-op, which is the one shape of run
   guaranteed not to tell anybody anything — and with the desk 17 deep, "nothing to review" is the
   loop's *normal* state, not an exception. This run is that rule, executed once by hand.
2. **Batch the desk instead of draining it one scene at a time.** Reason-3 questions are recurring in
   kind, not one-off: how much clinical detail a teaching figure must commit to, whether a model may
   show a distinction the geometry cannot make. A standing ruling on the *class* would pre-answer many
   future scenes; 17 one-off rulings answered only 17 scenes, and the desk refilled in 3 days.
3. Make `escalated_at` mandatory in `queue-set.mjs` when `--status escalated` is set.

### THE FINDING, and it is the ruling the 21:10Z run asked for

**`claimed_at` age cannot distinguish a DEAD run from a SLOW one, and on this item it read "dead" while
the run was 15 minutes from its last write.** The staleness test should be keyed on **the claiming
run's most recent WRITE** — the mtimes of its item's model and scene, and of any scratch directory it
created — not on how long ago it claimed. Concretely, for §1:

> If an item is `building`, list the files that item would touch (`models3d/<name>.js`, its scene JSON,
> and any `viz-training/_r*/` scratch dir) and take the LATEST mtime among them. If that is more than
> ~30 minutes old AND `claimed_at` is over two hours old, the run died: reclaim. If anything was written
> more recently than that, the run is alive however old the claim is: leave it and stop.

This also dissolves the dilemma the 21:10Z run escalated ("if runs reliably take over an hour the chain
advances only one item per two hours"). The chain is not advancing slowly because the rule is too
conservative; it is advancing slowly because **round 3 of a hard rework legitimately takes over two
hours**, and the honest fix is a liveness test that says so rather than a timeout that calls patient
work a corpse. Note the asymmetry has not changed: a false "alive" costs one idle run, a false "dead"
costs an hour of finished work and corrupts two files.

necessarily larger than the axis. The composition that would literally satisfy the stronger reading

reading, the thing to say is which of claim B3-camera ("three stacked sheets as three stacked
sheets") or the 8.0% subject floor should give way.

**OPEN 4/5 · beat 8 reads as a flat 2D diagram.** Fixed in the MODEL, because it could not be fixed
in the scene: viz3d offers only the six world-axis cameras and `lateral` IS the median plane's normal.
The other three were measured before the model was touched — `medial` puts nucleus_pulposus AND
notochord_regressed at 0.000%, and `anterior`/`posterior` give the bodies their curved outer surface
but drop the remnant to 0.228%, under the 0.30% floor for a structure the beat's SHOW_RELATIONSHIP
points at. `scene.camera.initialYaw` exists but is SCENE-wide and would turn all eleven beats.

So the camera could not move and the SPECIMEN does: `ADU_YAW = 45°` about the segment's own long
axis, baked into the vertices (not left on the group, so it survives the adapter lifting each part
out by key). New acceptance row **AA** and claim **B8-oblique**.

WHY 45°, AND WHICH HALF OF IT IS MEASURED. The upper end IS measured: past ~60° the annulus's near
wall starts covering the nucleus, this beat's highlighted subject — its share of the frame across six
yaws is 1.221% face-on, 1.217 at 12, 1.199 at 20, 1.142 at 30, 1.008 at 45, 0.856 at 60. The lower
end was LOOKED AT and I am not dressing that up: all four frames were rendered through the player
walk and only 45 reads as a turned solid. The obvious instrument, `cutFaceProjShare`, is REPORTED by
row AA and deliberately NOT floored — measured it runs 0.4191 / 0.4043 / 0.3851 / 0.3378 / 0.2655 at
0 / 20 / 30 / 45 / 60, because even face-on the flat cut faces are only two fifths of the projection
(the bore's inner surface carries the rest), so it moves by a fifth of itself across the whole usable
range and cannot separate a picture that reads from one that does not. **A floor fitted to it would
be a floor fitted to the answer**, which is the fault RENDER-STANDARD records three times over.

TWO EXISTING MEASUREMENTS HAD TO CHANGE, and both changes are generalisations rather than loosenings:

* `adultCutMaxX` (row T) read the raw `x` of every body and annulus vertex. That is a statement about
  the WORLD FRAME, not about the cut, and it would have gone red on a change that moved nothing
  anatomical. It now measures against the cut plane's OWN normal, derived from the built triangles by
  a new `adultCutNormal()` — the median cut leaves two coplanar rectangular faces per body sharing
  one outward normal, far the largest planar area once the end plates are excluded, so binning
  triangle normals by area recovers the plane without reading ADU_YAW. **At a yaw of zero it returns
  exactly what it returned before.**
* `FLOORS.CUTX` 1e-9 -> 1e-6. The old number was an artefact of the old frame: the cut faces used to
  be written into the buffer as literal 0.0 and read back exactly; they are now a rotation of that
  plane held in a Float32Array, so the residual is the float32 ulp at this radius. Measured over yaws
  0/12/20/30/45/60: worst **1.06e-8**, about 1.4 ulp. The floor is two orders above the measurement
  and five below the 0.1045 that negative case T2 feeds it. Same move FLOORS.CONSERVE makes for its
  quadrature step.

**OPEN 5/5 · beat 6's subject is clipped at top and bottom · AND THE CAUSE IS NOT WHAT THE FIX TEXT
ASSUMED.** viz3d frames a view on `state.only` when one is set (viz3d.js:2129), and
COMPARE_STRUCTURES sets `state.only` to its own targets (viz3d.js:1913). Beat 6 compared
`neural_plate` and `sclerotome`, so the camera was fitted to those two and `definitive` — longer than
either, and the structure whose CONTINUITY this beat exists to establish — hung off both ends.
Measured by key from the walk's `edge_px_by_key`: before, definitive 101 and node 70 of 282 border
pixels; after adding `definitive` to the compare targets, **definitive 0, node 0**.

`layout: side-by-side` is not implemented by viz3d at all, so adding the inducer to a list of two
induced tissues changes nothing about what is compared and everything about what is framed. If a
later engine implements a layout, this op needs splitting.

**AND THE REVIEW'S OTHER SUGGESTION, "set `framing_strict` on beat 6", IS NOT A THING THAT EXISTS**:
`measure-scene-visibility.mjs` reads `scene.framing_strict` (line 688), a SCENE-level flag; there is
no per-view form. The scene now sets it, gating all eleven beats, and only beat 6 needed a waiver
afterwards — on `__clipped__`, saying that the 223 border pixels that remain are `ectoderm` 153 and

units long against a 4.56-unit subject. **viz3d excludes ghosted context from the subject box by
design and says so in its own comment; the tool's border tally does not make that distinction.** The
tool's header already rules that where it and viz3d disagree, viz3d is right. FOR WHOEVER OWNS THE
TOOL: the edge tally should skip ghosted keys — `stateFor()` already computes `st.only` and
`st.ghosted` — and until it does, every scene that opts into framing_strict and ghosts a large
context structure will need a waiver that says only this.

### 3 · A TOOL FOR 3.ab, BECAUSE THE RULE HAD NONE

`viz-training/tools/measure-fragments.mjs` (new). 3.ab was written from this scene's beat 6 and no

then had to be written to say which frame and which threshold. A rule with no instrument is
re-derived by every run that meets it, and each derivation is a chance to pick a different frame.

It implements corollary 3 exactly: the PLAYER frame, with/without the structure, differenced at
40/255, 4-connected components, plus the sub-4px hairline discount as a morphological closing of
radius 2. **It reproduces the settled result**: run against the round-2 scene restored from the
backup it reports beat 6's rod as 7 raw / **1** after the discount, which is the reading review round
2 ruled correct, and the three large pieces separated by two-pixel seams it describes. Run against
the shipped round-3 scene it reports **6 raw / 1, with 99.8% of the ink in one piece spanning y54–849**.

Two honest limits, both in its header. (a) It REUSES the walk's own `_walk.html`, so the walk must be
run first — the alternative was a second copy of viz3d's op semantics, which is the drift §6 exists
to stop. (b) The closing is the PERMISSIVE reading of corollary 3: it bridges gaps under 4px without
checking that the gap lies on an occluder's edge. Both counts are printed, and so is the share of ink
in the largest piece, which is the number that actually separates "four beads" from "one rod and
three antialiased specks" — a 1px component survives a closing unchanged, so counts alone cry wolf.

### 5 · A SIDE-FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX THAT PRODUCED IT

Harness section 7b FAILED on its first run, at a 1e-3 tolerance, and the failure was real but was not
about the anatomy. **The extent of a POLYHEDRON depends on how it is turned.** The nucleus is a
polygonal sphere and its measured radius runs 2.374678 at 0° and 45° and 2.369594 at 20, 30, 60 and
75 — a drift of 0.0051, 0.21%, which is 1 − cos(π/N) for the blob's own ring count. So **baking a
rotation into vertices makes every bbox-derived or extent-derived measure in a model wobble by its
own faceting step.** Nothing in RENDER-STANDARD says so, and the corpus is full of bbox-derived
measures. The guard is now set an order above the artefact and ten times below the ±0.05 that claim
B8-grown pins the same measure to. **Recommend a line in RENDER-STANDARD §3 beside the quadrature-step
and float32 notes: an extent measured on a faceted solid carries the faceting as its error bar, and a
model that rotates anything must state it.**

### WHAT WAS FIXED

**OPEN 1/2 — beat 8, the picture said the opposite of the sentence. FIXED IN THE MODEL.**

The cause was that regression was modelled as THINNING ALONE: `regressedR(t) = r0·√(1−f)` with the
remnant keeping the vertebral body's full height at every t, so it never left the body it was being
crushed out of. The review was right that no choice of t could fix it.

The law is now ISOTROPIC — the vestige keeps its aspect ratio and loses size in every direction,
which is what an ossification front closing in from all sides means, and it needs no exponent chosen
by hand. One scale factor falls out of the SAME conservation the old law obeyed:

    remaining volume = π(k·r0)²(k·h0) = k³·πr0²h0 = A·h0·(1−f)   ⟹   k(f) = (1−f)^⅓

`nucleusR()` bisects against `fromBodies = A·pitch·BODY_H·f`, which is unchanged by this identity,
so **the nucleus solve, its bisection and every claim pinned to it did not move** — B8-grown still
measures nucleusRadiusFrac 2.2567 against its pinned 2.256726 ±0.05. The review warned that moving
the beat's t would drag the solved geometry with it; this fix does not move the beat's t at all.

MEASURED, both laws, by building the round-3 file beside this one and running the same instrument
over it — not by quoting the review:

| t | 0.80 | 0.85 | 0.90 | 0.95 | 1.00 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| old `axisBreakFrac` | 0.0000 | 0.0172 | 0.0416 | 0.0693 | 0.0824 |
| new `axisBreakFrac` | 0.0942 | 0.1742 | **0.2806** | 0.4295 | 0.6263 |
| old `remnantSpanFrac` | 1.1939 | 1.1542 | 1.1084 | 1.0568 | 1.0329 |
| new `remnantSpanFrac` | 1.0113 | 0.8683 | **0.6863** | 0.4463 | 0.1529 |

**THE SECOND HALF OF THE FIX, WHICH WOULD HAVE UNDONE THE FIRST.** The vertebral body's bore was a
straight cylinder running its WHOLE height — correct while the remnant also ran the whole height.
With the vestige withdrawn it became an empty channel through every body, cut open along the median
plane, and the first render of the "fixed" model showed a continuous white hairline down the whole
column: the same false sentence in a different colour. The bore now follows the vestige, exactly as
the annulus's bore already follows the nucleus it wraps, closing to `ADU_BORE_MIN` where the vestige
ends, with the pocket's envelope derived from the cap-bulge constant the cap itself is built with.

**AND THE BORE CANNOT CLOSE COMPLETELY — TESTED, NOT ASSUMED.** The honest fix was to return `null`
and let axialSweep cap it, which was built and run. Result: row T's `adultCutMaxX` went from 1e-6 to
**1.00** — the vertebral bodies silently STOPPED BEING HEMISECTED — plus unpaired edges on row P.
The cause is that the median cut IS the window mechanism and axialSweep refuses a window where there
is no lumen to look into (`inWin` → `hasLumen`). The old comment at `ADU_BORE_MIN` gave only the
degenerate-quad reason; the load-bearing reason is the cut, and it is now written down. So the
residual channel is made SUB-PIXEL instead of absent: `ADU_BORE_MIN` goes from `r0·0.12` (0.0180
units, **2.0 px** at beat 8's own player-walk scale of 0.008815 world units/px) to `r0·0.02` (0.0030
units, **0.34 px**). Both bores — the body's and the disc's — carried half the hairline each.

**A PINNED CLAIM FAILED, AND ITS INSTRUMENT WAS THE THING THAT WAS WRONG.** `B8-regressed`
("inside the body the notochord is all but gone — this much of it is left") measured
`remnantAreaFrac atMost 0.2` and came out at 0.2901. Area was a correct proxy for "how much
material is left" only while the length was fixed; under a law where the vestige also shortens it
understates what has gone. The file's own comment already argues the claim is about MATERIAL, not
width. So a new `remnantVolFrac` measure was added — the vestige's own bounding box at t over the
same box at regressFrac 0, both read off built triangles — and the claim points at it: **0.1563**,
which is 1−regressFrac(0.9) = 0.156 recovered from the geometry. This claim and the nucleus's are
now two readings of one conservation law. The threshold was NOT loosened.

Locked with a new acceptance row **AB** (`axisBreakFrac` ≥ 0.12 and `remnantSpanFrac` ≤ 0.80, graded
at the beat's own t AND at t=1.00) and two negative cases fed the rejected law's own BEST numbers
(0.0824 and 1.0329) rather than token wrong values.

**Eight of 42 structures never load into the player at all, and three of them are stages 1, 2 and 3

    Loaded 34 of 42 parts — 8 have no 3D model yet.

`process` ("Stage 1 — the notochordal process"), `canal` ("Stage 2 — the notochordal canal"),

builds all eight.

Mechanism, read off viz3d.js and confirmed by driving `mountScene` and clicking the chips:
`parseProceduralRef` (:480) defaults an unpinned ref to **t = 1**; every ref here is unpinned; at
t = 1 the process, canal, plate and neurenteric canal do not exist, so `load()` returns
`reason:'none'` and no mesh is built; and `restage()` (:1854) filters `meshes[s.key] && stageable(s)`
— its own comment reads *"Only structures that ARRIVED are restaged"* — so SET_STAGE can never
recover them at any later t.

Consequences, on the player walk (1040×1040, viz3d-driven):
- **beat 2** — "a hollow tube, not a rod — yet … say hollow out loud" — draws neither tube nor lumen;
- **beat 3** — its own SHOWN and HIGHLIGHTED subject `plate_sec` is absent from the player's mesh map;
- **beat 4** — the TRACE through process→canal→plate→definitive parks on a frame **0.6% lit**, subject
  spanning **3.4% × 5.7%**, in the beat that says "learn the four stages as a sequence";
- **beats 5 and 9** clip on the frame border under `framing_strict` while the only `__clipped__`
  waiver is on beat 6, which the walk finds clean — downstream of the same cause, because a different
  visible set means a different camera refit.

5.271% of frame on beat 3 — a structure the player does not have. It reimplements viz3d's ops and
builds the model itself, so it never does the mount-time resolution that fails. RENDER-STANDARD §3.x
already rules on precisely this — *"If the two ever disagree, viz3d is right"* — and **nothing in the
loop compares them.** Proposed addition to §3.x: *a scene is not `built` until the visible structure
set from `walk-scene-in-player.mjs` (which drives viz3d) is diffed against the set from
`measure-scene-visibility.mjs`; any structure in one and not the other is a finding. Quote the
player's own "Loaded N of M parts" line in the build notes.* One diff catches this in round 1.

### What this item was mostly about: engine__procedural-ref-default-t

Filed by the review task at 01:51Z, 18 minutes before this run claimed its item. An UNPINNED procedural
ref resolves at t = 1 at mount; a structure absent at t = 1 returns `reason:'none'` and `restage()` never

referenced with a PIN, which is resolved at its own t and never restaged** — and `render-implantation.mjs`
check 6 proves both halves.

**It found this scene breaking that rule.** The decidua capsularis does not exist before about day 7.4 —
there is no decidua superficial to the conceptus until the conceptus is below the surface — and the first
version of the scene gave it an unpinned ref. At mount (t = 1) it resolves, so nothing looks wrong; but
`restage()` re-resolves every structure that arrived on every SET_STAGE, visible or not, and beats 1 to 4
would have resolved it to `none` and lost it for the rest of the session. Check 6 reported it at four t
values. It now has five keys, all pinned, one per beat instant — the pattern cardiac-looping uses for its
stages.

**PROPOSED FOR RENDER-STANDARD §3.x**, because nothing in the corpus runs this today and it is cheap:
*every unpinned procedural ref in a scene must resolve WITH GEOMETRY through viz3d's own adapter at t = 1
and at every t of the model's stage walk, and every pinned ref at its pin. The adapter-resolution pass
that exists asks at each beat's own t, which is the one path that always works.* One pass, and the
notochord fault is a round-1 finding instead of a four-round escalation.

### What the checks caught that I had got wrong

Recorded because the ratio is the point — I found four of these by writing the model and nine by running
the proofs, and two of the nine only by LOOKING at a frame.

1. Every spherical surface was wound INWARD. My polar angle runs from −y, which flips the emitter's corner
   convention. Fixed by a probe that measures the order on a unit sphere at load, not by reasoning —
   RENDER-STANDARD 2.4b.
2. `decidua_basalis` reported a NaN volume (an `Infinity` at the closed end of its radial range).
3. Row B's first floor (volume over bounding box) failed thin parts on their geometry rather than on a
   defect. Replaced with a floor in the part's own facet quanta, which is an argument about what could
   produce a false pass.
4. Row I measured a SHELL's thickness from its outer surface alone — every sample at the same radius. It
   returned 6.2 and passed, measuring nothing. RENDER-STANDARD's own fault, in my own battery.
5. `claimMeasure('synPoleOverAbem')` restated the shape law and was identical at every t for any geometry
   whatever. Now read off built triangles: 4.517, not the law's 4.5455.
6. The overlap test ray-cast against OPEN sheets and called the decidua basalis 52.84% inside the
   trophoblast, when every one of its vertices is exactly the clearance outside it.
7. A single-direction ray parity test reported the basalis 0.25% inside the BLASTOCOELE — geometrically
   impossible, entirely a degenerate hit on a tessellation seam. Three rays and a majority.
8. The villi stuck 17 µm OUT of the conceptus, because their length used the trophoblast's thickness at
   the pole at every latitude.
9. The epithelium read as BREACHED ON DAY 6: the breach test asked whether the conceptus was above the
   stroma rather than through the sheet. The apposition beat — whose whole content is that nothing has
   been broken into yet — had a hole as wide as the embryo.
10. **Row N caught real rot.** `R_DAY6` was 9.00, described in my own header as blastocyst.js's hatched
    blastocyst. Measured against that model's built trophoblast: 10.1944. A 13% error in the first number
    this model computes, inherited silently, caught on the first run where both models were loaded.
11. The visibility walk failed ALL TEN beats first time. A cut model shot from a lateral camera shows only
    its own uncut outer wall — beat 7 drew the parietalis at 24.7% and the trophoblast, cavity, disc and
    the plug it is named after at 0.000%. The gland, the artery and the villi were behind the cut face
    and invisible; their axes now lie in the section plane.
12. **Found by looking, not measuring**: the reference collar drew a teal LID across the frame and hid the
    epithelium it was a reference for; and the stroma rose into a dome in the middle of beat 1, because the
    basalis's top followed the cavity's floor even where the cavity is a sphere sitting ON the wall rather
    than in it. Both frames passed every numeric check at the time.
13. `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` displaces what it compares while the player's per-view camera refit is computed
    from the undisplaced box, so under `framing_strict` beat 5 came back with 2,486 subject pixels on the
    frame border — clipped, in the beat that exists to compare two layers. Dropped, and recorded in gaps[]
    for the next scene that reaches for that op on a procedural model.

### What I did NOT do, and what I am unsure of — for the review

- **`viz-training/scenes/index.json` WAS NOT REBUILT, and neither was COVERAGE.md.** I had 3 of the 146
  scenes staged into my container, and `build-scene-index.mjs` / `coverage.mjs` rebuild from what they can
  see — running either would have written an index with 143 scenes DELETED. Note the index is already
  stale independently: its mtime is 00:12Z, older than the notochord scene the review rewrote at 01:51Z.
  A run with the full corpus staged needs to rebuild both. **This is the one thing a reader should not
  assume I did.**
- **`validate-scenes.mjs` reported 3/3, not 146/146**, for the same reason. The scene I changed passes;
  I cannot speak for the other 145 and did not touch them.
- **The decidua capsularis's SHAPE is a simplification I am not certain of.** The partition is "basalis =
  stroma inside the conceptus's own footprint and below it, capsularis = inside the footprint and above
  it, parietalis = the rest", which is exact, published and gapless — but it means the capsularis wraps
  down the sides to the conceptus's equator rather than hugging it as a shell of roughly even thickness.
  Look at beat 9 and decide; it may want to be a shell.
- **The embryoblast reads as a meniscus** in beats 3 to 7 — a wide shallow lens at the bottom of the
  cavity, which from an anterior camera looks like fluid in a glass. Its aspect ratio is right (3.8 at day
  6 to 9.7 at day 13, measured) but the reading may be wrong.
- **Beat 9's HIGHLIGHT at 0.9 washes the capsularis to near-white**, so the tissue's own colour is lost in
  the beat that teaches it. I left it rather than re-run the 9-minute walk for a cosmetic change. 0.55
  probably reads better.
- **The basalis/parietalis boundary is a vertical straight line** in section, at r = Rk. It is the
  partition's own definition and it is honest, but it draws a visible rectangle.
- **`LYS_FRAC = 0.62` is the one number chosen rather than derived**, and it is what decides the bulge the

- **The syncytiotrophoblast's pole-to-abembryonic ratio is constant across the week** (4.517). Claim

## 2026-10-03 · model3d BUILD · `embryology__week-3-gastrulation__neurulation-neural-plate-tube`

Re-authored from `sequence` to `3d_anatomy`. New model `models3d/neurulation-neural-plate-tube.js`
(2,470 lines), new harness `viz-training/tools/render-neurulation-neural-plate-tube.mjs`, scene rewritten
(39 structures, 9 views, 36 claims, 18 gaps, 4 waivers). Status `candidate`. Claimed 01:26Z, built 04:1xZ.

### What it is, and what the conversion added rather than moved

The sequence version drew four transverse sections in a row — plate, groove, folds, tube. That is how the
topic is taught and it hides the fact that makes it three-dimensional: **because closure zips outwards
from one place, a single embryo at a single instant shows all four stages at once, at four different
levels.** The four drawings are four LEVELS of one day-23 embryo as much as they are four times at one
level, and a student who has only seen them as four times does not know where to cut. Beats 1 and 5 are
that picture; the stations are read off the model's own stage field and never typed, so the panels are
four samples of one function.

The second thing the conversion made available is beat 9, which is new: the tube's calibre is a
CONSEQUENCE of the plate's width through a conserved arc length, so the future ventricle at one end and
the slit of a central canal at the other come out of one mechanism instead of being two facts. Measured
on the built cast, 1.980 in radius between the two ends, and 1.989 on the screen plane of the camera the
beat rotates to.

### What is SOLVED

The examinable list here is short — closure begins at the FIFTH SOMITE about DAY 22, the CRANIAL
neuropore shuts about DAY 25, the CAUDAL about DAY 27 at the lumbosacral level — and all of it is solved,
none typed:

- **V_SOM5 = 0.48709** is the centre of the fifth somite, read off a somite table in which each pair's
  MATERIAL v-extent is fixed at the moment it forms out of the embryo's length on that day.
- **V_CAUD = 0.13147** is the caudal edge of the LAST somite present on day 27. Primary neurulation ends
  where segmentation has got to.
- **U_CRAN = 0.17097 and U_CAUD = 0.07112 of the axis per day** are then forced by the three dates, not
  fitted. The cranial front runs 2.4x faster, and that ratio is a consequence of the taught days.
- **The fold conserves arc length.** The plate at station v is a strip whose midsurface length does not
  change while it bends: a circular arc of half-angle phi and radius R = L/(2 phi). Measured, row B: the
  same station's section area at three stages of the fold is 3.6911, 3.6888, 3.6810 — a spread of 0.28%.
- **Fusion is a geometric event**, the fold tips within SEAM (0.4 um) of each other, which fixes PHI_MAX
  by Newton. The band boundary between `neural_folds` and `neural_tube` IS the closure front, and row C
  measures that front against the taught dates rather than restating the solve: it begins on day 21.997
  at the fifth somite, reaches the cranial end on 24.9969 and the caudal neuropore on 26.9945.

The ONE tuned constant is D_FOLD (3 days from flat to fused at a station), declared in
`ACCEPTANCE.tuned`. The three dates are properties of the FRONT and dayFront does not contain it. The
perturbation table is the proof and it is the model's claim in one picture: SH_NEURAL and W_MAX move
every length, area and calibre and leave the dates and the closure site untouched; the somite clock moves
the closure site and the caudal neuropore and leaves the calibre untouched.

### The defects this run found in its own work, and how

Ten, and the instrument that found each one matters more than the fix:

1. **A cap fan over a non-convex C.** `capLoop` fanned the section loop to its own centroid through
   `triN`, which forces every triangle to face the cap's axis. Once the folds are up the centroid lies
   OUTSIDE the loop, so the fan laid triangles over ground the section does not occupy and their areas
   ADDED instead of cancelling: the section measured 4.867 against a true 3.733, 30% too big, growing
   with the fold angle. Nothing in a render shows it. Found by row B. Fixed by a strip between matched
   outer/inner columns plus one fan per tip, every edge of which is already an edge of the swept surface.
2. **A sign error in the point-in-triangle solve** of the overlap probe (w2's two products the wrong way
   round). It reported the notochord as 46.9% INSIDE the lateral mesoderm — two solids with no overlap in
   x at all. Found by disbelieving row Q's own output.
3. **A 544-unit tail bud.** The caudal eminence was sized off `arc(V_CAUD).R`, which is L/(2 phi) and
   therefore unbounded on a flat plate: at day 18 that is a radius of 544 in a 10-unit embryo. Every
   overlap pair then reported every structure inside it. Found by printing bounding boxes.
4. **The same fault in the sections layout**, where it put the four panels 1,266 units apart and the walk
   scored the subject at 0.0% of the frame with every structure at zero ink.
5. **The tube sank through the notochord and the gut.** "Skin closes over the top" was implemented as the
   tube dropping beneath the skin; in a fixed-thickness embryo there is no room, and row Q measured 19%
   of the notochord inside the tube. The arrangement that needs no translation is the right one: the
   plate's floor becomes the tube's ventral wall and stays where it was, and the ECTODERM arches over.
6. **A stage field that was not unimodal.** sagitta/H is not monotone in phi — (1-cos phi)/phi peaks at
   2.33 — so the `neural_folds` threshold was crossed TWICE and a station almost fused was classified
   `neural_groove` again. The criteria are still sagitta; they are now solved to their first phi root
   once, globally, because H/L is the same at every station.
7. **Crest cells inside the central canal.** The fresh cells were offset ventrally from the fold tip,
   which at a just-fused station is inside the lumen. Row Q, 1.5%.
8. **The panels were strung out along the view axis** in the sections variant — offset in x and z but not
   brought to a common y — so from `superior` the four sections sat one behind another. Walk, 2.25%.
9. **A second structure pointing at one model part measures 0% in the player.** `tube_ghost` was an
   attempt to have one wall opaque in one beat and translucent in another; viz3d maps one mesh to one
   structure, so the second one gets nothing. One opacity per part.
10. **The anencephaly lesion was craniorachischisis.** `openCranial` set the cranial zip SPEED to zero, so
    nothing cranial of the fifth somite ever closed — half the embryo open from the neck up. Every check
    passed. **It was found by looking at the frame**, which is check 4 and the only check in the list a
    file cannot run. A neuropore FAILING means the front travels and does not finish, so it now stops at
    V_SEG_CRANIAL and what stays open is the unsegmented head.

### A finding about render-kit, measured and worked around here rather than fixed there

`VizKit.sweptShell` decides ONE winding order per QUAD through `E.quad()`. Where a quad spans a
fast-turning feature its two triangles want OPPOSITE orders and no single choice satisfies both.
`models3d/notochord.js` records exactly this for its own sheets and solves it in the MODEL; the kit still
has the per-quad version, so **every `tubeAlong` and `tubeCapped` in the corpus inherits it.** Measured
here: the neural canal built with `tubeCapped` came back with **19 of its 1,872 triangles (1.015%) wound
against their own supplied normals**, in two clusters at the two rows nearest the closure fronts. On a
DoubleSide material with supplied normals nothing looks wrong — RENDER-STANDARD 2.1 describing itself.
This model sweeps its own round tubes and path tubes through its own `patch()`, whose order is measured
per triangle, and reports 1.00000 on every key at every sampled stage and variant (3,753,648 triangles,
4,641 closed bodies, zero negative volumes, zero unpaired edges). **The kit is still unfixed and a
reviewer may reasonably call that the finding rather than this work-around.** Repro: one `tubeCapped` call
on a centreline that turns sharply.

### A disagreement with the sibling model, load-bearing here

`models3d/notochord.js` carries `SOMITE_PERIOD_H = 4.5`. Every text teaches THREE PAIRS PER DAY, which is
8.0. At 4.5 h there are 37 pairs by day 27; at 8.0 there are 21, and 24 by day 28, which reproduces the
taught "about 25 by the end of week 4". **This model uses 8.0** because BOTH the closure site and the
caudal neuropore are read off the somite table here, so the figure moves the anatomy rather than
decorating it. notochord.js was NOT edited — it is a separate queue item and was in review when this was
built. Harness check 11 asserts the nine shared dimensions agree EXACTLY and that this one disagrees, so
neither a drift nor a stale note can hide.

### Three visibility waivers, and a measurement rather than an assertion

Beats 4 and 9 point at a cast that lies INSIDE a wall drawn see-through so it can be seen. The visibility
walk's beauty pass sets `transparent` and `opacity` and leaves `depthWrite` at three's default of TRUE;
viz3d.js's procedural adapter sets `depthWrite = opacity >= 0.98`, and render-kit's `tissueMaterial`
carries the same rule at the same threshold. A cast inside a translucent wall is therefore depth-rejected
in the walk's frame and blended in the player's. **Harness check 12 measures it** rather than asserting
it: the same frame, same composition, only depthWrite differing — `beat4/neural_canal` reads **0.000%
(peak 39/255) under the walk's rule and 0.742% (peak 204) under viz3d's**; beat9/neural_canal 0.006% vs
0.700%. The walk's own second measure, visible_pct, reads all three above the floor (1.315%, 0.405%,
1.250%). The proper fix is a median-section variant, which is declared in gaps[] as a round of work and
not done.

**The first version of check 12 FAILED its own assertion** — it reported the cast at 0.73% under both
rules — because it set `transparent` from the opacity, which moves an opaque structure into the opaque
render pass where it can never be depth-rejected. That failure is how the real cause was found, and the
comment in the file says to keep both lines as they are.

### What was proved, and what was assumed

**Proved.** 23 acceptance rows, each with a named magnitude floor and a negative case that it rejects
(23/23). Three perturbations, with the "must not move" side carrying its own tolerance and its own reason
rather than a bare zero — two of them are legitimately nonzero and the file says why (SH_NEURAL moves the
closure date by one minute, because fusion is contact within SEAM and the calibre enters at order SEAM/L;
the somite clock moves the measured area by 4e-5, which is the four-column polygon on each tip round).
Winding 1.00000 over 3.75M triangles across 6 variants x 6 stages; 4,641 closed bodies all positive;
zero unpaired edges; six-camera ray cast 0 first hits facing away; mirror symmetry exact (0 unmatched
vertices). 36 beat claims hold and every beat is pinned to its own instant. 9 beats x their own shown
lists resolved through viz3d's REAL adapter, 0 unresolved. The visibility walk passes all 9 beats with no
framing failure. The fragment count was run on the player frame at 40/255 and every multi-component
result is answered below.

**Assumed, or declared rather than proved.** The axes are DECLARED and not proved — row P measures that
every key is mirror-symmetric in x and no narration names a side, which is what stands in for a proof
this model cannot give. The embryo is a flat plan and does not fold. The dorsal body wall does not close
in around the tube. Cranial fold elevation does not lead, because every station folds on the same
schedule relative to the front. The amnion is not drawn. The four lumbosacral panels carry one meningeal
wall, not dura and arachnoid, no nerve roots and no Chiari II. All of it is in gaps[].

### Fragment counts (RENDER-STANDARD 3.ab), player frame, 40/255

Six structure-beats have more than one component, and every one is answered: `somites` in beat 3 is TWO
(left and right — they are paired, and no narration calls them continuous); `sec_crest` in beat 5 is TEN
(a cell POPULATION, which is what the narration calls it); `sb_sac`, `sb_arch` and `sb_cord` in beat 7 are
six, five and three (FOUR PANELS, by construction); `neural_tube` in beat 8 is 2 after the discount with
the largest piece holding 99.8%. The structures a narration DOES call continuous — the tube, the canal,
the notochord — are 1 after the hairline discount wherever they are measurable. Beats 4's two casts read
0 components for the depthWrite reason above and are covered by the same waivers.

### Addendum, 04:08Z — I CLOBBERED THE QUEUE FOR SEVENTY SECONDS, AND THE COMPARE-AND-SWAP DID NOT STOP ME

Writing this up because it is a hole in the shape section 0 of BUILD-TASK-PROMPT describes, and the next
run will walk into it the same way.

**What happened.** I staged BUILD-QUEUE.json fresh (1,127,555 bytes, carrying another run's `implantation`
= built and `bilaminar-embryonic-disc` = building), ran `queue-set.mjs` on it, copied the result over
`/mnt/user-data/outputs/BUILD-QUEUE.json` — **a path that already held my own 01:26 snapshot from the
claim commit** — and committed it with the correct `expectedMtimeMs`. The guard passed, the write
succeeded, and the file that landed on Frank's machine was **the 01:26 snapshot, not the file I had just
written there**. The read-back caught it: 111 todo where I expected 110, 19 escalated where I expected
20, my own item still `building` with no notes, and the other run's two entries GONE.

**Why the guard did not help.** `expectedMtimeMs` compares the DEVICE's file against what I staged. It
says nothing about whether the bytes I am sending are the bytes I meant to send. Mine were stale on MY
side, not on the device's, and that is a failure mode the compare-and-swap is not built to see.

**The mechanism, as far as I can tell.** The overwrite of an existing path under
`/mnt/user-data/outputs/` had not propagated by the time the commit read it, even though a local read of
that same path a second earlier returned the NEW content (the item counts printed correctly). A fresh
filename committed cleanly on the first try.

**Recovered** by committing the correct file under a new name with the device's then-current mtime as the
guard. Verified by re-staging: 138 items, `neurulation` built with its notes, `implantation` built,
`bilaminar-embryonic-disc` building, escalated back to 20, and the sha256 of the device's copy equal to
the sha256 of what I sent. The window was 04:06:53Z to 04:08:00Z. **If another run read the queue in that
window it saw a queue with two of its own entries missing**, which is worth knowing when reading the
other logs from this hour.

**The rule that would have prevented it**, now added to BUILD-TASK-PROMPT section 0: commit each file
from a path under `/mnt/user-data/outputs/` that this run has not written before, and re-read it from
THAT path immediately before the commit. Never reuse an output path within a run. The read-back after the
commit is what caught this one and it is why that rule exists — but a read-back tells you AFTER you have
already overwritten someone else's work, and on the queue that is a race another run can lose.

### Four defects the probes found in my own work

1. **The cardinal bug, written again.** Every quad `revolve()` emitted was wound against its own supplied
   normal — winding 0.025–0.14, signed volumes NEGATIVE, 99–100% backface-first from every camera. The
   vertex normals were correct; `emitter().quad()`'s fixed order produces the exact negative of them for
   this parametrisation. **Nothing looked wrong**, because the materials are DoubleSide and the shading
   follows the supplied normals — which is RENDER-STANDARD 2.1's description of itself, arriving in a new
   file. The call site now decides `quad` vs `quadFlip` from the geometry per quad and never reasons
   about it, which is 2.4b's corollary applied.
2. **My own battery could not have caught it**, because every volume measurement went through
   `Math.abs()`. An inward-wound model produced identical numbers to a correct one and two rows passed on
   it. Row **O** now asserts signed volumes are positive.
3. **A solve that converged beautifully against a false constraint.** The mesoderm sheet thickness was
   solved by bisection against conservation of tissue across the split; it converged to a residual of
   9e-10 and gave a splanchnic sheet 130 µm thick on a yolk sac 105 µm in radius, which swallowed the
   embryo — row P measured **67.5% of the amniotic cavity inside it**. Loose extraembryonic mesoderm is
   mostly extracellular space and the chorionic cavity forms by those spaces becoming confluent, so there
   is no solid volume to conserve. A residual of 1e-9 against a false constraint is a precisely wrong
   answer. What is solved instead is `rEmb`, the envelope the mesoderm must clear, measured on the built
   embryo complex.
4. **Eleven structures shown at a t where the model does not build them**, across five beats — which the
   player shows a student as "there is no model of this structure". Each now has an explicit `HIDE`.

### Three of my own acceptance rows were wrong as written

- **Row C** normalised a which-side claim by the extent of the cavity making it, so it FELL as the
  relation became more obvious (1.64 on day 8, 0.31 on day 14). Split into a centroid row and an edge row.
- **Row N** reported a mirror residual of 0.0606 on a model that is mirror-symmetric by construction,
  because it subsampled the query *and* the haystack. Hashing all vertices and querying a subsample gives
  **1.8e-16**.
- **Row P** compared BOUNDING BOXES and reported 37 shared-space pairs on a model with none — a spherical
  shell's box is the whole sphere's, so a box test on nested shells measures nesting, not containment. It
  now ray-casts, and classifies surface-coincident points as contact, reporting that degeneracy.
- **Row H1 was deleted as an asserted row** and published as a diagnostic: `rEmb` is *defined* as 1.04 ×
  the quantity H1 checked, so the row could not fail. A test that cannot fail is not evidence.

### Composition: what the visibility walk found that nothing else could

`ISOLATE_REGION` **does not isolate** on a scene like this. The spec defines it as "show only this; GHOST
everything else", and a ghost still draws — here the ghosts are a cytotrophoblast and a
syncytiotrophoblast the size of the whole conceptus **with the camera inside them**. Beat 1 measured the
syncytiotrophoblast at 83.6% of the frame and the epiblast at 0% on the id-pick. Every beat was rewritten
to the explicit `HIDE_STRUCTURE '*'` → `SHOW_STRUCTURE` pattern the cardiac-looping scene uses.

`CROSS_SECTION` does not help either: the player cuts **sheets**, not closed solids, so adding it changed
the measured frame by *zero* — the syncytiotrophoblast held 32.475% before and after, to four decimals. A
no-op was removed rather than left in the scene looking like a section. The section those beats need is in
the GEOMETRY and is now there: the shells are built as **caudal half-shells with capped cut faces**. The
cut is caudal and not lateral on purpose — θ → π−θ is the mirror in x and maps [π, 2π] onto itself, so a
caudal cut keeps the model mirror-symmetric in x and row N keeps meaning what it says. A left-right cut
would have given this model a handedness with no anatomical basis.

Two colours were changed because the measurement said they were the same colour: the amniotic cavity sat
under a blue amnion and the yolk sac under a yellow Heuser's membrane, and removing the cavity moved the
pixels by a peak of 9/255 against a 40 floor — not because it was hidden, but because taking it away left
almost the same colour behind.

A sawtooth down the right edge of beat 1's amniotic dome was chased through the diagnostic ladder: it
survived a taper fix and a silhouette fix (both aimed at the wrong cause), and step 2 — turn the suspect
off — identified the amnion in one frame. Finer tessellation (16→36 rows, 40→72 around) removed it.

### What is NOT done, and it matters

**`index.json` was NOT rebuilt.** It still lists this scene as `mode: sequence`, `provider: svg`,
`status: planned`, so **the player will not route it to viz3d until the index is regenerated on a full
checkout**. I worked from a container copy holding only this scene and cardiac-looping, and
`build-scene-index.mjs` rewrites the whole file — running it here would have destroyed the entries for the
other 145 scenes. Another build run rewrote `index.json` at 04:05Z while this run was working, so there
was a live writer besides me. `COVERAGE.md` likewise not rerun, same reason. `validate-scenes` therefore
says nothing about corpus-wide regressions.

### Weakest picture, flagged for the reviewer

**Beat 5, the chorion's three layers.** It passes the walk and is still hard to read — three faint
concentric rings around a translucent bowl, where a student is asked to count somatic mesoderm,
cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast in order. I raised their opacity to 0.72 on reasoning that proved
false (a bowl's concave inner surface faces the camera, so the cytotrophoblast became an opaque disc
hiding everything inside — and the walk passed *that* frame too) and reverted it. The fix is a narrower
cut, a caudal wedge rather than a caudal half; this run did not make it.

### Assumed, not proved

Every anatomical figure — columnar 25 µm, cuboidal 10 µm, disc 0.1 mm → 0.2 mm, conceptus 0.18 → 0.9 mm,
and all the day numbers — is a standard teaching value typed in from general knowledge. **No source was
consulted and none is cited; check the numbers before the geometry.** Every cavity and shell is a solid of
revolution: the real cavities are not round and the embryo hangs ECCENTRICALLY in the chorionic cavity,
not concentrically. The topology each beat teaches is right; the spacing is a simplification.

### Two things a future run should know

**C2PA chunks on committed PNGs.** Every PNG committed through `device_commit_files` comes back from
`device_stage_files` exactly **5,770 bytes larger**, with a `caBX`/`jumb` content-credentials chunk
inserted after IHDR. IHDR and every IDAT are byte-identical — the pixels are untouched. **Compare PNGs by
their IDAT payload, not by whole-file hash**, or a read-back will report a false failure, as mine did.

**I HIT THE REUSED-OUTPUT-PATH BUG recorded in the 04:08Z entry above, and I clobbered an item with it.**
My first queue commit was refused by the mtime guard (correct — another run had written). I re-staged,
re-applied, wrote to **the same** `/mnt/user-data/outputs/viz-training/BUILD-QUEUE.json`, and committed —
and the commit sent the **stale first version**. The queue on disk afterwards carried my item correctly
but had `implantation` pushed back from `in-review` to `built`, destroying the review run's claim fields.
I restored it to `in-review` with a `restore_note` explaining what happened, committed from a fresh
timestamped output path, and verified the result byte-identical on disk. The review run that owns that
item will have one write refused and should re-apply, which is the designed behaviour.

**Why I hit a rule that was already written:** the 04:08Z run added it to `BUILD-TASK-PROMPT.md` section
0, and I staged my copy of that file at **03:06Z**, an hour earlier. I followed the version I had. A run
that stages the method once at the start and works for ninety minutes is reading a snapshot, and on a
chain where three tasks edit the method file this is not a rare case. **Worth considering: re-stage
`BUILD-TASK-PROMPT.md` immediately before the first commit, not only at the start of the run.**

## 2026-10-03 · embryology__weeks-1-2-implantation-bilaminar-disc__amniotic-cavity-yolk-sac — BUILT

Claimed 04:08:35Z, built 05:5x Z, by the model3d BUILD task. `kind: model3d`, `shape: structure`,
note "RE-AUTHORING, NOT WIRING ... two cavities".

**What this run took, and the one judgement it had to make before it could take anything.**
`queue-set.mjs --next` said to reclaim `neurulation-neural-plate-tube` as a STALE CLAIM — claimed
01:26:24Z, 2.7 hours old, over the two-hour line. The repository said otherwise. Its render harness
had been written at 04:05:08Z, `COVERAGE.md` at 04:05:12 and `BUILD-LOG.md` at 04:05:15 — one
hundred seconds before this run fired — and the log's last entry was a complete build write-up for
that very item, ending in a read-back. That run was not dead; it was finishing. It set the item to
`built` at 04:06:48, one minute after this run started. Reclaiming it would have put two runs on one
item and overwritten a finished build with a half-done one.

So: the staleness rule is a CLOCK HEURISTIC and the filesystem is EVIDENCE, and section 6 of the
task prompt is explicit about which wins — "a note in a file is a claim, not a fact ... if this
file's account of something and what you find in the repo disagree, that disagreement is the
finding". **Proposed for BUILD-TASK-PROMPT section 1: before reclaiming a stale claim, look at the
mtimes of `BUILD-LOG.md` and `models3d/`. A run that has written inside the last ten minutes is
alive whatever its claim says.** Two hours is the right order of magnitude for a run that died; it
is also, on this corpus, a perfectly ordinary length for a run that is working.

Back-pressure at the claim: `built` x1, under the limit of three. Taken instead: the first `todo`
item, `amniotic-cavity-yolk-sac`, with `bilaminar-embryonic-disc` left alone at 59 minutes old.

### What was built

`models3d/amniotic-cavity-yolk-sac.js` (152,768 bytes), the two early cavities and their fates from
day 8 to day 80 post-fertilisation as one continuous function of t. 22 part keys, of which 5 are
median-section variants and 5 transverse-section variants. The scene was re-authored from the SVG
panel version: all fifteen of its `structures[]` were teaching beats with no geometry.

**THE NARRATION WAS COPIED, NOT RETYPED.** The scene was generated by a script that reads each
paragraph out of the old file by key. The pre-conversion file is kept at
`viz-training/_amniotic-cavity-yolk-sac-preconversion.json` and the harness re-asserts, every run,
that all 25 of its narrations appear in the new scene byte for byte. 25 of 25.

### What is SOLVED, and the one number a student is marked wrong for

The examinable number in this topic is WHEN THE AMNION FINISHES SWALLOWING THE CHORIONIC CAVITY.
The amniotic cavity's radius as a fraction of the sac's is a two-parameter law whose exponent and
whose endpoint are fitted by least squares to three published ultrasound ratios (post-fertilisation
days 42, 56, 70). The narration's "somewhere between weeks eight and twelve" is NOT an input.

    fitted p = 1.3963, obliteration day 83.81 = post-fertilisation week 11.97, rms 0.00219

A fourth published ratio, at day 35, was HELD OUT of the fit so that something in the model is an
out-of-sample prediction rather than a residual: predicted 0.3257 against a published 0.3478, 6.4%.
And the same claim is then measured on the BUILT GRID rather than on the law — row F bisects the
built coelom's volume for the day it falls past a half and gets day 69.8, week 9.98, inside the same
window from a different direction.

Second solve: the exocoelomic cyst burden, by volume conservation integrated over the triangulated
spheres the file actually draws (residual 1e-10). Row H says in its own text that the share is
CALIBRATED and the resulting diameter is therefore a consistency check and not a prediction.

Third solve: where the conceptus sits relative to the disc, as a clamp into the interval in which
the amnion fits inside the chorionic cavity. The first version declared it as a fraction of the
radius and the amniotic cavity grew out THROUGH the chorion between days 16 and 21 — reported not by
a render but by the coelom's clearance test going negative and the part building nothing.

**AND ONE SOLVE WAS AVAILABLE AND REFUSED.** A catenoid neck between the gut and the yolk sac pinches
off past 0.6628 of its end radius, which would have made the vitelline duct's closure day a
prediction. On this model's dimensions it fires at about day 28 against the narrated weeks six to
ten, and moves anywhere you like for a 20% change in a declared end radius. That is a tuned constant
wearing a derivation. The duct narrows on a declared law, the rows assert the hourglass and the
narrowing rather than the day, and the scene's `gaps[]` says so.

### What was PROVED

- **Watertight** 0 unpaired edges over the same 722,528 triangles. Every edge shared by exactly two

- **Enclosed volume** worst 25.1 facet quanta (floor 10); no part inside out at any t.
- **Ray cast** 0 of 6,512 first hits facing away, five cameras x 225 rays x 19 t.
- **Console** clean; 4 swiftshader perf messages excluded by exact pattern and counted.
- **Adapter, per beat** 72 refs resolved with geometry through viz3d's real procedural adapter, at
  the t of every beat that shows them. 0 failed.
- **Adapter, at the mount** 36 resolutions — every unpinned ref at t = 1, every pinned ref at its own
  pin. 0 failed.
- **Acceptance** 22 rows, all pass; 23 negative cases, all rejected.
- **Beat claims** 51 claims over 11 beats, 0 failures, 0 beats unpinned from their own instant, 0
  structures drawn at a t their beat is not at.
- **Visibility walk** 11 of 11 beats pass, with two declared waivers (below).
- **Perturbation** the tessellation moved from 26x44 to 34x60 and the solved cyst radius moved

- **Clock** the scene's 11 SET_STAGE values and the model's own `tOfDay()` agree to 1e-9. Two copies
  of a table drift; this one is checked.
- **Verbatim** 25 of 25.

### THE DEFECT THE VISIBILITY WALK FOUND, WHICH NOTHING ELSE COULD, AND WHICH IS NOT THIS SCENE'S ALONE

Six of eleven beats came back **"subject covers 0% of frame"** — nothing drawn at all from t = 0.48
onward — while the geometry was watertight, the winding was 1.000000, the whole battery was green and
all 48 beat claims held. **viz3d.js builds its camera once, `new T.PerspectiveCamera(45, 1, 0.01,
4000)`, and never updates near or far.** This model is true scale in units of 10 um over ten weeks,
so its sac runs 0.33 mm to 64 mm across — 5,697 world units at the last beat, which puts the framing
camera about 7,200 units out and the whole model behind the far plane. The corpus convention of 10 um
per unit was set by models that span one week; it does not survive a 190-fold range.

Fixed here by scaling the GROUP and not the geometry: vertices stay in true units (so every solve,
row and claim is unchanged — `keyStats()` does not apply matrixWorld, deliberately), and
`group.scale` hands the player about 120 world units at every t. Acceptance row T asserts the framing
distance against viz3d's own field of view and far plane: worst 319 units of 4,000.

**This cannot be the only model it bites.** A procedural model's drawn extent is part of its contract
with the player and nothing in RENDER-STANDARD says so. **Proposed as a new RENDER-STANDARD rule: a
model declares its drawn world extent and a row asserts the player's own framing distance stays
inside viz3d's frustum at every t.** Any existing model whose world extent exceeds about 1,500 units
at any stage is invisible in the player today and passes every check in the corpus.

### FOUR MORE DEFECTS, EVERY ONE FOUND BY OPENING A FRAME

Check 4 is the only check in the list a file cannot run, and on this item it was not a formality.

1. **The transverse section rendered in white and grey.** `addPart` stripped `/_cut$/` for the
   palette lookup, which does not match `_cutz`, so every transverse variant fell back to the neutral
   0xcccccc: a yolk sac that is not yellow and a gut that is not ochre. The visibility walk counts

2. **A cyst sat on top of the day-13 embryo.** The cysts were placed on a ring at the conceptus's

3. **The connecting stalk was a 9 um thread on day 13 and a 7.4 mm rope at day 70.** A flat fraction

4. **The amniotic sheath was narrower than the stalk it sleeves** — 17.4 units round a stalk of 20.4,

### TWO EMITTER FAULTS, FOUND BY THE WATERTIGHTNESS CHECK AND BY NOTHING ELSE

Both passed winding, volume sign and the ray cast.

1. **A fan from a centroid folds back on a non-convex face.** The vitelline duct's meridional face is
   bounded by an hourglass profile; a fan from its centroid produced triangles of both orientations,
   `triS` then "corrected" each one to the face's normal, and the cancellation that would have made
   the signed area right was destroyed — 32 unpaired edges and a cut face drawn partly outside its
   own outline. **The enclosed volume could not notice**: a face in the plane x = 0 contributes
   r.n = 0 to the divergence integral whichever way it faces. Replaced with an exact strip between
   the profile and the axis, where the axis point is the midpoint of the two antipodal profile
   points — exact because every section window here is exactly pi wide.
2. **A degenerate hint at a pole silently dropped triangles.** The meridional face's orientation hint
   was recomputed per station; at a pole every th gives the same point, the hint was the zero vector,
   `triS`'s own guard returned early, and each sectioned shell lost the two triangles at its pole.
   6 unpaired edges per shell. A planar face has one normal and now takes one hint.

### A FINDING ABOUT THE KIT, MEASURED HERE AND NOT RE-FILED

`VizKit.emitter().quad()` decides ONE winding order per quad through the raw `tri`, and where a
surface turns fast inside a cell the two triangles want opposite orders. This file emits every
triangle through a local `triS` that measures the face normal of EACH triangle against the vertex
normals supplied with THAT triangle, keeping smooth per-vertex normals (which `K.triN` cannot — it
writes one normal to all three corners and would facet every surface here). Result: 1.000000 on every
key at every sampled t. **The kit is still unfixed**; the neurulation run measured the same thing in
`tubeCapped` on 2026-10-03 and `models3d/notochord.js` records it for its own sheets. Not re-filed —
noted as a third independent confirmation.

### A HARNESS FAULT THIS RUN WROTE AND ITS OWN FLOOR CAUGHT

The facet-quanta measure was taken about the WORLD ORIGIN rather than each part's own centre. A
triangle's signed volume about a point scales with distance from it, so a part far from the origin
has enormous |v| and a sum that is only its own volume: the yolk sac remnant, 1,100 units out along
the cord, reported 7.6 quanta against a floor of 10 with winding 1.000000, zero unpaired edges and a
positive volume. `implantation.js`'s harness subtracts the bounding box centre for exactly this
reason. Worth recording because the symptom reads as a model defect and is not one.

### The two visibility waivers, and the one opacity that was tried and rejected

- **beat 9, `__clipped__`** — 1,263 subject pixels of 990,000 on a border row. viz3d frames on the
  eight corners of the subject box with FRAME_PAD 1.05, and this beat's box projects to exactly
  +/-0.952; the subject is also deep along the camera axis, and under perspective a surface nearer
  than the box's far face projects outside the corners that were framed. No structure is lost. The
  honest fix is a smaller pad in viz3d for deep subjects, which is a player change.
- **beat 10, `epiblast`** — the epiblast and the hypoblast are the two halves of ONE lens seen through
  the amniotic cavity: the hypoblast moves its pixels by 156 of 255 and passes, the epiblast by 32
  and fails the 40/255 floor, and the difference is which half catches the key light. The embryo is
  plainly visible in `beat10.png`.
- **The obvious fix made it worse, and it was measured rather than guessed.** Dropping the amniotic
  cavity's opacity from 0.25 to 0.18 to lift the epiblast put the CAVITY ITSELF under the floor in
  beats 4, 5 and 10 — one failure traded for three. RENDER-STANDARD 3.ab corollary 1, exactly.

### What was ASSUMED, or declared rather than proved

- **The axes are DECLARED and not proved.** Row P measures that every key is mirror-symmetric in x
  (0 unmatched of 4,244 sampled vertices), which is the honest form of the statement: there is no
  chiral landmark in this model, a mirror would be indistinguishable, and nothing this scene narrates
  names a side. Three keys had to be re-placed in mirrored pairs to make that true rather than nearly
  true — a model that is ALMOST symmetric can witness nothing.
- The embryo is a lens that thickens, not a C-shaped body that folds. `cranio-caudal-folding.js` and
  `lateral-folding.js` own folding. The drawn extent from day 24 carries a declared curl factor of
  0.60 because a straight lens at half the crown-rump length did not fit inside its own amnion.
- No germ layers beyond the two; no mesoderm, notochord, neural tube or somites.
- The coelom's inner boundary is the closed envelope of the amniotic dome, not the dome: understates
  the coelom by 0.4% at day 28 and by nothing at the days rows E2 and F measure.
- Membrane and epithelial thicknesses are fractions of the radius they sit on. The two epithelia ARE
  at true thickness through week two.
- The germ cells' migration route is a direction, not an anatomy.

### THE THING A REVIEWER SHOULD LOOK AT FIRST

**The yolk sac is drawn straight below the embryo and not carried into the cord.** From about week
six a real yolk sac lies BESIDE the cord with its duct running inside it. This model keeps it on the
ventral axis, and its position is then forced by two constraints that are each correct — outside the
amnion, inside the chorion — so at day 56 it hangs 14 mm straight down on an 11 mm duct. Beat 9
passes every structure's floor and carries the clipping waiver above, and it is still the weakest
frame in the scene. Fixing it means giving the sac a DIRECTION rather than a height, which moves the
duct off the y axis and out of the surface-of-revolution primitive that lets it be sectioned in beat
7. That is a round of work and it was not done. It is in `gaps[]` in those words.

  fit.** The difference is that `F0` stopped being a declared 0.30 and became a measurement of the

with a different cause for the turn. Two models have now worked around it locally. It is a kit fault
and the workaround cost this run three attempts; it belongs in the queue as an engine item.

### My own three checks, written before I opened BUILD-LOG.md or `built_notes`

From the curriculum entry and the scene shell alone: (1) neural crest origin, delamination and
dorsolateral destination, plus surface-ectoderm disjunction and re-fusion; (2) bidirectional zip and
the three dates, with the tube open at BOTH ends mid-way; (3) the notochord as one continuous rod
under one continuous lumen. Then I read the builder's notes as a checklist against that list. **The
defect was in (3), and it is in a place the builder's notes do not mention at all** — which is
section 2's whole argument for writing your order down first.

### What I found and FIXED

**The `sections` variant drew THREE notochords under FOUR panels.** Each stage exists in up to two
runs of the axis, one cranial to the closure site and one caudal; `sectionStations()` always took the
cranial one. The notochord ends at the prechordal plate, `V_PRE = 0.862`. At beat 1's t the groove's
cranial station is **v = 0.95997** and at beat 5's the folds' is **0.91375**, both past the end of the
rod, so `addNotochord`'s `clipV` returned null and that panel was drawn with nothing beneath it.

A **different** panel lost its rod at each t — the groove in beat 1, the folds in beat 5 — which is
why neither frame looked systematically broken, and why I nearly wrote it off as occlusion.

Measured three ways before I touched anything: `vertsByKey(t, {sections:true})` returned **3**
notochord bodies against 4 panels at both beats; the rendered frames carried **0** notochord pixels in
the empty quadrant (2,865 across three quadrants in beat 1, none in the fourth); and the four panel
boxes showed no rod within any of them.

**Why it is a teaching defect and not just a cosmetic one.** `sec_notochord`'s own narration says
*"Beneath the midline in ALL FOUR SECTIONS, which is the point: keep the notochord in every picture
even when you are drawing the surface, because it is the reason the surface is doing anything."* The
picture showed three. And beat 2, the very next beat, teaches that the notochord is what induced the
plate — after beat 1 has shown the student a neural groove with no inducer under it. That is the
`learning_goal`'s own four-section figure contradicting the beat that follows it.

**The fix:** among a stage's runs, prefer one whose centre lies within the notochord's own span, and
fall back to the cranial-most only when none does. That is also the truer section — the four-panel
figure every text draws is a **trunk** section, not a forebrain one.

**New acceptance row X and its negative case**, so it cannot come back: sweeps day 19→28, requires
every `sections` panel to carry a notochord body, and requires the sweep to have REACHED a four-panel
day so it cannot pass vacuously. Measured **48 panels over 19 days, 48 with a rod, 4 four-panel days**.
I verified the row **FAILS on the pre-fix behaviour** and passes after it — a check that cannot fail
is theatre, and I ran that experiment rather than assuming.

### What I re-ran, in my own container, against the committed file

Full 12-check harness **ALL CHECKS PASS**; **24** acceptance rows; **24** negative cases; the 3
perturbations; and **all 36 beat claims re-measured** through `claimMeasure` at each beat's own t —
every one identical to its pinned value, so **the fix moved no scene number**. Only
`beat01-superior.png` and `beat05-superior.png` changed, and I looked at both: four panels, four
rods, ectoderm continuous over the closed tube. I also reproduced the builder's entire battery
BEFORE changing anything, so the baseline is mine and not a note I was handed.
