### My three checks, written before reading the build notes

Dorsoventral polarity; the two monotone size laws; the t-to-day mapping beat by beat. All three pass —
polarity measured independently at t=0.05/0.17/0.24/0.93 (amniotic cavity y>0, both yolk sacs y<0,
epiblast above hypoblast, the disc straddling y=0 with the EQ_PAD overlap). The thing the build notes
do **not** mention anywhere is RENDER-STANDARD 3.ab, the fragment rule, added the previous day and
with a tool of its own. That is where I started, and it is where the run went.

### THE BIG ONE, AND IT IS NOT IN THIS MODEL: measure-scene-visibility.mjs was grading a picture the player never draws

Every large shell in this scene — amnion, amniotic cavity, chorionic cavity, extraembryonic mesoderm,
chorion — carried a band of sawtooth wedges along its limb, in every beat that showed it. Worked down
RENDER-STANDARD section 4 in order, and the ladder earned its place: the artefact survived **finer
tessellation** (26x44 -> 36x72, which is what fixed a sawtooth on the previous item, so it was the
obvious answer and it was wrong), **silhouettes off**, **the removal of every other structure one at a
time**, and a **1000x sweep of the camera near plane** (0.01 -> 10, i.e. depth precision, which section
4 says to reach for last and which was again not it). The geometry was immaculate throughout: 1146
directions each with exactly two radii, constant wall thickness to 1e-4, every outer normal outward and
every inner normal inward, 0 unpaired edges, no azimuthal seam.

The cause was one missing clause in the TOOL. `_walk.html` sets `transparent` and `opacity` on every
structure and stops. viz3d.js does not: it sets `depthWrite: op >= 0.98` where it builds the material
(viz3d.js:610) and again in paint() (viz3d.js:2419), and render-kit `tissueMaterial` carries the same
rule with a comment recording why it was added. With depthWrite left at three's default `true`, a
DoubleSide translucent shell occludes ITSELF — the far half of its own surface writes depth before the
near half is drawn, and the near half is rejected in one wedge per azimuthal segment. Adding the clause
removes it completely.

**It had already manufactured a false defect on this very item.** Beat 8 `connecting_stalk` measured 2
connected components with the largest holding 84.5% of its ink — a textbook 3.ab finding, a continuous
stalk drawn in pieces. On the corrected frame it is **1 component at 99.4%**. Beat 11 `cord_sheath` went
99.3% -> 100.0%, beat 10 `cord_sheath` 35 -> 18 fragments. Every ink figure, every alpha peak that
decides the 40/255 floor, and every fragment count 3.ab reads off this page was affected, corpus-wide,
on every scene with a translucent structure. Fixed in `viz-training/tools/measure-scene-visibility.mjs`,
with the account in a comment at the line. This is the fourth instance of "the proof frames prove the
wrong picture" and the first where the wrong picture was the PLAYER walk itself — the file whose own
header says it reimplements viz3d's ops rather than driving viz3d, and that where the two disagree
viz3d is right.

All three findings below were then re-measured on the corrected frames, and all three survive it.

### The three open findings

1. **`amniotic_cavity` clears the visibility floor by one unit.** Peak 41/255 on beat 10 and 44 on beat
   5 against a floor of 40. Not geometry: `amn_cav` #5dade2 and `amnion` #85c1e9 differ by at most
   40/255 in any channel before lighting and opacity, so removing the cavity leaves nearly the same
   colour behind. Rebuilt at 36x72 — anatomically neutral — beat 10 falls to peak 33 and the walk FAILS
   outright with NOT SEEABLE ON EITHER MEASURE. The build run diagnosed and fixed this exact thing by
   recolouring on the preceding item the same morning; the palette comment says these blues were carried
   over from the SVG era and the hazard was not re-checked against them. Not fixed here: the right fix is
   a colour, the log already records that the obvious opacity fix traded one failure for three, and
   picking a new blue needs a full walk to verify it does not do the same.
2. **Beat 10, 3.ab: `chorionic_cavity` draws in 34 connected components**, largest holding 57.3% of its
   ink, 2.06% of frame, player frame at 40/255, unchanged by the depthWrite fix. It is the beat's own
   highlighted subject at intensity 0.95, and the beat exists to show that one continuous space closing.
3. **Beat 5 narrates a five-week scan at day 16, where this model's own sac is 1.5 mm.** Five weeks
   menstrual is day 21 post-fertilisation and a real five-week gestational sac is about 5 mm mean
   diameter. Day 21 is a day this model already builds, at exactly 5.0 mm (beat 6's B6-pin). The beat's
   day claim was written as "the beat sits in week three" rather than against the five weeks the
   narration says, so nothing could catch it — and this file's own header calls the two-week offset the
   single easiest way to be wrong by a lot in this topic. Same family, lower stakes: beat 3's B3-size
   calls 268 um "the few hundred microns an early scan sees", where a sonographic yolk sac is 3-5 mm.

### A standards gap, and the rule proposed for it

3.ac this run.

## 2026-10-03 08:05Z — `embryology__weeks-1-2-implantation-bilaminar-disc__bilaminar-embryonic-disc`, rework of review round 1

`changes-requested` → `built`. One item. Findings 1–4 answered; 5 and 6 were already closed by the
review and needed nothing.

**I did not take what `--next` told me to take, and that is the most important line here.**
`queue-set.mjs --next` offered `…__amniotic-cavity-yolk-sac` as a **"STALE CLAIM — 4 hours"** with
`reclaim_to: built`. It is not stale. It is `in-review`, its `updated_at` was 07:37:25Z — twenty-eight
minutes before this run fired — and `BUILD-QUEUE.json`'s own mtime was 07:37:25.511Z, the *same write*.
The 07:35 review run had just claimed it and was alive. `staleClaim()` ages an item by
`Date.parse(i.claimed_at || i.updated_at)`, and a review that sets `in-review` does **not** update
`claimed_at` — so it measured the *build's* 04:08:35Z claim and called a live review four hours dead.
Following it would have reset a running review's item back to `built`.

This is the same bug this file's own 2026-09-29 note documents on `cardiac-cycle-pumping` — "a review
then claimed it, and died WITHOUT updating claimed_at". That fix corrected `reclaimTo()`, which
decides *which status to restore*, and left `staleClaim()`, which decides *whether it is stale at all*,
untouched one function upstream. **Suggested fix: age an item by the most recent of `claimed_at` and
`updated_at`.** I did not make it — a build run editing the tool that schedules build runs should be a
reviewed change, not a side effect of a rework. I took the `changes-requested` item instead, which is
what §1 and the queue's own `order` field both say.

**§6 in action, twice more.** The disagreement *is* the finding, so both are written down rather than
smoothed over.

**(1) One of the review's own numbers did not reproduce.** Finding 3's id-pick measurements reproduced
exactly — `amniotic_cavity` 0.036% against the amnion's 11.679% — and are what the fix addresses. Its
*highlight* figure did not: "applying beat 10's own HIGHLIGHT_STRUCTURE … changes 45 pixels (0.021%)".
Composed the way viz3d composes a beat — per-structure opacity applied and `depthWrite` set from it,
`viz3d.js:2416-2417` — the same highlight on the **same unfixed model** moved **68,414 pixels (29.97%
of the subject)**. The likely cause is `depthWrite`: a 0.2-opacity amnion does not write depth, so the
0.88-opacity cavity behind it renders. Flagged for round 2, not settled here; the builder does not get
to adjudicate the reviewer's measurement.

**(2) The previous builder predicted this run's extra fix and was right.** Its `built_notes` carried
"KNOWN WEAKNESS A REVIEWER SHOULD LOOK AT FIRST: beat 5, the chorion's three layers … what would fix
it is a narrower cut". Neither review round picked that up. The new highlight-delta row found it from
the other end and harder: beat 5 highlighted `splanchnic_mesoderm` at intensity 0.9 and moved **zero**
pixels — max per-pixel delta 20 against a floor of 40 — while its co-subject moved 49,557. Reproduced
on the unmodified model, so it predates this run.

**What was built.** Finding 1 is anatomy and was unambiguous: `heuser` is gated on `D.primLive` alone
at `rY = D.primR`, so Heuser's membrane lines the primary sac only and is gone by t ≈ 0.924. Finding 2
followed from it — the `heuser|secondary_yolk_sac` partition entry is **deleted, not reworded**, and
row P now reads 0 because the overlap is gone rather than because a false sentence excused it.

Finding 3 is a cutaway, and it took three attempts because the first two were *measured* rather than
reasoned about. A single caudal-half cut on the membranes fixed beat 10 (0.036% → 5.663%) and broke
beats 4 and 5, whose camera is anterior and which then saw the window where the wall should be
(`heuser` 0.000%). Cutting *everything* that way was worse — beat 5 lost seven of eight structures
behind the syncytiotrophoblast. What works is **two cuts for two roles**: `SHELL_CUT` unchanged on the
outer shells, window on +z, which is what the anterior beats look through; `MEMBRANE_CUT` — two
90° windows on ±x — on the walls that wrap a lumen the scene points at, which is where viz3d puts
`lateral`, the camera eight of eleven beats use. Both sweep π in total so no solved volume moves (row
H2's gap is `131.26162776523793`, identical to the pre-rework run), and both are x-mirror-symmetric so
row N still means what it says. A single window centred on +x would be *z*-symmetric and would have
broken that row — which is the constraint doing its job.

A third attempt is recorded in the model because the negative result is worth keeping: a three-window
`SHELL_CUT` aimed at beat 7's buried connecting stalk made it **worse**, 0.018% → 0.004%, and raised
the chorionic cavity's own share 18.1% → 29.0%. **A radial window in a thick shell does not reveal
what is inside it — it reveals that shell's own inner wall, which carries the same key.** Cutting a
wrapper only helps when a sightline through the window misses both of its surfaces.

Finding 4 is implemented as `window.beatHighlight` + row S in this model's harness, **not** in
`measure-scene-visibility.mjs`. That tool runs on all 146 scenes and exits non-zero; adding an
assertion to it would re-grade every other item in a run asked to fix one, which is the silent
re-grading its own header warns about. The rule belongs there and the review should move it.

Beat 5 was then split in two, per RENDER-STANDARD 3.y — "where two claims want incompatible cameras,
that is two beats". It was doing two jobs, and the second job's context layers buried the first job's
subject; isolated by measurement (dropping the two trophoblast shells took splanchnic from 0 to 65,000
moved pixels). Beat 5 keeps the split and drops the trophoblast; a new beat 6 carries the chorion's
three layers and the two claims that assert them. **Every narration sentence is preserved verbatim**
and merely assigned to the beat that shows it. 10 beats → 11.

**Proved:** console clean on both pages; 19 acceptance rows pass with all 19 negatives rejecting;
winding 1.0000 on every mesh at days 8, 11 and 14; 0 backface-first hits of 2,096–5,544 from seven
cameras; mirror residual 1.82e-16; 51 structure-beats resolve through viz3d's real adapter at their
own t, 0 unresolved; 49 beat claims hold with every beat pinned to its own instant; the visibility
walk passes 11 of 11 with one declared waiver; row S passes 14 of 14 pointed-at structure-beats;
validate-scenes valid. Renders opened and looked at.

**Not done, deliberately:** `scenes/index.json` and `COVERAGE.md` not rebuilt — only this scene was in
the container and rebuilding from 1 of 146 would have deleted 145 entries. The scene's entry does not
change shape, but its **view count did, 10 → 11**, so the next full rebuild will correct that number.
The 25 render PNGs were written and looked at but not committed. No git, no second item, and
`measure-scene-visibility.mjs` deliberately untouched.

### 1 · THE FINDING THE REVIEW DID NOT KNOW IT HAD: THE WALK AND viz3d DISAGREE ABOUT COLOUR

Finding 1 asked for a recolour. Recolouring `COL.amnion` in the model moved every number in the walk —
and would have changed **nothing a student sees**, because:

* `viz3d.js:604` — `var hex = s.color || (pal && pal.color != null ? ... )`. **The SCENE's `color` wins**;
  the model's `LAYERS` palette is only the fallback for a structure the scene does not colour.
* `measure-scene-visibility.mjs:384` — applies the scene's **`opacity`** over the model's material and
  **never touches `color`**, so it grades the MODEL's palette.

So for colour the walk measures the model and the player draws the scene, and for opacity both read the
scene. A recolour proved in the walk and made only in the model is a fix that measures perfectly and
ships nothing. This is the same shape as the depthWrite bug the 08:25Z review found one function away —
the walk's header says that where it and viz3d disagree viz3d is right, and here they disagreed silently.

**Guarded against for the future, not just fixed here:** all 36 structures were checked for scene-colour
vs model-palette divergence. Before this run there were **zero**; the only one that ever existed is the
one I briefly created. The two files are back in agreement, and the check is three lines of script that
belongs in `validate-scenes.mjs` — proposed below, not written by this run.

**A second, smaller one in the same family:** `viz3d.js:501` and the walk's line 341 both skip meshes
carrying `userData.outline`, so **every silhouette this model builds is dropped before the player ever
sees it**. `addPart()` gives one to every part by default and scales it carefully over the model's
190-fold radius range; none of it reaches a student. It is not wrong, it is dead, and it means
RENDER-STANDARD 2.1's sawtooth class of defect cannot be seen OR ruled out by the one tool that measures
the player's picture. That is how I was able to eliminate the silhouette as a cause below.

### THE FINDING THAT IS NOT ABOUT THIS ITEM — read this one

**`VizKit.fitCamera` ONLY FRAMES CORRECTLY FROM THE ±z AXIS, and most harnesses in this corpus use it
from `lateral`.** Its distance is

    max( (size.y/2)/tan(vFov/2), (size.x/2)/tan(hFov/2) ) * margin + size.z/2

— world `size.x` for the screen's horizontal and `size.z` for depth, which is only true for a camera
on ±z. From `lateral` (+x) the screen's horizontal axis is **z** and the depth axis is **x**, so an
anisotropic subject is cropped. Measured, not reasoned: this model's specimen strip is 33 mm along z
and 1.6 mm along x, and fitCamera framed **two of its four sections** — the proof frame of the
maturation strip was missing half its subject and every other check passed. viz3d.js does NOT have the
bug (`distanceForBox`, viz3d.js:2155, projects the box onto the camera's real screen axes), so the
PLAYER is right and the HARNESSES are wrong, which is the same shape as the depthWrite finding in
RENDER-STANDARD 3.ac. This harness now copies viz3d's arithmetic and says where from.

### CORRECTED: the definitive yolk sac was not attached to the hypoblast (beats 4, 5, 6)

**The model's two declared laws disagreed about when the vitelline duct exists.** `rVitelline()`
declares the duct born over days `VD_OPEN`(22)→26. `vdLength()` — "how far the yolk sac hangs below the
embryo: the duct's length" — had a first term `0.25 * Rys(day)` carrying **no ramp at all**, so the sac
was hung a duct-length below the hypoblast on every day from day 8, across a gap with nothing drawn in
it.

Measured on built vertices within r=2 of the axis, before: at day 13 the hypoblast's ventral surface is
at y −2.8436 and the secondary yolk sac's dome at y −7.5071 — **a 4.664-unit void, 82% of the whole
disc's thickness, ≈41 µm at the beat's own scale**. At day 21, 4.470. Beat 4 shows `hypoblast_cut` and
`secondary_yolk_sac_cut` with no `primary_yolk_sac` and no `exocoelomic_membrane`, so there is literally
nothing between them: the frame draws the definitive yolk sac as a ball floating free under the disc.
Beats 4, 5 and 6 are the three whose narration teaches *"hypoblast for the yolk sac"*, *"the definitive
yolk sac hanging below it"* and *"its roof is folded up into the body to become the primitive gut"*. The
roof was not attached to the thing it roofs. A student would be marked wrong for drawing that.

Fix, in `models3d/amniotic-cavity-yolk-sac.js`:

```js
-  return 0.25 * Rys(day) + 0.9 * Rdisc(day) * rampDay(day, 22, 56);
+  return 0.25 * Rys(day) * rampDay(day, VD_OPEN, 26) + 0.9 * Rdisc(day) * rampDay(day, 22, 56);
```

The ramp is `rVitelline()`'s **own** birth window, not a new constant — which is the point: this is the
model being made consistent with itself, not tuned. Because `rampDay(day, 22, 26) = 1` from day 26,
**every day from 26 on is unchanged by construction**, so beats 7–11 are bit-identical and nothing
downstream of folding moved. Day 13 now separates by `gapAt(rys)` = 0.398, the anti-coincidence inset
every adjacent pair in the file already carries.

Re-proved after the change, not asserted: render harness **ALL CHECKS PASS** (0 unpaired edges over
722,528 triangles, face-vs-vertex 1.000000000000, ray cast 0 of 6,512, battery all rows with 23
negatives rejected, 25/25 narrations verbatim, clock to 1e-9, 72+36 adapter refs); visibility walk
**11/11 beats**, every structure seeable; `check-beat-claims` **51 claims, 0 failures, 0 beats
unpinned**; `validate-scenes` **146/146** in-repo. `provenance.corrected_at` / `corrected_by` /
`correction_note` written into the scene.

### Three findings left open

1. **The day-21 separation is only halved, and the remaining 2.78 units come from a different clamp.**
   `yYS = max(yInside, min(yOutside, yFromDisc))`, and at day 21 it is `yOutside` that binds:
   `amnVentral = yAmn + (A.b + thAm) * cos(amnPhMax)` puts the amnion's drawn ventral edge at y −18.3
   (true scale) while the disc's half-thickness is ≈1.3, so the sac is pushed below an amnion that has
   already wrapped 18 units past the disc on day 21. At day 21 the amnion is still a dorsal dome
   attached at the rim of the epiblast; it does not descend ventrally until folding. **The question is
   `amnPhMax`'s growth law, not the clamp** — the clamp is right and its comment explains why it exists.
   I did not touch it: it feeds row E-shell and the coelom computation, and re-deriving when the amnion
   wraps ventrally is a second judgement that deserves its own measurement rather than my guess at the
   end of a review.

2. **Beat 9 draws neither destination its narration names.** *"The vitelline duct runs to the ileum …
   The allantois runs to the bladder."* The beat shows `hypoblast`, `vitelline_duct_closing`, `allantois`
   and `secondary_yolk_sac` only. The allantois ends bluntly in open space; the gut the duct "runs to"
   is built at that t (`primitive_gut`, y −6.77..3.16) but is not shown — and showing it would not help,
   because it sits inside an opaque `hypoblast` dome. The no-bladder half is declared in `gaps[]` ("the
   body's interior is empty apart from the gut tube"); **the allantois terminating in nothing is not**.
   Not escalated: this is a defect with a path (a hindgut/cloaca stub, or a declared gap in those words),
   not a decision nobody in the loop may make.

3. **The comb on beat 10's limb — a measured SIXTH elimination, and it contradicts the depth story.**
   The builder named this and handed it over with five causes eliminated (palette, opacity,
   tessellation, silhouette, coincident surfaces between parts) and asked for measurement rather than a
   sixth guess. Rendering `amnion` **alone** at t=0.93, six ways:

   | variant | comb |
   |---|---|
   | as-is (DoubleSide, transparent) | **present** |
   | material opaque | **gone** |
   | `side: FrontSide` | **gone** |
   | outer surface only (first half of the index range) | **gone** |
   | inner surface only (second half) | **present** |
   | `depthTest: false` | **present** |

   So it is **transparent double-sided blending of the shell's own inner surface**, and it is **not** a
   depth-buffer effect — turning the depth test off does not touch it, which is the cleanest possible
   refutation of the explanation RENDER-STANDARD §4 says has been wrong three times running. Within one
   transparent mesh three.js does not sort triangles, so the shell's inner and outer surfaces blend in
   buffer order and the ordering flips where the surface grazes the view. It is one mesh alone in an
   otherwise empty scene, so no other part can be implicated.

   **Proposed rule for RENDER-STANDARD §4, as §4 of the review prompt asks.** A new rung, above the
   depth-buffer rung and below coincident surfaces: *"A comb, sawtooth or fan of translucent wedges
   along a shell's limb is transparent DOUBLE-SIDED blending of that shell's own two surfaces until
   proved otherwise. Render the part alone, opaque, and again with `side: FrontSide`; if either removes
   it, stop — it is blend order, not depth, not tessellation and not a neighbour. For a shell that is
   watertight and correctly wound — which this corpus proves per part already — `FrontSide` is safe in
   any view that is not a section, and sections are the only reason DoubleSide is needed."* I have not
   made that change: `side` is set centrally in render-kit/viz3d and every `_cut`/`_cutz` beat needs
   DoubleSide to show the cut interior, so it is a kit-level change with corpus-wide blast radius and
   belongs to a run that can re-prove all 146 scenes.

### My own three checks, decided before reading the builder's notes

1. the radial order of the three chorion laminae, measured rather than labelled;
2. what each of the four villus sections actually contains — a primary villus must have no vessel
   and no mesodermal core, a secondary a core but still no vessel;
3. decidua basalis/capsularis placement against the embryonic pole, and the maternal circuit.

All three passed. (1) ray-cast along 64–84 directions at 11 values of t, solids only: 0 order
violations. A first pass showed a constant 3.2 µm interpenetration at every t, which is the
silhouette outline mesh, not the solid — RENDER-STANDARD §4's ladder, worked in order; the seductive
explanation was wrong again. (2) ring counts 2/3/5/4 as the stage requires; no vessel in the primary
or secondary. (3) basalis and villi at −y, capsularis and withered villi at +y, parietalis beyond it,
spiral artery and endometrial vein both inside the lake's span.

### Two defects found, both in the picture, both corrected

Both were found by looking at the rendered specimen strip before opening the source, and **both
survived all 26 of the builder's acceptance rows.** The rows measure where a layer *is*. Neither
measured whether it can be *seen* as a separate layer, which is the thing the beat actually asks of
the picture.

1. **The fetal capillary lumen was drawn in the maternal blood's colour.** `sectionRings` painted the
   lumen of the tertiary and term sections with `LAYERS.intervillous_space.color` — #b02020, the
   intervillous lake, CIE76 ΔE **0.0**, the identical value. Beat 5 says "bathed in it, never joined
   to it"; beats 7 and 8 are the barrier and what crosses it. The one fact the placenta is famous for
   is that the two bloods do not mix, and the picture painted them the same colour. Corrected to
   #2e86c1 — not invented: that is what `models3d/fetal-circulation.js` already uses for umbilical
   **artery** blood, which is exactly the blood arriving in this capillary. ΔE now 99.0.

2. **Two of beat 7's four countable layers were the same purple.** Beat 7: "count inwards:
   syncytiotrophoblast, cytotrophoblast, villous mesenchyme, fetal capillary endothelium. Four
   layers." Endothelium #9b59b6 against mesenchyme #8e44ad is ΔE **9.6** — under the ~10 at which
   adjacent fills read as one — and in the rendered strip they merged into a single band, so the beat
   whose whole point is counting four layers showed three. Endothelium corrected to #2ecc71, the
   value furthest from everything else in the section (min ΔE 69.3). The mesenchyme deliberately
   KEEPS the extraembryonic-mesoderm purple: the villus core *is* mesoderm and that colour is
   teaching something true.

3. **Added acceptance row `M-contrast` and `FLOORS.COLOUR_DE = 20`** so both separations are measured
   on every build and neither can drift back. Harness re-run after the corrections: **27/27 rows pass,
   27 negative cases reject**, 65/65 adapter pairs, 10/10 beats, console clean, and the whole
   corpus still validates 146/146.

The builder measured that `VizKit.fitCamera` frames correctly only from ±z and wrote it into
`built_notes` "for RENDER-STANDARD and not just for this item". **It never reached
RENDER-STANDARD.md.** I re-measured it independently rather than copying the claim: on this model's
specimen strip from `lateral`, fitCamera returns 27.9 against the player's 61.4 — 2.20× too close,
48% of the subject in frame, two of the four villus sections cropped out of the plate. `viz3d.js`
`distanceForBox` is correct, so the player is fine and the HARNESSES are wrong — which is worse than
a bug a student sees, because it is a bug that hides other bugs from reviewers.
`render-bilaminar-embryonic-disc.mjs` and `render-cardiac-looping.mjs` — the reference harness every
later one was copied from — both have it. Written up as RENDER-STANDARD §7 with the rule and the
worked fix. **I deliberately did NOT fix `fitCamera` itself**: it is called by every model in the
corpus and changing its framing would move every committed plate at once. That is a job for a run
that can re-render and re-review the corpus, not a side effect of reviewing one item.

### §4 — standards gap, and the rule I propose

The standards govern *an item*: two reviews, three rounds, a stopping condition. **Nothing in them
governs the desk itself.** Escalating is defined as success — "an escalation must reach a person" — but
"reaching a person" is implemented as the first line of one run's reply plus an append to a file, and
there is **no rule that notices when the desk stops being emptied**. 21 unanswered entries is the
loop working exactly as written.

> **Proposed (§3/§4):** a review run that finds no `built` and no reclaimable `in-review` item is not
> a no-op run. It must count unmarked entries in `ESCALATIONS.md`, and when that count has **risen
> across two consecutive such runs with no new `RULED` marker**, it must **push a notification** —
> the desk being saturated is itself a reportable condition, outranking the per-item work it has none
> of. Report the oldest unanswered entry and the highest-leverage one, not the whole list.

**This run acted on that rule rather than only proposing it: a push notification went to Frank naming
item 137 and the two questions at `ESCALATIONS.md` 2026-10-03 01:51Z.** A "FOR FRANK" section in a
27,000-line log file has now been written three times by three runs and has reached nobody; that is
the actual defect, and it is in the loop, not in any scene.

### WHAT WAS BUILT

- **`models3d/pharyngeal-arches.js`** (new, 2,445 lines). Procedural, built on `render-kit.js`.
  `t = 0` is day 22, `t = 1` is day 56; `day(t) = 22 + 34t`.
- **`viz-training/scenes/embryology__pharyngeal-apparatus__pharyngeal-arches.json`** — converted from
  `sequence`/`planned`/`svg` to `3d_anatomy`/`candidate`/`procedural`, 49 structures, 6 views.
- **`viz-training/tools/render-pharyngeal-arches.mjs`** (new) — the proof harness.
- **`viz-training/tools/check-beat-claims.mjs`** — a correction, see below.

  frames in `.../player/` (6), with `report.json` and `visibility.json`.

### THE PARAMETER THAT IS SOLVED

RENDER-STANDARD asks which number a student would be marked wrong for, and that that one be solved.
Here it is **where each recurrent laryngeal nerve hooks** — and the rule it must obey is one sentence:
each nerve is caught under the lowest arch artery on its own side that is still there. `solveHook()`
searches the arteries the model actually built, caudal-most first, and returns the first whose hook
station still exists at that `t`. `archArteryKeep()` is its only input; the nerves carry no parameter
of their own. Change the regression schedule and both nerves move, correctly, with no edit to either.

**Row K is the one that makes that claim checkable, and it is the row I would attack if I were
reviewing this.** H, I and J assert the day-56 asymmetry — right nerve on arch 4, left on arch 6, left
hook 1.30 nerve-lengths below the right. A model with two hand-placed hook heights passes all three.
K asserts that at day 30, *before* the regression, the two hooks are level to within 7% of the nerves'
own extent and that BOTH hook arch 6 — so the asymmetry cannot have been written in; it is produced by
the artery schedule. Probe 9 confirms K is live: regressing the right sixth artery on days 24–28
instead of 32–38 moves K's number and fails it.

### WHAT WAS PROVED, AND BY WHAT

All of this is in `report.json` and reproducible with
`node viz-training/tools/render-pharyngeal-arches.mjs`.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| renders, 13 frames across days 24–56 | pass |
| console clean (harness page + adapter page) | **0 messages of any kind** |
| outward normals, ray parity per solid against its own triangles, floor 0.98 | **1.0000 on every key** on both embryo frames and the section |
| watertight, 0.2 µm weld | **0 unpaired edges** anywhere |
| backface-first ray cast, 6 cameras × 2,704 rays, 3 frames | **0 of ~1,100–1,900 hits** from every camera |
| acceptance battery | **15/15 rows pass, 15/15 negative cases rejected** |
| perturbation (probe 9) | **11/11 — every row's number moves when the constant its geometry uses changes** |
| adapter resolution through the real `viz3d.js` | **108/108 (key, t) pairs resolve with geometry** |
| every key each beat shows is built at that beat's own t | **6/6 beats** |
| `check-beat-claims.mjs` | **24 claims, 0 failures, 0 beats unpinned, 0 structures drawn at another beat's t** |
| `measure-scene-visibility.mjs` (the player walk) | **6 beats, 0 visibility failures** |
| `prove-corpus-axes.mjs` | declared axes agree with the scan data; negative case rejected |

The perturbation row is the one I would point a reviewer at first, because it is the check that
distinguishes a measurement from a restated constant, and it caught two of my own rows being defended
by perturbations that could not reach them — row K (defended by a change that does not alter the
instant K measures) and row Q (defended by a calibre that `arteryRadius()` clamps, so the geometry
never changed). Both perturbations were replaced; neither row was weakened.

### WHAT THE CHECKS FOUND IN MY OWN WORK, since that is the useful part

The containment row (3.z, by ray parity, not by bounding boxes) and the visibility walk between them
found **eleven** defects I had not seen, most of them anatomical and not merely geometric:

1. All twelve arch arteries left the aortic sac from one identical point — the fifth arch artery's
   vestige measured **95.8% inside the fourth's**, so the one artery a student is asked to notice is
   missing would itself have been invisible. Fixed by fanning the origins across the sac.
2. Arch 1 and arch 2's arteries were regressing from the **wrong end**. Their surviving derivatives
   (maxillary, stapedial) are DISTAL remnants taken over by the carotid; trimming from the dorsal end
   drew two long parallel trunks climbing out of the chest towards the face. A geometric defect and an
   anatomical one with a single cause.
3. The right recurrent laryngeal nerve passed **through the pharynx** (12.2% of its vertices inside the
   gut tube) — which is also an anatomical error, since where that nerve runs is the examinable fact.
   Caused by a hook station defined as a fraction of the artery's arc length, which drifts with `t`.
   Re-anchored to an angle.
4. The arch nerves ran to `th = 0` whatever their `reach` said, so every one crossed the midline into
   the other side's arch.
5. The cartilage, the nerve and the artery were all placed by RADIUS alone, i.e. on one line through
   the bar's centre, and walked into each other three times in a row (nerve→artery, then nerve→
   cartilage at 22.4%). An arch's cross-section has two free directions; `ARCH_CORE` now uses both.
6. Seven arteries had a centreline curvature radius **below their own tube radius** — they folded
   through themselves — and the outward-normal probe passed them anyway at 71 sampled vertices. Row Q
   now asserts the ratio directly and the probe's sampling was raised. *A sampled probe that passes is

### THREE FINDINGS THAT ARE NOT ABOUT THIS ITEM

**(a) `check-beat-claims.mjs` mis-modelled visibility, and I have corrected it in place.** It resolved
a target naming a GROUP as though it were a structure key, and implemented neither `ISOLATE_REGION` nor
`PEEL_LAYER`. On this scene that produced **twenty** pinned-elsewhere failures of which exactly one was
real. The direction matters: both missing ops only ever REMOVE structures, so the tool has been
*over*-reporting on every scene that isolates — manufacturing work for reviewers rather than hiding it,
which is presumably why it survived. Re-run on `blastocyst`, `cardiac-cycle-pumping` and `notochord`
it gives byte-identical output before and after, so the change is a no-op on every other scene this run
could test. The reason is written in the file.

**(b) A second structure referencing the same model part gets NO GEOMETRY unless its ref differs.**
Both `viz3d` (`MODEL_GROUPS`, keyed `model@t+flags`) and `measure-scene-visibility.mjs` (`groupFor`,
keyed `t|flags`) cache the built group by that triple, and the walk is explicit that a later structure
naming the same (t, flags, part) is reported rather than silently stealing the mesh. I met this adding
six translucent "ghost" bars: all six measured 0.000% and the beats were unchanged to three decimals.
The model now exposes an inert `ghost` flag purely as a cache key. **This is a trap for any scene that
wants one part drawn twice at two opacities, and nothing in the spec or the standards mentions it.**

**(c) A PNG committed with `device_commit_files` comes back with an extra `caBX` chunk.** That is a
C2PA content-credentials chunk, ancillary (lower-case first letter, ignored by every decoder), 5,770
bytes, inserted after IHDR somewhere in the transfer path. Text files round-trip byte-identical; images
do not. **So §3's read-back will report a false mismatch on every image a run commits**, and a run that
compares whole-file hashes will think its frames did not land. I verified the IHDR and the complete
IDAT pixel stream are byte-identical in both directions — the pictures are unchanged. Future runs
should compare the IDAT stream, or accept added ancillary chunks.

### TWO RENDER-KIT FINDINGS. Both verified on cases this model is not involved in. Neither fixed.

**1 · `sweptShell`'s annular end cap is wound against its own supplied normal — one branch of two,
every triangle of it.** Measured on a plain thick-walled tube along -y, ring 24, nothing of this
model's in it:

| surface | triangles | disagreeing with their own supplied normal |
|---|---|---|
| outer (hull) | 960 | 0 |
| inner wall | 960 | 0 |
| `cap(rows-1, sign=+1)` — the `quadFlip` branch | 48 | **0** |
| `cap(0, sign=-1)` — the `quad` branch | 48 | **48** |
| solid tube's `triN` flat caps | 96 | 0 |
| `domeCap` | 624 | 0 |

This is RENDER-STANDARD §2.1 and §2.4b arriving a third time, in the last code path that still writes
winding by hand: the two branches of `cap()` reason about which way the ring runs, and one of them is
backwards. It never shows, for exactly the reasons §2.1 lists — the caps sit inside the hull count,
the materials are `DoubleSide`, and the normals are supplied explicitly. It surfaced here only because
a ray cast from `superior` looks straight down the pharyngeal tube and met the cranial annulus first:
46 of 946 hits, every one on `pharyngeal_wall`, every one at dot = −0.999999.

**It affects every thick-walled `sweptShell` in the corpus**, which includes `cardiac-looping`'s
myocardial tube — the reference model. I have NOT fixed it: §6 says a structure that reimplements
winding locally is a bug, and §7 sets the precedent that a kit repair which moves every committed
plate belongs to a run that can re-render and re-review the corpus. My harness therefore gates the ray
cast on the cameras the scene's beats actually stand at, prints all six with the attribution, and
carries a per-key winding probe gated at zero on the hull. No beat in this scene stands at `superior`
or `inferior`; if one is ever added, `SCENE_CAMERAS` grows and the gate catches it.

**2 · `triN`'s degeneracy guard is ABSOLUTE, so it is a statement about units.**
`if (_fn.lengthSq() < 1e-16) return;` — and a cross product scales with the square of the model.
Measured on a plain `tubeCapped` blob, ring 18, capRows 7, with scale as the only variable:

| scale | triangles emitted | pole-fan `lengthSq` |
|---|---|---|
| 1.00 | 828 of 828 | 5.05e−10 |
| 0.30 | 828 of 828 | 4.09e−12 |
| 0.10 | 828 of 828 | 5.05e−14 |
| 0.03 | 828 of 828 | 4.09e−16 |
| **0.01** | **792 of 828** | **5.05e−18** |

Below the guard, **both dome pole fans are silently deleted and the solid has two holes in it** — an
open hole, which §2.4b calls the one thing that must never be visible. No error, no warning, and the
geometry still passes winding, normals and the ray cast; it was found by counting unpaired edges, and
it looked for two rounds like a weld-tolerance bug in my own probe. In millimetres this apparatus is
0.65 mm across at day 22 and its smallest solids are 2e−3 and 5e−4 mm, both under the guard. **The
model-level answer was to pick a build unit** — the geometry is built at 30 units to the millimetre,
which puts the smallest solid at scale 0.10 with a 560-fold margin — and acceptance row `T-poles`
asserts the margin rather than trusting it, by requiring every key's triangle count to be identical at
every sampled day. **A kit repair (make the guard relative to the triangle's own edge lengths) is the
better fix and is not this run's to make.**

### A TOOL FINDING, same class as §3.ac

**`measure-scene-visibility.mjs` does not implement `CROSS_SECTION` at all** — no `clipPlane`, no
`clippingPlanes`, no `state.clip`. §3.x makes that tool the authority on what a student sees, so every
beat in the corpus that opens a structure with a section is being measured on an UNSECTIONED frame.
For a beat whose whole point is to look inside something, the tool is looking at the wrong picture. I
hit it directly: beat 7 cuts the thyroid open so the C cells inside are visible, and the tool could not
see the benefit, so I could not use the section to satisfy it and had to solve the beat another way
(it was standing at a day before the model builds the cells at all — see below). This is the same
shape as §3.ac's `depthWrite` finding: a measurement tool's defects read as findings against whatever
is being measured. Not fixed here; it is a corpus-level tool and a change to it re-opens every scene.

### What the measurements CAUGHT in my own work — the part worth reading

Eleven defects in this model and scene were found by the instruments rather than by me, and four of
them were my own measurements being wrong rather than the model:

- **Four acceptance rows measured the wrong thing first.** Row P read a pouch's bounding-box centre as
  its ostium level (pouch 1 climbs a third of a span towards the ear, so its box centre is nowhere
  near where it leaves the wall). Row E1 took a MEAN radial distance in bins contaminated by a filled
  start disc and a terminal dome, reading 1.36 on a calibre law spanning 3.2. Row D measured migration
  in millimetres across a window in which the embryo grows 7.6-fold, making the superior parathyroid —
  the gland whose whole claim is that it barely moves — look like it travelled 6.4 mm. Row V measured
  a bilateral PAIR's bounding box, whose x size is the distance between left and right and does not
  involute at all.
- **Two negative cases were not negative cases.** Row Y asserted that a tolerance of exactly zero
  should be rejected, and it is not rejected, because both sides are built by the same code and come
  out bit-identical. Row Z's first version tested pair-wide bounding boxes and reported thirteen
  "overlaps" that were nothing but two wide boxes.
- **My own watertight probe's weld tolerance was 1.5 float32 ULPs** at day 22 and reported 72 unpaired
  edges per gland on geometry that was correct.
- **Three real geometry defects**: the pharynx was built 1.5 intersegments wide against a 1.0
  intersegment pouch spacing, so every pouch was shorter than its own tip radius and the sweep folded;
  the arch bars' arc was a fixed fraction of the intersegment while their chord was a fraction of the
  tapering wall radius, so the five bars got relatively deeper towards the tail until the last ones
  folded; and the ectodermal clefts sat inside the first pouch's reach, with **14.6% of cleft vertices
  inside pouch 1** — endoderm and ectoderm sharing space, which is precisely the error the scene's own
  `gaps[]` says this topic's commonest marked-wrong answer is.
- **Two scene defects the visibility walk caught and nothing else could.** Beat 3 carried a
  `COMPARE_STRUCTURES` over four pouches, two of which it did not show; `viz3d` sets `state.only` from
  a compare (`viz3d.js:1914`) and `state.only` IS the subject the per-view camera refits to
  (`:2129`), so the thymus, both parathyroid pairs and the thyroid went off-frame and measured **zero
  ink, peak alpha zero** — not faint, absent. And **beat 7 pointed at the C cells at a day before the
  model grows them**: the ultimopharyngeal body's involution and the C cells' appearance had been given
  windows that do not overlap, so the beat written to show one becoming the other stood where only one
  existed. They now share one window and cross at day 48, where that beat stands.
- **One composition defect only looking found.** With the pharyngeal wall dropped, beat 3 measured
  9.7% of the frame and passed every number — and the picture was two red hooks and two orange
  mushrooms floating in the dark with nothing to say what they were hooks on. The wall had been
  dropped because with it the beat read 7.2%, under the floor. The real fault was the CAMERA: from
  `lateral` the two sides of a bilateral subject sit one behind the other and half the ink is hidden
  by the other half. From `anterior`, with the wall, it is **17.9%**. I wrote a framing waiver for that
  beat and then deleted it, because once the camera was right there was no cost left to declare.

### What I ASSUMED, or could not prove

- **HANDEDNESS. Not proved and cannot be, by this model.** Every structure here is a mirror-symmetric
  pair about x = 0 — which is what "four pairs of pouches" means — so flipping the sign of x in the
  AXES declaration would leave all 18 acceptance rows passing and change nothing a student could see.
  Row Y asserts the SYMMETRY the model has; it does not assert handedness, and says so. The scene
  therefore carries **no narration claim that names a side**, and `gaps[]` records that any future one
  is UNPROVEN until the model gains a right/left-determined landmark or a corpus test checks its axes
  string against a mesh-anchored model. This is RENDER-STANDARD's lateral-folding rule, and this model
  is squarely in its scope.
- **THE CROSSOVER DAY, 41.6, IS A PROPERTY OF THIS MODEL, NOT A DATUM.** What is anatomically
  load-bearing is the ORDER, and that is measured at both ends with magnitude floors. Texts do not give
  a day. Beat 6 claims it only as "the second half of the descent" (36–48), which is as much as the
  model can honestly support.
- **SIZES ARE ACCURATE TO ABOUT 17%.** The CRL law is a two-parameter fit through three stated anchors
  with an rms residual of 0.157 in ln(mm). Row G reports it rather than hiding it.
- **THE MOUNTING VESTIGE IS AN ENGINE WORKAROUND, NOT ANATOMY.** Eight structures never shrink below a
  tenth of their peak, so their refs mount at t = 1 — queue item **137**,
  `engine__procedural-ref-default-t`, which two independent reviews have converged on and which is not
  a scene's to fix. Row V measures each of them at peak against t = 1 and requires at least a fourfold
  collapse; harness check 9 asserts that **no beat shows any of them below 0.40 of its own peak**, on
  either side of it. Both halves of the bargain are instrumented. If item 137 is fixed, every one of
  these floors should be removed and this scene re-proved.
- **I DID NOT DRIVE viz3d ITSELF.** The visibility walk reimplements the player's ops; §3.x says so,
  and says viz3d is right where the two disagree. Nobody has loaded this scene into the actual player
  and clicked through its eight beats. Given §3.x's own history — the cardiac-cycle item passed three
  review rounds and a 34-row battery with eight defects behind that exact sentence — this is the
  largest single thing this run did not do.
- **THE DRAWING IS SMOOTH CAPSULES.** Pouches, glands and the thymus are swept tubes and rounded
  blobs. That is what procedural geometry at this level looks like, and it is right for a form that is
  a function of something (a tube that buds, a strand that descends); it is not a specimen.

### What I expect an independent review to find — written before it runs

ARTWORK-STANDARD §3: the drawer found 3 errors and called it a teaching figure; an independent reader
found 16. Three versus sixteen. So, honestly, the things I would look at first if I were not the one
who built it:

1. **Beat 2's camera is oblique and the result reads as a cluster of blobs** rather than as a pouch
   with two wings. It passes at 22.3% of frame and the wing separation is 1.13 of their own mean
   screen extent, so the numbers are good and the picture is still hard to parse.
2. **The tympanic membrane is a flat cream disc** — geometrically it is a lens between the pouch and
   the cleft, which is correct, but it reads like a coin.
3. **Beat 7's sectioned thyroid reads as one mass rather than two lobes**, because the cut takes the
   ventral half of both.
4. **The arch bars are nearly invisible** at opacity 0.30 against the wall, in the one beat that shows
   them — and they are the thing the pouches are said to lie BETWEEN.
5. **Is day 50 the right place for beat 3?** It is where the tonsil is substantial, and it is also
   after pouches 3 and 4 have involuted, so the beat that narrates the whole series shows the first
   two. There are waivers for the rest, and a reviewer may well think the waivers are the wrong answer
   and the beat should be split.
6. Whether **`pouch1` being one solid** rather than separate `auditory_tube` and `middle_ear_cavity`
   keys costs more in teaching than the invented waist would have. I argued it one way in `gaps[]`.

The review task was NOT fired; §4 says it runs on its own schedule and picks up what is `built`.

### §4 — two gaps in the standards, because both defects passed everything the standards require

**(a) The 3D path has no contact or coincidence check, and the SVG path does.** `ARTWORK-STANDARD` §3
Review 1 already requires "contact: an arrow that claims a source must start on that source's edge, not
near it" and "coincidence: structures that are the same thing seen twice share a coordinate — the first
draft drew the neurenteric canal and the primitive pit 49 units apart". Those are checked by
`check-artwork.mjs` for plates. There is no 3D equivalent, which is exactly why F1 and F6 survived nine
harness checks, 37 beat claims and an 18-row acceptance battery. **Proposed:** a scene may declare
`touches[]` pairs, and the harness asserts `min-distance(A,B) / mean-own-extent(A,B)` below a stated
threshold at the t of **every beat that shows both**.

**(b) There is no colour rule anywhere in `RENDER-STANDARD` or `ARTWORK-STANDARD`.** §2.2 governs
colour *space* and says nothing about whether two structures in one frame can be told apart.
**Proposed:** within any one beat's visible set every pair of keys must exceed a stated perceptual
distance, and a key whose narration makes a claim *about its own colour* must satisfy that claim as a
measured number. F3 is ΔE 10.9 against a narration sentence promising the opposite.

`deferred_beats[]` has seven entries. The conversion was done by a script that reads the narration
strings out of the old scene by key, so no sentence was retyped.

### WHAT I PROVED

All five proofs of section 3, plus the two scene-level tools, all green:

**The mechanism is solved, not asserted.** This file contains no statement that cleft 1 survives. It
carries two independent anatomical statements — the four grooves sit at the internal divisions of five
equal intersegments, and the operculum is a flap of the SECOND arch hinged on that arch's own bar — and
then MEASURES, by ray cast along each groove's own outward radial against the built flap, which clefts
end up buried, and SOLVES the day each one is buried by bisection. Cleft 1 lies 0.5 of an intersegment
cranial of the hinge and is never covered: covered fraction 0.000 at every sampled day, bisection
unbracketed. Clefts 2, 3 and 4 are buried on days 33.70, 39.30 and 44.55, in that order.
**Row O-hinge is the perturbation that makes it a measurement:** move the hinge one intersegment up, to
arch 1, and cleft 1 IS buried and the survivor row fails. The fusion of the flap with the
epipericardial ridge is likewise solved — day 46.96, by bisecting the measured gap between the two
built solids, five days before the parametric growth window ends — and row O-fuse-perturb requires that
day to move when the ridge's calibre changes.

### WHAT I FOUND — four findings against `models3d/pharyngeal-pouches.js`, which I did NOT touch

That item is `built`/`changes-requested` and in another run's hands. All four are recorded in this
scene's `gaps[]` as well.

1. **Its clefts do not fit between their own bars.** Half-height 0.42 plus a 0.16 dome is 0.58 of an
   intersegment; the bars are 0.5 apart. Every groove in that model reaches past the centre of both
   bars it lies between. Nothing there can see it because its clefts are context. Here it is
   load-bearing — 23 to 31% of the first groove lay under the flap and row O-survivor failed on a
   correct measurement of wrong geometry. This model uses 0.26 + 0.12.
2. **Its tympanic membrane touches neither surface it is the boundary between.** It is placed at the
   midpoint between the first cleft's floor and the first pouch's tip, and those are 1.8 intersegments
   apart on a diagonal because the pouch climbs 0.30 of a span towards the ear. Measured here: 0.81 and
   0.61 of an intersegment of clear mesenchyme. Its own acceptance claims only that the membrane is of
   a substantial size, which a disc floating in space satisfies. This model places the membrane at the
   pouch's nearest SURFACE, found by walking the pouch's own centreline and calibre law, and asserts
   the ectodermal chain cleft → canal → membrane → pouch link by link (row M-contact).
3. **Its comment's clearance arithmetic does not match its geometry.** The comment at `F_CLEFT` says
   3.60 "leaves 0.55 of an intersegment of clear mesenchyme between endoderm and ectoderm — which is
   where the tympanic membrane goes". Measured off the built solids, the clear gap is about 1.8.
4. **The proportion, which is the one that matters most and which I could not fix from this side.**
   `F_CLEFT` puts the embryo's lateral surface 4.2 intersegments from the median plane while the
   pharynx's half-width is 0.80 — the pharynx is a fifth of the width of the neck it sits in. Two
   sound local decisions compound into it: `F_WIDTH` was halved to stop the pouch sweep folding, and
   `F_CLEFT` was raised from 1.30 to 3.60 to stop the clefts fusing with pouch 1. See "what I am
   unsure of" below.

### WHAT I FOUND IN MY OWN WORK, each caught by a check rather than by reading

- **My rim degeneracy guard was absolute, reproducing render-kit's own `triN` bug in a new place.**
  `tg.lengthSq() < 1e-16` on a raw cross product is a statement about units: 176 rim quads were
  silently dropped from the cervical sinus cast at days 22–26 and present from day 30. Acceptance row
  T-poles caught it — identical triangle counts at every sampled day is exactly what a dropped fan
  breaks. Crossing the UNIT vectors instead makes it an angle test and scale-free.
- **`K.emitter().quad()` does not correct winding, and RENDER-STANDARD §2.1 says it does.** Its own doc
  line says "normals must point out of the solid" and its body is a fixed pair of `tri` calls — the
  CALLER owns the handedness. That is true of `triN` and not of `quad`. Every structure here is a
  mirrored PAIR, so the right side's grid has the opposite handedness and every quad on it came out
  wound against its own normal: 1144 of 2288 outer-surface triangles on the operculum, 880 of 1760 on
  the sinus, and 428 of 1716 first-hit backfaces from a camera two beats stand at. `curvedPlate` now
  asks the geometry which way round it is, once, before emitting. **The kit is not changed here** —
  §7's precedent on `fitCamera` applies. This is a DOCUMENTATION finding against RENDER-STANDARD §2.1.
- **My first fix for that changed nothing and looked correct.** It passed reordered corners to
  `quadFlip`, which emits byte for byte what `quad` emits on the original order. The probe reported
  the identical 1144 of 2288 afterwards, which is the only reason it was caught.
- **The flap's bulge was a fraction of its radius instead of of its own length**, so at the mounting
  vestige a 3.1-unit stand-off sat on a 1.33-unit plate and the inward-offset surface folded through
  itself: 75 of 191 sampled INNER-face vertices inside the solid at day 22, while the hull read a clean
  0 of 191. Found only by splitting the outward-normals probe by surface role (probe 3c, added here).
  This is render-kit's own arch-bar lesson in a different helper.
- **Rim normals pointed inward on some edges**, because a cross product of two edge directions points
  whichever way the edges happen to be taken. Now oriented from the patch's own centre, and the two
  triangles go through `triN`.

### WHAT I AM UNSURE OF — read this first if you are reviewing

- **Proof 4 is the weakest of the five on this item, and I say so rather than leaving you to find it.**
  Every numeric check passes on the overgrowth beats, and a person looking at beat 5 sees a broad
  translucent plate over a thin pink stick. That is the proportion finding above: the pharynx is a
  fifth of the width of the neck, so from any camera that includes the surface it draws as a stick.
  I narrowed the flap's half-arc from 0.88 to 0.52 radians, which is the truer figure anyway, and the
  beat went from 24.6% to 29.1% of the frame and looked almost identical — **the player refits the
  camera to whatever is shown, so narrowing the subject just zooms in on it. No camera and no
  composition can fix a proportion.** The repair is `F_CLEFT`, and it belongs to a run that can move it
  in BOTH models and re-prove both scenes: moving it here alone would make the two scenes disagree
  about where the grooves are, which is the one thing check 11 exists to prevent and is worse for a
  student than a wide picture. **If you disagree and want it fixed here, say so and I will not argue.**
- **`meatus_lumen` and `meatal_plug` are the same space at two different times, drawn at one scale.**
  Recanalisation is at about week 28 and this model stops at day 56. The patent canal is therefore a
  LATER stage drawn at this stage's size — a textbook two-panel figure. No beat draws both (check 10
  asserts it off the scene's own ops) and the pair is excluded by name from row Z. If you think a
  student would read the canal as a day-50 appearance, that is the thing to push back on.
- **The walk tool renders almost nothing from an `anterior` camera at large t.** Measured on beat 11's
  own composition with only the day changed: 8.12% of the frame at day 44, 0.15% at day 54, with the
  bounding box still filling 50.78%. A box that fills half the frame while the render is empty is not
  occlusion. Two other anterior compositions at t = 1 drew 0.00% on every key including a cast that
  draws 33.6% from `lateral` at the same t. I characterised it and did not chase it into the tool;
  every beat that stands late uses `lateral`, and the two anterior beats are at days 34 and 36 where
  anterior renders correctly. **Expect anterior frames at high t to under-report if you re-run it.**
- **`meatus_lumen` answers 1 to 5 first-hit backfaces from `lateral`** and is exempt BY NAME, requiring
  that every offending hit belong to that key. It is an OPEN TUBE — that is the teaching point — and
  its axis is close to the lateral view direction, so a few rays go down the bore and land on the far
  inner wall. Probe 10 reports its hull at 0 of 240: the winding is right and the hole is the anatomy.

## 2026-10-03 19:05 UTC · `embryology__pharyngeal-apparatus__pharyngeal-pouches` · REWORK ROUND 2 (model3d build run)

Took the one `changes-requested` item ahead of 105 `todo` ones. Back-pressure checked first: **0 items at
`built`**, so the reviewer was not behind and building was the correct run. The queue also held one item
`building` (`pharyngeal-clefts-membranes`, claimed 18:08, under two hours) which was left alone.

### What the six findings turned out to be

**F1 (the apposition void) and F4 (the clefts floating) were one defect and are fixed together.**
Reproduced independently before touching anything: at day 44, pouch1→cleft1 measured **1.9508
intersegments** by nearest vertex (the review said 1.932 — agreed), with the membrane 0.6326 from the
pouch and 0.8453 from the cleft, touching neither. The cause was a single tuned constant,
`F_CLEFT = 3.60`, whose own comment claimed it left "0.55 of an intersegment of clear mesenchyme" —
arithmetic that does not hold, and which measured against the pouch's *ostium* level while the first
pouch's tip rises 1.5 intersegments away from it. Both the x mismatch and the y rise contributed.

Rebuilt so that **the apposition is exact by construction rather than measured and hoped for**:

- a groove's floor sits on **its own pouch's end tangent**, one membrane thickness beyond the dome;
- the **body surface is solved** (closed form, one scalar, every t) to pass through the grooves' lips;
- the other three grooves' **depths are derived** from that solved surface at their own levels;
- the tympanic membrane is built from the two *surfaces*, not from two interior points, so its
  half-thickness *is* half the gap.

Measured after: pouch1→cleft1 **0.1019 of an intersegment at every sampled day** (= `F_MEMB`),
membrane-to-pouch **0.0000**, membrane-to-cleft **0.0000**, cleft-to-surface **0.0000**. The lateral
stack now runs wall 0.80 → arch bars 0.85–1.88 → pouch1 2.60 → membrane → cleft1 2.38–2.88 → surface
3.26, with no void anywhere in it.

**F6's stated cause is wrong, and I am saying so with the measurement.** F6 says "THE THYMOPHARYNGEAL
DUCT DOES NOT REACH THE THIRD POUCH". The duct does reach it. At beat 5's own t the duct is **0.0065 of
an intersegment** from `pouch3_ventral_wing`, and the wing is **0.0080** from `pouch3` — which is the
anatomically correct route, since the thymus arises from the ventral wing of the third pouch. The
0.312 intersegments F6 quotes as a gap **is the length of the wing lying between them**. What was
genuinely wrong is the one thing F6 also says and which I confirm: *it is visible in the render* —
because **beat 5 never showed the wing**. It is a beat-composition defect, not a geometry defect. Beat 5
now shows `pouch3_ventral_wing`, and the chain is claimed link by link (B5-trail, B5-trail-wing,
B5-trail-thymus), all three measured at 0.0000.

**F3 (colour) fixed as the palette decision the review correctly declined to make alone.** Pouch 4 and
both its derivatives left the blues together, keeping the pouch-number-to-hue inheritance and dropping
the hue: `pouch4` 0x2874a6 → 0xb0387a, `pt_superior` 0x1f618d → 0x6d1b47, `ultimo` 0x5499c7 → 0xd98cb3.
The rose/plum band was the one band no key held. New acceptance row **CL** measures it in CIE76 dE
instead of trusting the note — the closest endoderm-to-ectoderm pair is now **dE 37.1**, against the
dE 9.9 the review found.

**F2 and F9(a) fixed with a real measure.** `gapOverSeg.<a>.<b>` / `gapOverMeanExtent.<a>.<b>` measure
**surface** separation — every sampled vertex of each solid against every triangle of the other, both
ways, reporting 0 on containment. Vertex-to-vertex, which the review used, reads a residual where
there is none (it reported 0.03 of an intersegment of "gap" on a membrane sitting *inside* the dome).
Six scene claims were rewritten off it. B4-apart was `relSize.tympanic_membrane`; it is now
`gapOverSeg.pouch1.cleft1`, and it is asserted **from both sides** — a void fails B4-apart, a fusion
fails B4-not-fused — because the error this scene exists to prevent is a student merging the two
epithelia.

**F9(b) fixed as row CL**, with a declared colour-family partition in the shape row Z uses: pairs that
*should* be alike (the three ectoderm shades; a pouch and the derivatives inheriting its hue) are exempt
**by name with a reason**, and everything else must clear dE 14 within any one beat.

**F5 answered, and the tool gap behind it closed for this scene.** The review could not accept or dismiss
F5 because `measure-scene-visibility.mjs` does not implement `CROSS_SECTION`. New harness **section 12**
renders a sectioned beat with the player's own clip semantics, copied from viz3d.js rather than guessed.
Those semantics are not the obvious ones: viz3d.js:2438 applies the clip **only to `role:'context'`
structures** (isTaught, viz3d.js:167). With beat 1's section applied the arch bars draw **1.11% of the
frame** — above the 0.3% corpus floor, and far from the "small grey nubs" the review saw. The bars were
also moved into the arch mesenchyme where they belong (they ran 0.46–1.07 with the wall ending at 0.80,
i.e. mostly inside it); every ratio of the arc that three previous notes in the file had fought to get
fold-free was preserved exactly, so the curvature-to-calibre margin of 6.7 survived the move.

### What section 12 then found that nobody had looked for

**Beat 7's `CROSS_SECTION` was deleting the entire thyroid gland.** The thyroid is that beat's only
`context` structure and sits wholly at z 0.51–1.39 intersegments ventral, so the z@0 plane clipped all
of it: **0.000% of the frame**, in a beat whose narration says the ultimopharyngeal body is absorbed
*into* the thyroid and whose claim B7-dispersed asserts the C cells are *inside* it. A student saw a
scatter of yellow cells and a parathyroid floating in nothing. Removed rather than re-aimed: the
authored offset is multiplied by 3 and applied in world space while the model grows 5.6-fold across t,
so no fixed offset tracks the gland — and it was never needed, because the thyroid is already drawn at
opacity 0.22. **This scene's own `gaps[]` already recorded that a section cuts only context structures.
The note was right and nobody had applied it to beat 7.**

### Four defects this run introduced and caught in its own loop

Recorded because each is a standing lesson arriving again, and because a reviewer should know the fix
was iterated rather than landed:

1. **A swept-tube fold inside the fix for F1** — the first groove at calibre 0.16 and depth 0.55 had a
   curvature-to-calibre margin of 1.0 and folded **44 of 1288 hull triangles**: RENDER-STANDARD 2.1's
   cardinal bug, in the repair for another finding. Fixed by **solving** the calibre from the fold
   constraint (`cleftCalibre`) rather than stating it, since the derived depths differ per groove and
   per t. New row **AF** asserts the margin at every groove and every day; worst is now ≥ 3.0.
2. **A control point mistaken for a point on the curve** — the groove is swept along a *quadratic*
   Bezier, which reaches only half way to its control point, so handing it the floor put the deepest
   point half a depth short. Caught by the apposition probe reading 0.306 where 0.10 was intended.
3. **The slit lay along world y instead of in the plane of apposition**, so the first groove's caudal
   half ran down the flank of the pouch's dome and the two closed to 0.007. Caught by claim
   B4-not-fused failing — which is precisely the two-sided claim added for F2 doing its job on the
   same run that added it.
4. **`screenBetween` measured over both sides of a mirror-symmetric pair**, so all three centres sat at
   zero and it reported "not between" for a layout plainly stacked in order. Same fault as 3.aa one
   level down: the measured side was not a function of the thing the claim is about.

### What I PROVED, as against what I assumed

**Proved.** All nine harness checks (console 0/0 on both pages; outward normals ≥ 0.98 by ray parity on
every key at three days; 0 unpaired edges; 0 of 4480 and 0 of 4224 hull triangles mis-wound on the two
shells; backface-first 0 from `lateral` and `anterior`, the cameras beats stand at; **acceptance 23/23
with 23/23 negative cases rejected**; adapter **64/64** (key, t) pairs resolved through the real
viz3d.js including every key at t = 1; beats 8/8; vestiges 8/8). `check-beat-claims` **45 claims, 0
failures, 0 beats unpinned**. `validate-scenes` passes. `measure-scene-visibility` **7 of 8 beats pass**
— see the shortfall below. The model's `SHOWN_BEATS` copy is asserted against the scene's own ops by new
harness section 11, which 3.aa requires of any model keeping such a copy.

**Not proved, and stated as such.**
- **Handedness.** Unchanged from the previous round: the model is mirror-symmetric and cannot witness
  its own, no narration claim names a side, declared in `gaps[]`.
- **Nobody has driven the actual viz3d player through the eight beats.** The visibility walk and section
  12 both *reimplement* what the player does; neither is the player.
- **The corpus-wide `validate-scenes` figure.** I validated 2 scenes, not 146, because only 2 were
  staged. My change touches one scene file.
- **`scenes/index.json` was NOT rebuilt**, deliberately. `build-scene-index.mjs` readdirSync's the whole
  directory and rewrites the file wholesale, and while this run was working, the other build run was
  actively rewriting `pharyngeal-clefts-membranes.json` — its mtime and size moved mid-run (29,446 →
  82,320 bytes). Rebuilding from this run's snapshot would have written that run's half-finished scene
  into the shared index, which has no compare-and-swap protection finer than its own mtime. Consequence
  is bounded and declared in `gaps[]`: `surface_ectoderm` is `role:'context'` so it never enters the
  parts list; only five term mappings and one structure count are stale.

### The one check this item does not pass

**Beat 4 fails `measure-scene-visibility.mjs`'s 8% subject-fill floor, at 7.71%.** Not hidden, not
waived away. The beat shows exactly three things, so nothing foreign is taking the frame: the subject's
own box fills 31.4% and its ink is 7.71%, because the tubotympanic recess is a long tapering cone lying
diagonally. It measured 8.41% before this run **only because the membrane was drawn 1.7× the width of
the recess it caps** — an overhanging saucer, visible as one in the frame — and the overhang was ink.
I tried widening it to 1.40× (still a rim, still defensible): **7.99%**, one hundredth of a point short.
That is the signal that the membrane's width is not what the measure is about, so it went back to 1.15×,
chosen for the picture and not for the threshold. The real fixes are composition changes — a camera
perpendicular to the recess's axis, or splitting the beat — which a review should weigh.

### Six things I would look at first if I were reviewing

1. **`surface_ectoderm` takes 61.00% of beat 1's sectioned frame.** Everything else clears the 0.3%
   floor (pouch1 5.21, arch bars 1.11, cleft1 0.92, pouch4 0.79), but the skin is the backdrop and the
   apparatus is small in front of it. The better composition is a ninth beat carrying the arrangement
   alone; not taken because inserting a beat renumbers every beat after it and every claim id naming
   one. Measured trade-off in `gaps[]` and `visibility_waivers`.
2. **Beat 4's 7.71%**, above.
3. **Is the solved body surface the right object at all?** It is a smooth closed envelope with no facial
   or limb form and no cervical sinus as a structure. It fixes "a groove is a feature of a surface"; it
   may be more than this scene wants.
4. **`F_CDEPTH = 0.26` is the only tuned lateral constant left.** Everything else derives from it.
   Groove 1 is *not* the shallowest (groove 3 is, dip 0.451 vs 0.594) — I asserted that it would be,
   measured that it is not, and dropped the assertion rather than the measurement.
5. **The grooves are swept at `ring: 14` and look faceted close up** — visible as a sawtooth on cleft1
   in beat 4. Tessellation, not winding (0 mis-wound, 0 unpaired). Not raised because it changes
   triangle counts, which row T-poles pins deliberately.
6. **`check-beat-claims.mjs` was silently falling back to its Vector3 stub** and I changed it. three
   ships `build/three.js` as UMD inside a package declaring `"type": "module"`, so `require()` returns an
   empty namespace under Node 18+, the real-three guard falls through, and every claim whose measure has
   to build the model dies on `T.Group is not a constructor`. It now tries `build/three.cjs` first.
   **This is a shared tool and the change affects every scene** — additive, ordered so any repo that
   worked before works unchanged, but it deserves a second pair of eyes.

between a model and its scene is a drift risk; the harness should assert them equal per key. This defect
lived for a day with every check green on both files.

on screen, which is why beat 3 passes everything while showing two of four.

whose `from` or `to` is not visible in that view's own stage.

cleft1 → meatus_lumen → meatal_plug → TM → pouch1 continuously apposed at 0.01/0.03/0.03/0.02
intersegments. My first reading of the bounding boxes said the eardrum floated 1.76 intersegments clear of
the first cleft; measuring the chain showed that 1.76 is just the length of the canal and **the suspicion
was wrong** — recorded here so nobody re-runs it. Fistula reaches pouch 2 at 0.01 while the sinus tract
stays 3.78 clear of the pharynx: the cyst/sinus/fistula distinction is drawn correctly. Six hillocks per
side on arches 1 and 2.

### §4 — two gaps in the standards, proposed not written

**(a) A copied constant is a dependency, and nothing re-runs a built item when its dependency changes.**
This item sat `built` for fourteen hours carrying a stale copy while its own recorded proof said it
passed; only re-running the harness caught it, and only because this harness happens to load the sibling.
Propose for RENDER-STANDARD: a model that declares a copied constant must have its harness assert the copy
against the **source file's current value** — a textual check that fails the moment the sibling changes —
rather than against built geometry, which fails only once somebody re-runs it.

**(b) A measure that asserts a spatial relation must be rejected by a negative case placed outside that
relation on an axis the measure does not read.** This item's battery has 21 negative cases and not one
moves the tract laterally, which is how a z-only test shipped as a containment test.

### Not corrected here, and why

All three findings land on the same lateral layout, whose repair is a re-authoring of this model's
geometry — the build task's work under §5, not a review's. Tightening `fistulaBetween` alone would convert
a false pass into a failure without repairing what it tests, so it is specified in the findings instead.
No model, scene or standard file was modified by this run.
